This study presents an example from the Middle Permian Maokou Formation (Sichuan, China) while, some evidence suggest dolomite formed in association with evaporative or hydrothermal fluid, re-evaluation from new data sets suggest dolomitization by normal seawater. The Maokou Formation comprises three main petrographic types of dolomites (micro-, fine-, and medium-coarse crystalline), that lack evaporites, exhibit dull-red cathodoluminescence, near-ideal cation ordering (0.56–1.0), and are cross-cut by fitted fabric microstylolites, which was interpreted to have formed penecontemporaneously into the early burial diagenetic realm. Their relatively constant δ13C values (2.79–6.03‰), 87Sr/86Sr ratios (0.70737–0.70768), negative Ce and no positive Eu anomalies match coeval seawater. Negative δ18O values and few samples with Mn/Sr ratios <2 reflect closed-system recrystallization. Restored primary temperatures (27.9°C to 56.3°C), corrected for solid-state reordering via forward Δ47 modeling, and δ18Ofluid values (−0.8 to +1.2‰ VSMOW) are within the normal seawater range. U-Pb dating gives ages of 254.2±3.9 Ma (D1), 250.7±5.1 Ma (D2), and 249.2±2.5 Ma (D3), indistinguishable from each other but significantly older than saddle dolomite (244.8±1.5 Ma). This analysis strongly suggests that the dolomite was replaced by Permian normal seawater and subsequently experienced closed-system recrystallization during burial stage. The vertical variation of C-O isotopes and elemental data correlate with high-frequency sea-level fluctuations, confirming sea-level-driven sustained seawater circulation and cyclic reflux recharge as the driving mechanism for dolomitization. This study has revealed that the normal-seawater dolomitization could also proceed in a shallow-water platform, providing insights for coeval reservoirs in the Yangtze Block and similar settings worldwide.

title: Biomass-burning smoke water-soluble organic matter reverses ferrihydrite colloid-inhibited mobility of Cd 2+ through saturated porous media via interface fractionation and selective binding
description: Publication date: 30 September 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 720 Author(s): Bin Wang, Nan Yang, Kunyu Wen, ZhiWei Chen, Boyun Zheng, Yanbin Ma, Li Zhang, Zhichong Qi
abstract: Biomass burning events release large amounts of pyrogenic dissolved organic matter (BBS-WSOM) into terrestrial ecosystems, where it interacts with iron oxides and trace metals. However, how the molecular heterogeneity of BBS-WSOM governs colloid-facilitated metal transport remains poorly constrained. Here, we combined column transport experiments with multispectral analysis to elucidate how BBS-WSOM modulates the co-mobility of ferrihydrite (Fh) colloids and Cd2+ in saturated porous media. We found that humic-like components with higher aromaticity and hydrophobicity were preferentially retained on sand surfaces, whereas protein-like components remained largely in the aqueous phase. Protein-like components were the primary agents responsible for Cd2+ complexation, thus facilitating Cd2+ mobility. Although Fh colloids alone suppressed Cd2+ transport, the presence of BBS-WSOM not only neutralized this suppression but further enhanced Cd2+ mobility in the ternary system (Cd2+ + Fh + WSOMs) compared to the binary system (Cd2+ + WSOMs). This counterintuitive enhancement arose from molecular fractionation at the Fh-water interface: Fh preferentially adsorbed humic-like components, enriching the aqueous phase with protein-like components that bound Cd2+ more effectively. These findings reveal that the trade-off between humic-like and protein-like components within pyrogenic DOM critically controls the direction and magnitude of colloid-mediated metal transport. Our study provides mechanistic insights into how wildfire-derived or burning-derived DOM alters subsurface Cd geochemistry, with implications for the coupled cycling of carbon, iron, and trace metals in fire-impacted terrestrial environments.

title: Mechanisms of iodate reduction by sediment siderite and its contribution to iodide enrichment in groundwater
description: Publication date: 30 September 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 720 Author(s): Shilin Zhao, Junxia Li, Yinchun Su, Daolian Deng, Wenyi Zhang, Qian Liao, Xianjun Xie, Yanxin Wang
abstract: The enrichment of iodine in groundwater poses serious health risks worldwide, yet the abiotic mechanisms driving iodine mobilization in anoxic aquifers remain incompletely understood. Siderite, a ubiquitous Fe(II)-bearing mineral in reducing environments, may play an important role in iodine speciation; however, its reactivity toward iodine species transformation remains largely unexplored. Herein, we investigated the reduction of iodate (IO3 −) by siderite and the subsequent mechanisms of iodine release using both synthetic minerals and natural sediments from the Hetao Basin with varying Fe(II)‑carbonate contents. Batch kinetic experiments demonstrated that structural Fe(II) in siderite rapidly reduced IO3 − to highly mobile iodide (I−) within 20 min. The reduction kinetics and mineral transformation pathways were strongly controlled by the initial Fe(II)siderite:IO3 − molar ratio: excess IO3 − promoted the oxidation of siderite to goethite (FeOOH), whereas excess Fe(II)siderite favored the formation of magnetite (Fe3O4). Incubation experiments with natural sediments further revealed the critical role of intrinsic Fe(II)‑carbonate content in determining the IO3 − reduction capacity of sediments. Deep sediments enriched in siderite rapidly reduced IO3 − to I−, whereas shallow, siderite-depleted sediments exhibited negligible reduction. In addition, amendment of these shallow sediments with exogenous siderite induced the release of intrinsic sediment-bound iodine into the aqueous phase as I−. Overall, this study highlights the importance of siderite in iodine species transformation and provides new mechanistic insights into iodine enrichment in reducing groundwater systems.

title: Carboxyl-Fe and phosphonate-Fe interactions control the redistribution of organic phosphate during ferrihydrite transformation
description: Publication date: 30 September 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 720 Author(s): Xiaofan Pan, Zhenzhen Zhao, Xin Huang, Ning Deng
abstract: Transformation of poorly crystalline ferrihydrite (Fh) into crystalline phases is a critical process controlling mineral stability and element cycling. However, the molecular mechanisms by which organic phosphorus (OP) compounds influence Fh transformation remain unclear. Here, we investigated the effects of three representative OPs with distinct functional groups—triethyl phosphate (TEP), 2-phosphonobutane-1,2,4-tricarboxylic acid (PBTC), and 1-hydroxyethylidene-1,1-diphosphonic acid (HEDP)—on Fh transformation. Results showed that TEP, containing only a phosphate group, showed negligible adsorption and minimal effect, whereas PBTC and HEDP strongly bound to Fh via carboxyl and phosphonate groups, respectively, significantly slowing transformation. Synchrotron-based FTIR indicated that PBTC predominantly bound to Fh through strong Fe-carboxyl interactions, while HEDP mainly formed Fe-phosphonate complexes on Fh surfaces. The stronger carboxyl-mediated surface complexation of PBTC resulted in persistent association with the solid phase throughout the transformation process. In contrast, HEDP exhibited dynamic redistribution during Fh transformation, characterized by initial release followed by re-immobilization. Geochemical modeling showed that the complexation of HEDP with aqueous Fe3+ favored the incorporation of Fe3+-HEDP complexes into growing secondary mineral phases, leading to HEDP refixation. These results reveal that OP functional groups govern both Fe mineral stability and OPs fate, providing mechanistic insights into organic ligand-mediated Fe mineral evolution.

title: Subseafloor processes in ultramafic-influenced volcanic-hosted hydrothermal systems: An insight from the Gnitahei massive sulfide mineralization, Arctic Mid-Ocean Ridges
description: Publication date: 30 September 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 720 Author(s): Sabina Strmić Palinkaš, Marie Wold, Rolf Birger Pedersen, Håvard Hallås Stubseid, Fredrik Sahlström, Lahaye Yann, Leif-Erik Rydland Pedersen, Jorge E. Spangenberg
abstract: The extinct Gnitahei seafloor massive sulfide (SMS) deposit was discovered in 2019 on the ultraslow spreading Mohns Ridge (Arctic Mid-Ocean Ridge System, 72.8°N, 3.81°E, 3022–2760 mbsl). It provides a unique opportunity to study subseafloor hydrothermal processes without drilling, as tectonic uplift and ongoing mass wasting expose the deeper parts of the hydrothermal system. The deposit is hosted by hydrothermally altered basalts within the footwall of a NE–SW striking normal fault, in proximity to the active Fåvne Vent Field. Driven by extensional tectonics and facilitated by the thin oceanic crust along the ultraslow-spreading Mohns Ridge, hydrothermal circulation likely extends deep into the serpentinized upper mantle. Hydrothermal alteration exhibits vertical zonation. Chloritization accompanied by remobilization of silica, LILEs, and REEs dominate the deeper parts of the system. In contrast, silicification associated with an enrichment in LILEs and REEs characterizes the upper part of the Gnitahei SMS deposit. The paleosurface is clearly marked by a layer of red jasper. The sulfide mineralization is dominated by pyrite and marcasite, with euhedral pyrite prevailing in deeper zones and colloform pyrite being more abundant near the paleosurface. Native gold occurs mostly as inclusions in pyrite. Trace-element data obtained from pyrite, including elevated Ni and Co concentrations and a high Au/Ag ratios, are consistent with fluid interaction with underlying ultramafic rocks. Sulfur isotope composition of pyrite reveals a strong 34S enrichment (bulk δ34SVCDT = 11.1–15.9‰; in-situ δ34SVCDT = 10.8–17.3‰), indicating a significant contribution of reduced seawater sulfate, which constitutes ∼50% of the total sulfur according to a two-component mixing model. The high influx of reduced sulfate is attributed to reducing conditions driven by serpentinization of ultramafic lithologies. Under these conditions, seawater sulfate can be reduced prior to anhydrite deposition, allowing isotopically heavy sulfur to infiltrate the hydrothermal system. Depth-dependent decreases in δ34S values likely reflect greater contributions of reduced seawater sulfate in shallower zones and/or enhanced fractionation at lower temperatures.

title: A first principles critique of the back calculation method: Understanding and assessing the alteration of atmospheric gases trapped in ancient fluid inclusions
description: Publication date: 30 September 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 720 Author(s): Justin G. Park, Morgan F. Schaller
abstract: The extraction of atmospheric gases from fluid inclusions has emerged as an extremely promising approach for directly constraining the composition of Earth's ancient atmosphere. However, the veracity of data obtained from these inclusions critically depends on how well one can account for the effects of physical chemistry and post-depositional alteration. The Back Calculation Method (BCM) attempts to discern unaltered atmospheric compositions from variably modified inclusion gases, primarily O2 and CO2, but fails to account for the effects of gas solubility. Moreover, the method lacks an explicit mathematical formulation, and limited articulation of its implicit assumptions and limitations has introduced ambiguity in the interpretation of reconstructed atmospheric compositions. From first principles, we derive the formulation underlying the BCM and use it to formally evaluate the limitations of the method. We expand this framework to include the variable effects of gas solubility and incorporate recent techniques to partition inclusion volatiles trapped in the gaseous and aqueous phases. Re-examination of modern inclusion gases reveals evidence of heterogeneous entrapment of gas and brine, as well as post-entrapment alteration of O2 and CO2, with distinct stoichiometric relationships observed between samples. These observations violate the core assumptions of the BCM, suggesting the technique has been applied inappropriately to ancient samples and that their interpreted atmospheric compositions require thorough reevaluation. We conclude by demonstrating carbon isotope measurements of inclusion CO2 can be incorporated to assess the extent of gas alteration and provide an outline for future work intending to reconstruct atmospheric compositions from these inclusions.

title: The influence of coral nutritional status on its skeletal carbon isotope fractionation and δ 13 C values
description: Publication date: 30 September 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 720 Author(s): Shendong Xu, Jie Gao, Zhinan Zhang, Kefu Yu, Yiqi Zhao, Biao Chen
abstract: Almost all scleractinian corals are mixotrophic organisms and their skeleton stable carbon isotopes (δ13Cs) were widely used for environmental and climatic records. However, the interpretation of coral δ13Cs is still complicated and controversial. In particular, the impact of nutritional status (i.e. relative intensity of autotrophic photosynthetic and heterotrophic predation) and related photosynthesis/respiration ratio (P/R) on the coral δ13Cs was not well understood. In this study, coral samples (Favia palauensis) were collected from three coral reefs of different latitudes in the South China Sea (SCS), Weizhou (∼21°N), Xisha (∼16°N) and Nansha (∼9°N) Islands. Different types of physiological and geochemical parameters, including symbiodiniaceae (i.e. symbiotic zooxanthellae) density, tissue biomass, δ13C of zooxanthellae (δ13Cz), host tissue (δ13Ch), skeleton (δ13Cs) were measured. We also collected environmental and ambient seawater parameters, including ‌Sea Surface Temperature, ‌Sea Surface Salinity, Photosynthetically Active Radiation, Rainfall and Seawater δ18O and δ13CDIC. The P/R ratio was calculated based on these parameters. We conducted this study to analysis the spatial distribution characteristics of coral nutritional status, and then explore the potential impacts of coral's nutritional status on their P/R ratios and skeletal δ13C in the SCS. Our results show that corals have relatively high autotrophic photosynthesis intensity and P/R ratios in Weizhou reef. On the contrary, corals in relatively low latitude Xisha and Nansha reefs are more dependent on heterotrophic predation and have lower P/R ratios. Correspondingly, coral δ13Cs is more positive in Weizhou than that in Xisha and Nansha. In particular, there are high correlations between δ13Cs and δ13Cz of corals in Weizhou, but not in Xisha and Nansha. Overall, the corals in all three reef areas showed a positive correlation between P/R and δ13Cs values (p<0.05). These results indicate that different coral nutritional status and related P/R have different effects on δ13Cs. This maybe one of the important factors leading to the spatial variation of skeletal δ13C in the SCS. We suggest that special attention should be paid to this case when using coral skeletal δ13C for paleoclimate reconstruction, especially when conducting comparative analysis of climate in different regions of the world based on coral skeletal δ13C.

title: Selenium isotope fractionation during pyrite oxidation and acid mine drainage formation: Combined field and experimental constraints
description: Publication date: 30 September 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 720 Author(s): José Luis Guerrero, Stephan König, Rafael Pérez-López, Carolina Rosca, Carlos J. Garrido, José Miguel Nieto
abstract: Selenium (Se) is a redox-sensitive chalcophile element whose isotopes provide valuable constraints on oxidative processes at the Earth's surface. This study presents a combined field and experimental investigation of Se isotope fractionation (δ82/76Se) during pyrite (FeS2) oxidation under acid mine drainage (AMD) conditions, integrating field observations, column experiments, geochemical modeling, and mineralogical characterization. Field leachates from the Tharsis mining district (Iberian Pyrite Belt) exhibit extreme acidity (pH ≈ 1–2), elevated Eh values (> 600 mV) consistent with ongoing pyrite oxidation, elevated Se concentrations (up to 1.3 × 103 μg/L), and significant isotopic variability, with δ82/76Se values ranging from −4.1 ± 0.53‰ at the waste dump outflow to +1.19 ± 0.07‰ in a receiving pond. Column experiments reproduce and extend this trend, with early leachates showing slightly negative values (≈ −1‰) attributed to rapid flushing of isotopically light, labile Se pools, followed by a progressive increase to a stable plateau of +12 ± 1‰. Speciation modeling indicates that dissolved Se occurs predominantly as Se(IV), excluding redox partitioning between aqueous oxidation states as the main control on Se isotope fractionation. Rayleigh-type calculations show that adsorption alone cannot account for the observed >10‰ isotopic shift. Instead, the isotopic evolution reflects open-system processes involving continuous Se release from sulfide oxidation, surface interactions with Fe(III) phases, and localized redox transformations. The agreement between field and experimental trends defines a coherent framework for Se isotope behavior during sulfide weathering. These results demonstrate the high mobility of Se under AMD conditions and highlight the potential of δ82/76Se as a tracer of oxidative release and attenuation processes in natural and mining-impacted environments.

title: Experimental insights into chlorine and bromine isotope fractionation during evaporation and mineral precipitation in multicomponent brines
description: Publication date: 30 September 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 720 Author(s): Yon-Gyung Ryuh, Randy L. Stotler, Shaun K. Frape
abstract: Chloride and bromide are commonly used as tracers in various aqueous geochemistry fields as a result of their well-known conservative behaviors. However, the behavior of their stable isotopes during evaporation and mineral precipitation remains poorly constrained. This study investigates how chlorine and bromine isotopes fractionate during evaporation of seawater. Synthetic seawater was evaporated under controlled conditions, and the isotopic compositions of chlorine and bromine were measured in brine, solids, and gas phase throughout sequential mineral precipitation. The results show that chlorine and bromine isotopes respond to distinct processes that vary with mineralogy and evaporation stage. Bromine isotopes fractionate during early calcium-phase precipitation through lattice substitution into aragonite, but mineralogical shifts with increasing salinity result in Br incorporation into precipitates through physical brine entrapment limiting further fractionation. In contrast, during halite precipitation, chlorine isotopes exhibit systematic lattice-controlled fractionation behavior broadly consistent with near-equilibrium fractionation, while bromine isotopes exhibit more complex behavior. Bromine isotope evolution during this stage is interpreted to reflect a combination of inefficient lattice incorporation and selective loss of isotopically light bromine to the gas phase. These findings suggest that chlorine and bromine isotopes may respond differently due to mineral-specific and process-dependent mechanisms, highlighting processes that may influence halogen isotope signatures in natural evaporite and saline systems.

title: Organic carbon enrichment in carbonate concretions of the Rincon Shale, California, USA: Implications for organic matter preservation in concretions
description: Publication date: 30 September 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 720 Author(s): Sean J. Loyd, Melonie D. Reyes, Natasha Kuhn, Adam D. Woods, Allyson M. Fry-Petit, Ashley E. Godoy
abstract: Carbonate concretions often form as a byproduct of the degradation of organic matter and/or methane in sediments. Despite these origins, concretions may subsequently protect sedimentary organic matter from degradation after precipitation. The degree to which concretions preferentially preserve organic material is poorly characterized, as are the degradation processes/environments against which they are most effective. Here, concretions and host sediment of the Miocene Rincon Shale are compared geochemically to assess the preservation capacity of concretions. Magnesian calcite and dolomite concretions of the Rincon Shale express carbonate carbon isotope compositions (δ13Ccarb) consistent with formation via microbial oxidative reactions and methanogenesis, respectively. Host shale laminae deflection around the concretions and high cement contents suggest that concretions formed at relatively shallow sediment depths during early diagenesis. Concretions contain higher concentrations of total carbonate-free organic carbon (TOCCF), iron, and manganese than neighboring host shales. When considered collectively, host shale and concretion Oxygen Index (OI) data correlate with TOCCF contents, consistent with oxidative weathering. However, most concretions express lower OI compositions than neighboring shales. Combined lower OI and higher TOCCF, iron, and manganese in concretions suggest that concretions protect organic matter and metal sulfides from oxidative weathering in outcrop. This preferential preservation indicates that concretions 1) represent a better target for outcrop-based study using organic archives and 2) may delay the weathering of sedimentary organic matter and impact carbon cycling.

title: 40 Ar/ 39 Ar geochronology, Sr Nd isotopes and melting conditions of the Dahongshan alkaline basalts: Constraints on mantle modification beneath the northern Yangtze Craton
description: Publication date: 30 September 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 720 Author(s): Yue Song, Xuan-Ce Wang, Simon A. Wilde, Xiang-Zhong Li, Chong-Jin Pang, Si-Yu Hu, Yang Luo, Jia-Xu Tang, Si-Zhe Fu
abstract: We present new groundmass 40Ar/39Ar ages, whole-rock major and trace element data, SrNd isotopic compositions, and P–T estimates for the Dahongshan alkaline basalts in the northern Yangtze Craton, China. Integrating these data with regional records demonstrates that Late Cretaceous mafic magmatism in the northern Yangtze Craton records a transition from subduction-modified lithospheric mantle to increasingly asthenosphere-influenced melting. Four representative samples yield concordant plateau-like weighted mean 40Ar/39Ar ages of 83.4–84.1 Ma (2σ), constraining the eruption of Dahongshan magmas to ca. 84 Ma. The basalts have intraplate, OIB-like trace element patterns, elevated LREE/HREE ratios, and a narrow range of SrNd isotopic compositions ((87Sr/86Sr)ᵢ = 0.704358–0.704800; εNd(t) = −0.80 to +1.35), indicating derivation from a moderately enriched, pyroxenite-influenced mantle source with a mafic component and only limited syn-ascent crustal assimilation. Low Ce/Pb and Nb/U ratios, together with pronounced positive Pb anomalies, are interpreted as source-inherited features rather than evidence for significant crustal assimilation. Primary melt reconstruction and complementary whole-rock major element modelling yield low- to moderate-pressure P–T estimates of 1.4–2.1 GPa and 1252–1356 °C, interpreted to record final melt–mantle equilibration or segregation during ascent rather than the depth of melt initiation. In contrast, REE systematics indicate a garnet-influenced melting signal, suggesting that melt generation was initiated deeper, probably near the garnet–spinel transition, before undergoing re-equilibration at shallower lithospheric levels. Regional comparisons support a temporal shift from Early Cretaceous lithosphere-derived arc-like magmatism to Late Cretaceous increasingly asthenosphere-influenced volcanism, followed by Cenozoic deeper-sourced alkaline basalts consistent with garnet-facies melting during post-extension thermal adjustment.

title: Mineralogical and geochemical fingerprints for quantifying modern glacial and paleo-weathering sediments in the Amundsen Sea, West Antarctica
description: Publication date: 30 September 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 720 Author(s): Hebin Shao, Yong Yu, Shouye Yang, Jianfeng He, Yulong Guo, Di Cai, Guangfu Luo, Yingchun Cui, Li Wu, Hao Zhang
abstract: Silicate weathering regulates Earth's carbon cycle and climate, yet paleo-weathering products in Antarctic marine sediments obscure primary weathering signatures, a major challenge in polar carbon cycle studies. The Amundsen Sea, a key marginal sea of West Antarctica, contains abundant paleo-weathering products (i.e. materials sourced from Pre-Oligocene sedimentary rocks and reworked into modern sediments), but quantitative constraints on their contributions to sediment provenance remain lacking. We analyzed 12 clay-sized surface sediment samples from the western Amundsen Sea via mineralogical, elemental geochemical, and Sr-Nd-Li-Mg isotopic analyses. Results show clear spatial heterogeneity: samples from the east side of this area show higher kaolinite, chemical index of alteration (CIA) and δ26Mg, along with lower δ7Li. The proxies reveal intense chemical weathering of the source bedrock in the pre-glacial warm interval. By contrast, samples from the west side are dominated by chlorite and illite, with lower CIA and δ26Mg but higher δ7Li, reflecting limited chemical weathering of the source bedrock. Mineralogical and geochemical indices effectively distinguish three sediment provenance endmembers (Post-Oligocene igneous rocks, Pre-Oligocene igneous rocks, and Pre-Oligocene sedimentary rocks), and a mass balance model based on εNd and δ26Mg isotopes was established to quantify their relative contributions to shelf sediment provenance. This model shows that paleo-weathering sediments account for up to 60% of clay-sized sediments from the eastern side of the western Amundsen Sea, with contributions of 30%–50% in coastal areas via ocean current transport, while clay-sized sediments from the west side are dominated by modern glacial weathering products of Post-Oligocene volcanic rocks (up to 64%). Our findings establish a multi-proxy mineralogical and geochemical fingerprint framework for distinguishing and quantifying modern glacial and paleo-weathering sediments in West Antarctica, and provide critical insights for paleoclimatic reconstruction and understanding the impact of glacial erosion on marine carbon cycle dynamics in Antarctica.

title: Alteration kinetics of basaltic glass in acidic conditions: The effect of temperature and pH on glass dissolution and alteration layer formation
description: Publication date: 30 September 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 720 Author(s): Arpad Pusztai, Bastien Wild, Samuel Tardif, Zijie Liu, François Guyot, Imene Esteve, Alejandro Fernandez-Martinez, Damien Daval
abstract: Quantifying basaltic glass alteration kinetics is essential for modelling carbon sequestration and global biogeochemical cycles. However, current literature rates diverge by up to two orders of magnitude due to surface area normalization uncertainties (BET vs. geometric) and conflicting reports on the pH-dependence of activation energies (E a ). In this study, we resolve these inconsistencies by combining Vertical Scanning Interferometry (VSI) and in situ synchrotron X-ray Reflectivity (XRR) to decouple glass network dissolution from Amorphous Silica-rich Surface Layer (ASSL) growth between 5 and 60 °C and pH 2–5. Our results demonstrate that both dissolution and ASSL growth proceed linearly over time, following a surface-reaction-controlled regime. We show that the surface retreat method (VSI) provides a robust, normalization-independent proxy for network breakdown, yielding rates consistent with Si release. Furthermore, XRR data reveal that steady-state ASSL densities decrease with increasing growth rates, suggesting the formation of more porous structures at low pH. Contrary to common assumptions in long-term field rates, we find no evidence of surface passivation: ASSLs remain permeable and do not act as diffusion barriers over weeks-long experiments, accounting for up to 80% of the total altered volume. The temperature dependence of the dissolution rate (r) is best described by a pH-dependent Arrhenius law: r = A pH . exp − E a , pH RT a H + n where A pH is the pH-dependent preexponential factor, R is the gas constant, a H+ is the activity of protons, n the reaction order with respect to protons, which is close to 1 on the investigated temperature range, and where the apparent E a decreases from 62.9 ± 2.0 kJ/mol at pH 2 to values near zero (< 20 kJ/mol) as the pH approaches the point of zero charge of the glass. By providing quantitatively decoupled kinetics for substrate dissolution and layer formation, this work offers a high-resolution framework to refine predictive models of basalt weathering in both natural and engineered acidic environments.

title: A lithium isotopic perspective of basalt weathering: Cycling of Li and its mobility relative to ca and Mg
description: Publication date: Available online 5 August 2026 Source: Chemical Geology Author(s): Anup Kumar Sharma, Tarun Kumar Dalai, Sambuddha Misra, Prem Chand Kisku, Jitendra Kumar Pattanaik
abstract: Lithium isotope compositions (δ7Li) are extensively utilized to trace silicate weathering and reverse weathering in both terrestrial and marine realms. Although the direction and magnitude of Li isotope fractionation during Li adsorption onto secondary minerals are well understood, the relative influence of Li partitioning via its adsorption vis-à-vis structural incorporation into clay minerals on overall Li isotope fractionation remains poorly constrained. In this study, we attempt to determine the processes regulating Li distribution and its isotope fractionation by quantifying the Li concentration and isotope ratio of the bulk, exchangeable, oxyhydroxide phases, and clay-sized fractions of two basaltic weathering profiles from the Rajmahal Volcanic Province (India). The observed decrease in δ7Li values toward the top of the weathering profiles, coupled with increases in Li/Al, Fe/Al, and Mn/Al ratios, indicates role of clay minerals and FeMn oxyhydroxides in the preferential adsorption and/or structural incorporation of 6Li. In the Dalahi profile, adsorption and desorption of Li exhibits possible pH dependency. Mass balance calculations demonstrate that crystal-bound Li in clay minerals dominates the total Li budget of the weathered basalts and therefore, drives the depth-dependent variation in δ7Li within the weathering profiles. There is excellent agreement between two independent calculations of δ7Li of weathering solutions, which are about 8.1–12.6‰ higher than that of the parent basalts. Notably, calculated δ7Li values for weathering solutions are within the range of δ7Li offsets observed between the rocks and solutions in river and groundwater systems in basaltic catchments. We established empirical relationships between δ7Li, mobility of Li relative to Ca and Mg, and the chemical index of alteration (CIA) in weathering profiles. These relationships provide a framework for reliable prediction of δ7Li and Li mobility relative to Ca and Mg during basaltic weathering. Additionally, by integrating published data on δ7Li and CIA in river sediments with the results of this study, we demonstrate that δ7Li values of river sediments can be predicted from their CIA values. The results and findings of this study provide new insights for investigating weathering processes in both modern and ancient records by using δ7Li as a tracer of weathering intensity and the relative mobilities of Li, Ca and Mg.

title: Flux-dominated crustal helium enrichment beyond Cratonic Basins: Evidence from geothermal fluids in the Cathaysia Block, South China
description: Publication date: Available online 4 August 2026 Source: Chemical Geology Author(s): Xuelian Huang, Shuai Wang, Yunkai Lei, Xueqing Wu, Jingyu Lin, Xiangxian Ma, Wenjing Lin, Daniele L. Pinti, Guodong Zheng, Shihua Qi
abstract: Helium (He) is an irreplaceable resource for medical applications and high-end manufacturing. Global He production is currently dominated by He-rich natural gas accumulations in cratonic basins, whereas the origin and release–migration processes of He in tectonically active zones remain poorly constrained. This study investigates geothermal fluids from the Cathaysia Block (CB) in southern China, a representative tectonically reworked continental region, using newly collected and compiled gas and noble gas data (n = 217) to elucidate the formation of He-rich geothermal systems outside cratonic settings. He concentrations in geothermal gases range from 10 to 18,300 ppm, and He-rich samples (He >1000 ppm) are consistently characterized by N2-dominated compositions. He concentrations are systematically higher in the inland domain than in coastal areas, and extremely He-rich fluids (He >10,000 ppm) occur exclusively in areas adjacent to Precambrian crustal relics. He isotope ratios (0.04–2.28 Rc/Ra) indicate minor mantle contributions, while radiogenic crustal He dominates (67.2–99.7%). Compositional and isotopic relationships among He–CO2–N2 suggest that He enrichment is jointly controlled by CO2 removal and the addition of He-rich deep fluids. Regional thermal anomalies and seismic activities enhanced the mobilization of He accumulated in both Yanshanian high-radioactivity granites and Precambrian continental fragments, while deep major faults act as efficient migration pathways. Overall, the He-rich geothermal system in the CB exhibits the characteristics of an open crustal He flux system, defined by favorable source rocks, enhanced release, rapid migration, and limited preservation. Under suitable sealing conditions, such systems may also have He accumulation potential in sedimentary basins (e.g., the Sanshui Basin). Our results demonstrate that tectonically active regions can host flux-dominated crustal He systems and highlight the need to expand He exploration beyond conventional cratonic basins to tectonically reworked continental margins worldwide.

title: High precision water quantification by Raman spectroscopy: Applications to volcanic and extraterrestrial samples
description: Publication date: Available online 4 August 2026 Source: Chemical Geology Author(s): E.G. Huggins, E. Gazel, M. Gavrilenko, K. Dayton, J.D. Bixler, W.H. Towbin, T. Plank
abstract: Volcanic petrology is a promising field to quantify processes that occur during eruptions, but it currently relies on very expensive and complex analytical techniques. Of particular importance is the development of precise, high spatial resolution techniques to measure volatile species (e.g., H2O, CO2, S) in volcanic glasses for understanding magmatic storage and eruptive potential. H2O controls the chemical and physical properties of magmas, impacting crystallization, viscosity, and buoyancy, and plays a significant role in the development of terrestrial planets. The predominant tools used to measure volatiles in volcanic glasses (as recorded in melt inclusions; MIs) typically require extensive and time-consuming sample preparation, and instrumentation is often not available in the timeframe of ongoing volcanic eruptions. Confocal Raman spectroscopy provides an alternative method that has been used successfully in recent years to quantify H2O contents of volcanic glasses and MIs with high spatial resolution, minimal sample preparation, and high throughput, such that samples can be analyzed within hours to days following sample collection. Here, we present high-precision calibrations for measuring dissolved H2O in silicate glasses by Raman spectroscopy using a high-energy 473-nm (blue) excitation source. To understand how this calibration compares to those derived from other microanalytical techniques, we analyzed reference glasses commonly used in different laboratories to calibrate volatile species. We then applied this calibration to exposed terrestrial MIs, melt embayments, and unexposed terrestrial and Martian MIs. The development of a method to measure water concentrations in unexposed MIs is critical for applications where preservation of rare samples is essential.

title: Bromine solubility in silicate melts and its implications for volcanic HBr degassing
description: Publication date: Available online 3 August 2026 Source: Chemical Geology Author(s): Lauren R. Gorojovsky, Richard W. Thomas, Bernard J. Wood
abstract: We have determined the solubility of bromine in silicate melts using Ag-AgBr(±AgI) buffers to control fBr2, together with C-CO-CO2 and Re–ReO2 buffers to control fO2 over a broad range of melt compositions at 0.5–2.5 GPa and 1200–1500 °C. In the dilute region, melt Br concentrations vary with fB r 2 0.5 and f O 2 − 0.25 , consistent with dissolution through the exchange of two Br− ions for one O2− ion, analogous to the mechanism proposed for chlorine. Henry's law behaviour extends to 1.1 wt% Br, well above concentrations in natural melts. We use these relationships to define bromide capacity and, by combining our results with published hydrous fluid-melt partitioning data, derive a model applicable from 790 to 1500 °C and 0.1–2.5 GPa. The resulting equation is: log C Br = 3.94 + − 972 X SiO 2 + 3360 X FeO tot + 3382 X CaO − 659 X H O 0.5 + 201 X Na O 0.5 − 11 X K O 0.5 − 1277 P − 6322 / T where T is in K, P in GPa, and Xi denotes single cation oxide mole fraction. Bromide capacity decreases with increasing pressure and temperature, decreases with increasing SiO2 and K2O contents, and increases with CaO and FeO, so that bromine solubility decreases in the order basalt > andesite > dacite > rhyolite. Bromide capacity is lower than chloride capacity for all compositions investigated, showing that bromine is consistently less soluble than chlorine in silicate melts. Despite this lower melt solubility, application of the bromide capacity model to H2O-rich low-pressure fluids indicate that Br and Cl degas similarly as HBr and HCl, respectively, so the HBr/HCl ratio of volcanic gases should closely reflect the Br/Cl ratio of the melt with little fractionation. These results provide a thermodynamic framework for modelling bromine behaviour in magmatic and volcanic systems.

title: Carbonate precipitation and CO₂ sources in a Hypersaline Crater Lake of the Pali Aike Volcanic Field, Southern Patagonia
description: Publication date: Available online 3 August 2026 Source: Chemical Geology Author(s): Carolina Henríquez, Raphael Pietzsch, Leonardo Fadel Cury, Paulo Quezada, Guido Alonso, Luis Mancini, Mauricio Calderón, Anelize Bahniuk
abstract: Carbonate precipitation in southern high-latitude environments remains poorly constrained in terms of its controlling mechanisms, particularly in continental settings where climatic extremes, volcanic substrates, and inherited glacial processes converge. Here we investigate carbonate formation in an alkaline lake hosted within Middle Pleistocene maars of the Pali Aike Volcanic Field, southern Patagonia. This setting provides a natural laboratory to investigate interactions between silicate weathering, carbon cycling, and CaCO₃ supersaturation. Mineralogical and geochemical data, including 87Sr/86Sr, δ13C, and δ18O, from carbonates, basalts, soils, sediments, and lake waters were used to constrain the processes controlling carbonate precipitation. The δ13C composition of dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) indicates that silicate weathering involving soil-derived and atmospheric CO₂ is the primary source of carbon to the lake system. Carbonate speciation reveals a strong dominance of HCO₃− and CO₃2− over dissolved CO₂ in the lake carbon pool. Strontium isotopic compositions identify mafic rock weathering as the principal source of dissolved Ca. Combined evidence from Sr partitioning, weathering indices, aqueous geochemistry, and stable isotopes indicates carbonate precipitation under sustained supersaturation, modulated by kinetic constraints rather than simple equilibrium conditions. These results define an integrated geochemical framework in which silicate weathering intensity, carbon cycle dynamics, and precipitation kinetics jointly regulate carbonate formation, with implications for interpreting lacustrine carbonate archives in high-latitude continental systems.

title: 40 Ar/ 39 Ar calibration of sanidine standards QSs and YBCs with Fish Canyon sanidine
description: Publication date: Available online 1 August 2026 Source: Chemical Geology Author(s): Paul R. Renne, Brian R. Jicha, William S. Cassata, Roland Mundil, Andrew J. Tholt
abstract: ~30 Ma (YBCs) and ~ 120 Ma (QSs) sanidines are evaluated as 40Ar/39Ar standards in comparison with existing standards of similar ages. 40Ar*/39ArK ratios (F-values) in each relative to the widely used Fish Canyon sanidine (i.e. R FCs YBCs and R FCs QSs ) were determined on three different mass spectrometers. YCBs proved to have excess between-grain dispersion of F values and K/Ca, low %40Ar*, and is deemed to be inferior to the similarly-aged Taylor Creek sanidine (TCs) as a 40Ar/39Ar standard. QSs is significantly more reproducible at the single-grain level in terms of F values and K/Ca, and is recommended as an international standard in favor of the ~99 Ma GA-1550 biotite. New CA-IDTIMS UPb data on zircons from the QSs host obsidian yield an inferred eruption age of 120.56 ± 0.26 Ma (2σ), indistinguishable from the sanidine 40Ar/39Ar age determined by the most recent 40Ar/39Ar-U-Pb intercalibration. Further radioisotopic analyses of both phases in other labs would be desirable in order to increase the utility of data from this sample for ongoing intercalibration efforts.

title: Towards accurate Ca isotope fractionation at equilibrium between minerals and aqueous solutions with electronic structure calculations: Multi-framework comparison for validation and correction, and the control of structural cations
description: Publication date: Available online 30 July 2026 Source: Chemical Geology Author(s): Merlin Méheut, Vasileios Mavromatis, Magali Benoît, Jacques Schott
abstract: Theoretical calculation of equilibrium fractionation of Ca isotopes shows particularly challenging due to the limitations of DFT frameworks to properly reproduce the important vibrational properties. This is even more challenging for mineral-solution equilibria, as frameworks adapted to minerals do not properly reproduce aqueous solution structures. Based on careful correction of calculated frequencies by experimental ones, a rescaling parameter can be proposed to obtain reference ln β values from eight different theoretical frameworks, within an uncertainty ( σ ) ranging between 0.25 ‰ (PBEsol and PBE functionals) and 0.75 ‰ (LDA functional, PBE or BLYP functionals with Grimme-D2 correction) at 300K. Frameworks showing more consistent structural prediction (with consistent offsets on Ca-O distances) also show more consistent predicted fractionation properties. Eight well characterized minerals (anhydrite, fluorite, diopside, grossular, calcite, dolomite, aragonite, CaO lime) were used for the validation and correction procedure, and six more (wollastonite, anorthite, huntite, monticellite, akermanite, gypsum) were calculated to infer the controls of Ca isotope fractionation and compare to experimental or natural estimates. Ca isotopes fractionation properties of a mineral shows connected to Ca-O distance, coordination and the type of structural cation, following the expression: (1) l n α m i n e r a l − C a O = l n β C a O × ( b × Δ d + c ( c o o r d ) + d ( c a t i o n ) ) , where α m i n e r a l − C a O is the fractionation of Ca isotopes with respect to CaO lime; β C a O is the β -factor of CaO lime; Δ d is the relative difference in Ca-O distance between the mineral and CaO lime; b=-7.44 at 300K; c is the coordination effect, varying monotonically from 0 for c(6) to ≈ +0.30 for c(8)=c(9); d is the effect of the cations present in the structure (in addition to Ca2＋), determined for Si 4 + , S 5 + , C 4 + , P 5 + (based on Antonelli et al. (2019) calculations), and H + . The obtained cation effects appear to be related to their electronegativities. Assuming calcite-Ca2＋(aq.) fractionation as null, one can compare our predicted mineral-calcite fractionations with experimental mineral-Ca2＋(aq.) fractionations. The predicted aragonite-calcite and anhydrite-calcite fractionations are twice as large as the corresponding mineral-Ca2＋(aq.) experimental values, suggesting perturbing effects in solution (speciation, kinetic effects). On the contrary, predicted gypsum-calcite fractionations are in agreement with gypsum-Ca2＋(aq.) experimental values. Predicted dolomite-calcite fractionation agrees with fractionation occurring during biogenic dolomite precipitation, but dolomitization does not seem to follow isotopic equilibrium.

title: The selenium cycling variation corresponding to the evolution of early animals in the Weng'an biota
description: Publication date: Available online 27 July 2026 Source: Chemical Geology Author(s): Zhiyuan Ren, Jie Long, Shixi Zhang, Yajun Du, Tengwen Long, Yung-Tsang Chen, Kunli Luo
abstract: The Weng'an biota witnessed the critical expansion and differentiation of early animals in the Ediacaran Period. It shows an enrichment of bioessential elements such as Se and Mo accompanying the expansion of Megasphaera fossils. However, whether the expansion of early animals affected the Se source and its preservation remains unclear. This research focuses on studying the Se speciation and preservation variations in the Weng'an biota along with the occurrence, expansion, and disappearance of Megasphaera fossils and the covariation of redox conditions. Before the Megasphaera occurrence, it shows 14.5% of bioavailable Se(VI) and Se(IV) (29 ppb), 2% (up to 13 ppb) of Se(0), 57% (56 ppb) of Se(II) and 26.5% (40 ppb) of organic Se (Org-Se). The bioavailable Se(VI) and Se(IV) increased to 35% (160–8000 ppb) in the first occurrence datum of Megasphaera while the Se(0), Se(-II), and Org-Se decreased to 1% (155 ppb), 54% (7800 ppb), and 10% (1500 ppb) respectively. The Se(VI) + Se(IV) and Se(-II) changed to 46% (10,000 ppb) and 40% (9200 ppb) respectively within the acme interval of Megasphaera while the proportions of Se(0) and Org-Se remained similar to the occurrence layer. In the decline interval, the Se(VI) + Se(IV), Se(-II) and Org-Se varied to 9% (8 ppb), 76% (56 ppb), and 15% (40 ppb) respectively while the Se(0) became undetectable. After excluding the effects of terrestrial input and hydrothermal activities, we proposed that the Se cycling variation in the Weng'an biota was highly probably related to the evolution of Megasphaera.

title: Nitrate persistence and inland salinisation in an intensively irrigated Mediterranean river basin district: Diagnostic evidence from WFD monitoring data (Thessaly, central Greece)
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part A Author(s): Evangelos Tziritis, Dimitra Siakka, Vasilios Pisinaras
abstract: Intensive irrigation in semi-arid Mediterranean basins generates two co-occurring but mechanistically distinct groundwater stressors, nitrate contamination from fertiliser leaching and inland salinisation from ionic enrichment processes, that standard regulatory assessments fail to capture as a linked system. This study develops a probabilistic diagnostic framework and applies it to five years of Water Framework Directive (WFD) compliance monitoring data (2019–2023, 98 stations, 964 samples) from the Thessaly River Basin District, central Greece, one of Europe’s most groundwater-dependent agricultural systems. Multi-year median nitrate exceeded the 50 mg/L WFD threshold at 15.3% of stations and the 25 mg/L Nitrates Directive alert level at 28.6%; annual basin-wide medians remained within a narrow range (12.4–17.9 mg/L), consistent with quasi-steady-state release from legacy vadose zone stores. A bootstrap exceedance analysis (10,000 iterations) identified six stations where the 95% confidence interval for P(NO3 − > 50 mg/L) exceeded 0.50, three of which were located within officially compliant water bodies. Salinisation was spatially restricted, chloride-dominated (96.5% of high-EC records), and nearly completely decoupled from the nitrate footprint (7.1% co-exceedance). Na/Cl molar ratios and Gibbs diagram positioning indicate that evapoconcentrative and evaporitic processes are dominant salinisation mechanisms; however, ambiguous ionic signatures at a small number of stations preclude the definitive exclusion of relict or deep saline sources without isotopic confirmation. A Shannon entropy-weighted Compound Vulnerability Index and a classification concordance analysis (Cohen’s κ = 0.273) demonstrate that WFD spatial aggregation at the water body level systematically underestimates the active contamination footprint. The framework is reproducible from standard WISE data and can be directly transferred to any river basin district reporting WFD.

title: Divergent seasonal dynamics of high-resolution phosphorus speciation in sediment porewater of small estuaries
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part A Author(s): Yeran Yin, Hanchang Zhou, Yurui Li, Zheng Wang, Kai Xiao, Zhanrong Guo, Feng Pan, Bojie Fu
abstract: Dissolved reactive phosphorus (DRP) and dissolved organic phosphorus (DOP) are key constituents of the sediment porewater phosphorus (P) pool. However, a systematic understanding of their seasonal dynamics and coupling mechanisms, especially for DOP in small estuarine systems, remains limited. By combining in situ high-resolution porewater sampling with a microplate P digestion assay, we conducted a spatiotemporal investigation to elucidate the distribution, release mechanisms, and coupling with iron‑manganese (Fe-Mn) redox cycling of both DRP and DOP. The results showed that porewater DRP concentrations increased with depth and positively correlated with dissolved Fe-Mn, while DOP concentrations generally fluctuated with depth. DRP mobility was governed by the Fe-Mn redox sequence, featured by high availability under reducing conditions in summer and winter (mean of 0.36–0.44 mg L−1), whereas DOP production was driven by temperature-dependent organic matter (OM) mineralization merely in summer (mean of 0.79 mg L−1). The diffusion fluxes across the sediment–water interface confirmed these pathways: DRP release was minimal in oxic spring but increased in other seasons, while DOP release was strongly temperature-dependent, peaking exclusively in summer. Overall, the current results suggest that a seasonally differentiated dual‑pathway mechanism coordinates Fe-Mn redox and OM mineralization to control P speciation and release. These insights move beyond a simplistic view of internal P loading and are critical for understanding P dynamics in the two studied small estuarine systems.

title: Diverging hydrometeorological drivers of flashier floods in a warming climate
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part A Author(s): Fengjia Zhou, Shuo Wang, Louise Slater, Peirong Lin, Hanbo Yang, Sijie Tang, Amir AghaKouchak
abstract: The monitoring and forecasting of flash floods present significant challenges due to their rapid onset. While extreme rainfall events, a primary driver of flooding, are becoming flashier, there is no consensus on whether floods will exhibit similar trends in a warming climate. Here, we assess flash flood risk development over four decades across 741 basins globally using the flashiness index. Our findings reveal a significant shift towards flashier floods in nearly one-third of the basins, predominantly concentrated in cold and arid regions of the northern mid-latitudes. In these regions, the increase in flashiness is largely associated with larger flood peaks rather than changes in timing. We identify basins characterised by rising flood peaks, which are likely to require flood defence infrastructure capable of withstanding more severe flood events, as well as those marked by shorter onset times, which may face challenges in implementing short-term early warning systems. Specifically, the increase in flashiness in most North American basins is mainly associated with rising flood peaks, whereas in most European basins, it is dominated by shorter onset times. These findings underscore the urgency of implementing region-specific strategies to adapt to flashier floods in a warmer future.

title: HydEquivNet: bridging classical unit hydrograph theory and data-driven hydrology via scale-equivariant learning
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part A Author(s): Jingzhe Liu, Chenhui Jiang, Yongnan Zhu, Shan Jiang, Ziqian Gong, Jiaqi Zhai, Jing Zhao, Yulong Gao, Tao Wang
abstract: Traditional data-driven Deep Learning (DL) hydrological models often suffer from poor physical consistency and weak extrapolation robustness. To address this, we propose HydEquivNet (HEN), a novel architecture that introduces Lie group equivariance into hydrological modeling. By employing steerable Hermite basis convolutions, HEN embeds scale-equivariant physical priors into feature extraction, drawing on classical unit hydrograph theory and mass-consistency considerations to form learnable routing priors. The model utilizes a hybrid structure, integrating equivariant layers for physical feature extraction with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks for nonlinear residual compensation. Extensive validation on 531 Catchment Attributes and Meteorology for Large-sample Studies (CAMELS) catchments shows that HEN achieves a median Nash-Sutcliffe Efficiency (NSE) of 0.724 and avoids negative NSE values in the evaluated catchments. Controlled precipitation-scaling experiments further indicate improved equivariance-guided proportional-response robustness under synthetic out-of-distribution input amplification. Furthermore, model-derived routing diagnostics show interpretable unit-hydrograph-like response patterns, including a 0.94 bin-averaged correlation between extracted Peak Lag Time ( T p ) and a physically motivated concentration–time factor (CTF). HEN thus offers a parameter-efficient and transparent route toward more physically informed rainfall-runoff modeling under changing hydroclimatic conditions.

title: Natural and anthropogenic hydrodynamics shape selenium fate and risk in a sediment-laden river
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part A Author(s): Haotian Ma, Yidi Wang, Liang Shen, Hongbo Wang, Xavier Supe Tulcan, Ping Wang
abstract: Selenium (Se) dynamics in sediment-rich rivers are shaped by both natural hydrodynamics and anthropogenic regulation, but the mechanisms controlling its distribution among dissolved, suspended particulate, and sedimentary phases remain poorly understood. This study investigated the spatiotemporal patterns, controlling factors, and ecological and human health risks of Se in the Yellow River. Results showed that dissolved and sedimentary Se concentrations were consistently higher in autumn (dissolved mean: 1.14 μg/L; sedimentary mean: 0.30 mg/kg) than in spring (mean: 0.65 μg/L and 0.23 mg/kg, respectively), while suspended particulate matter (SPM)-Se exhibited an opposite seasonal trend, peaking in spring (mean: 0.50 mg/kg) compared to autumn (mean: 0.31 mg/kg). Spatial multivariate analyses revealed significant differences in Se distribution among different media, characterized by strong spatial heterogeneity in dissolved Se and comparatively homogenized patterns in particulate and sedimentary phases. Partitioning and driver identification analyses indicated that dissolved-particulate Se distribution was predominantly controlled by hydrodynamic conditions and suspended sediment variability. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-based SEM) further confirmed that hydrological conditions, anthropogenic factors, and nutrients jointly influenced Se redistribution, and highlighted the role of SPM as a transitional carrier between dissolved and sedimentary phases. While the basin-wide ecological and human health risks remained generally low, a seasonal shift in moderate ecological risk from the plateau headwaters in spring to the middle-lower reaches in autumn was observed. These findings underscore the necessity of incorporating hydrological dynamics and anthropogenic regulation into the risk management of hazardous trace elements in regulated river systems.

title: High-resolution spatiotemporal monitoring of chlorophyll-a in small inland reservoirs using multi-source remote sensing data fusion
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part A Author(s): Pengfei Han, Jian Wu, Jingjing Wu, Wei Wang, Chi Zhang, Zhuohang Xin
abstract: Small reservoirs are highly vulnerable to rapid cyanobacterial blooms, yet routine monitoring is constrained by the spatial–temporal trade-off of single-sensor satellite observations. To address this limitation, we fused Sentinel-2 MSI (10–20 m, ∼5 d) and Sentinel-3 OLCI (300 m, daily) data using the Spatial and Temporal Adaptive Reflectance Fusion Model (STARFM) to generate a Sentinel-2-like dataset (10 m, daily) for Zhuwei Reservoir during the ice-free seasons (April–November) of 2016–2024. Validation against coincident Sentinel-2 scenes showed good agreement between the fused and reference reflectance fields (RMSE 37 dB, SSIM > 0.8). After excluding oligotrophic and severe-bloom samples that were not used for quantitative retrieval, the remaining 93 paired samples collected during ten field campaigns in 2023–2024 were used to compare several established Chlorophyll-a (Chl-a) retrieval algorithms. The Normalized Difference Chlorophyll Index (NDCI) showed the best performance and was therefore selected as the most suitable algorithm for moderate-bloom conditions (R 2 = 0.72, RRMSE = 26.2%, and MAE = 11.89 μg/L). Application of the selected model to the fused record revealed a weak overall decline in reservoir-mean Chl-a (−0.313 μg/L/yr), pronounced summer maxima, and persistent hotspots in the northwestern, northern, and northeastern sectors. These results demonstrate the practical value of combining spatiotemporal fusion with locally evaluated Chl-a retrieval for gap-reduced monitoring of bloom dynamics in small reservoirs.

title: A machine-learning-enhanced fuzzy evaluation framework for hydrochemical evolution and ecohydrological attribution in a megacity river basin
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part A Author(s): Jie Ren, Guilin Han, Xi Gao, Shitong Zhang, Qian Zhang
abstract: Megacity rivers are crucial for urban sustainability, supporting water supply, flood control, and ecological services. This study investigated the hydrochemical evolution and driving factors of the Chaobai River basin, a representative megacity river in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region, and developed a Fuzzy Comprehensive Evaluation (FCE) framework for boundary-sensitive water-quality assessment under winter baseflow conditions. The framework integrates Random Forest (RF), Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP), and Entropy methods to construct a hybrid weighting scheme. Hydrochemical facies and ion-ratio diagnostics indicate a basin-scale downstream shift from carbonate-weathering control toward anthropogenic salinization and nutrient enrichment, evidenced by higher Ca2+/Na+ and Mg2+/Na+ ratios upstream (ANOVA, p < 0.01) and elevated Cl− signatures relative to background rivers (Mann-Whitney, p < 0.01). Comprehensive weighting highlighted Na+, Cl−, NO3 −, and K+ as primary water-quality indicators, consistent with cumulative inputs from urban effluents and agricultural sources. FCE results indicated that 83% of samples were classified within Grades I ∼ III, reflecting generally good water quality, whereas the membership-probability analysis showed a dominant tendency toward Grade III ∼ IV, suggesting emerging anthropogenic dominance. The RF-improved FCE framework refined indicator weighting by incorporating nonlinear statistical relationships and provided a more interpretable basis for water-quality classification. Compared with the Entropy-weighted Water Quality Index (EWQI), the FCE method better captured boundary-adjacent conditions and emerging anthropogenic influence that were not resolved by a single composite index. This approach provides a boundary-sensitive framework for linking hydrochemical patterns with water-quality classification in the Chaobai River basin and a methodological reference for regulated rivers under comparable settings.

title: Competitive adsorption and co-transport of live and hypochlorite-inactivated Azospirillum brasilense in saturated sand
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part A Author(s): Fengxian Chen, Zeev Ronen, Gilboa Arye
abstract: Azospirillum brasilense is widely applied in cereal production to enhance plant growth and stress tolerance, and its mobility in sandy soils is critical for successful root colonization. In irrigation systems, operational disinfection processes can unintentionally reduce bacterial viability, generating large fractions of inactivated cells that may coexist and interact with live cells during subsurface transport. Here, we investigated the physicochemical properties, adsorption behavior, and co-transport dynamics of live and hypochlorite-inactivated A. brasilense strains Sp7 and Cd in saturated sand. Inactivated cells exhibited slight reductions in cell size, increased hydrophobicity, and less negative surface charge, which together lowered the XDLVO interaction energy barrier and enhanced their affinity for sand surfaces. Adsorption isotherms showed clear competitive adsorption between live and inactivated cells, with inactivated cells exhibiting stronger overall attachment. Column transport experiments further revealed that live cells transported more rapidly and were recovered in greater proportions than inactivated cells, whereas inactivated cells showed stronger retention and lower detachment. In mixed systems, the presence of inactivated cells reduced the effective retention capacity available to live cells and altered their attachment behavior. The one-site and two-site attachment/detachment model with Langmuirian blocking successfully described the observed breakthrough curves and retention profiles. These results indicate that inactivated bacterial biomass is not inert but can influence bacterial retention and transport by competing for retention domains and modifying attachment dynamics. Accounting for viability-dependent changes in surface properties and competitive interactions may help improve predictions of beneficial bacterial mobility and delivery efficiency in sandy soils.

title: How emergent-constrained precipitation projections reshape watershed hydrology?
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part A Author(s): Yilan Li, Tongbi Tu, Xiaohong Chen
abstract: Intensifying climate change is expected to substantially reshape watershed hydrology, yet large discrepancies among global climate models (GCMs)—particularly in precipitation projections—remain a major obstacle to reliable runoff forecasting. Here, using the Xijiang River Basin as a testbed, we develop and apply a novel model-selection-based emergent constraint (EC) framework to constrain CMIP6 precipitation projections and reduce inter-model spread by identifying models that exhibit physically consistent historical–future relationships. The constrained projections are then integrated into a hybrid hydrological modeling framework to evaluate how reduced precipitation uncertainty propagates through watershed processes across multiple temporal scales. The EC increases projected precipitation growth rates by 7–84% relative to the raw CMIP6 ensemble while reducing their uncertainty by 6.8–15.2%. However, the corresponding reductions in hydrological uncertainty are comparatively modest: annual and monthly runoff uncertainties decrease by only 2.8–14.2% and 4.18–16.28%, respectively, and the uncertainty range of extreme floods expands by 1.81–22.55% in most scenarios. Across emission scenarios, hydrological responses consistently show enhanced wet-season runoff, reduced dry-season flows, and intensified extreme floods, suggesting a heightened risk of drought–flood alternation under future climate conditions. These results show that the model-selection-based emergent constraint framework effectively identifies GCMs suitable for regional projections, while also revealing that substantial reductions in precipitation uncertainty do not translate proportionally into improved hydrological predictability, reflecting the nonlinear and scale-dependent propagation of climate signals through watershed processes.

title: KURVE: A web-based tool for estimating soil water retention and hydraulic conductivity curves using a k -nearest neighbor approach
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part A Author(s): Amir Verdi
abstract: Direct measurement of the soil water retention curve (WRC) and hydraulic conductivity curve (HCC) is expensive and time-consuming. Pedotransfer functions (PTFs) are statistical models that estimate soil hydraulic properties using basic soil data that are typically available or easier to measure. This paper introduces KURVE, a novel web-based tool that uses a recently published HYPROP-WP4C-based German reference dataset and a k-nearest neighbor approach to estimate complete WRCs and HCCs. KURVE selects nearest soils from the reference dataset based on basic soil properties, including soil texture, bulk density (BD), and organic carbon content (OCC), and estimates target-soil hydraulic curves by averaging fitted van Genuchten (VG) and Peters–Durner–Iden (VG-PDI) hydraulic functions from the selected neighbors. The performance of KURVE was evaluated using two independent datasets, a large international dataset and a smaller regional dataset from California, USA, and was compared with the widely used Rosetta and Rosetta3 PTF models. KURVE showed promising performance for estimating both curves. For WRC prediction, KURVE achieved RMSE values as low as 0.061 cm3 cm⁻3 for the international dataset and 0.039 cm3 cm⁻3 for the California dataset, which was comparable to or slightly better than Rosetta-based models. For HCC prediction, KURVE substantially outperformed Rosetta-based models, with minimum log(K) RMSE values of 0.594 for the international dataset and 0.560 for the California dataset when soil texture and BD were used as inputs. The results also showed that adding BD to soil texture improved model performance, whereas adding OCC as an additional predictor did not provide consistent improvement. KURVE is freely available at kurve-ptf.streamlit.app and provides the scientific community with an accessible tool for applications that require soil hydraulic information.

title: Source identification of multi-process clogging in a deep groundwater recharge well: a combined mineralogical-geochemical approach
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part A Author(s): Yang Xu, Xinwang Li, Suying Ma, Yinhuan Fu, Xueyan Ye, Yalin Song, Xinqiang Du
abstract: Deep groundwater recharge wells are vulnerable to clogging, but field identification of the responsible solids is difficult because they may originate from recharge water, aquifer materials, well construction, corrosion, and hydrochemical reactions. This study characterized clogging-associated deposits and mobilized solids from a deep groundwater recharge well in the North China Plain using X-ray diffraction, X-ray fluorescence, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, water-quality analysis, and PHREEQC geochemical mixing simulations. Deposits on the galvanized pump pipe contained Zn-Fe corrosion phases, including hydrozincite, akaganeite, and hematite. Muddy and flange-associated deposits and solids discharged during air-lift rehabilitation contained quartz, feldspars, clay minerals, and Fe oxides, indicating the coexistence of mineral particles and corrosion-derived solids. Wellhead yellow foam was amorphous and multi-elemental but cannot represent in situ aquifer clogging deposits. Recharge water containing 8 mg/L total suspended solids introduced a gross external particle load of 611.2064 kg over 76,400.8 m3. Mineralogical overlap also indicated an internally available or previously deposited pool of mobilizable particles, although the relative contributions of external and internal sources could not be resolved. Geochemical modeling confirmed carbonate supersaturation under mixed recharge-native groundwater conditions. The results identify particle input and remobilization, well-material corrosion, and carbonate precipitation potential as coexisting clogging-related processes. Management should therefore combine particle-load control, improved well development, corrosion monitoring, and mixing-based geochemical assessment.

title: Estimating daily evapotranspiration from remotely sensed instantaneous observations with surface flux equilibrium (SFE) theory and maximum entropy production (MEP) principle
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part A Author(s): Xin Pan, Zhanchuan Wang, Jinlong Shi, Yuanbo Liu, Zi Yang, Xu Ding, Suyi Liu, Hongjun Zhu, Congbao Zhu, Shile Yang, Yingbao Yang
abstract: As the important component in the regional water and energy budget, territorial evapotranspiration (ET) can be derived from remote sensing with the help of temporal upscaling method. In this study, a temporal upscaling method was developed on basis of physics-based Surface Flux Equilibrium (SFE) Theory and Maximum Entropy Production (MEP) Principle. The proposed method eliminates the uncertainties derived from the empirical assumption of constant coefficients and the semi-empirical parameterization of resistances in traditional methods, and can be transferred to two conventional temporal upscaling method in some situations. Validated by ground observations at 80 globally distributed sites, the proposed method (only using ground observations) shows a satisfactory accuracy, especially in the situations of the medium aridity (RMSE: 16 W/m2), high vegetation coverage (RMSE: 20 W/m2) and low latitude (14 W/m2). Furthermore, the proposed method shows the best performance when only using remote sensing with a RMSE (R2) of 34 W/m2 (0.53). The proposed method also provides an optionally optimum simplification with a similar RMSE&RE and a relatively more significant underestimation (near to 25% of underestimation for only using remote sensing). It believed that the proposed method is helpful for the temporally upscaling (from remote sensed instantaneous ET to daily ET) in the producing of global daily or monthly ET products.

title: Hydrologic–anthropogenic mismatch modulates carbon–nutrient stoichiometric instability in an integrated agriculture–aquaculture watershed of southern China
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part A Author(s): Yezhao Cai, Nian She, Kairong Lin, Pengjun Li
abstract: Hydrologic volatility driven by climate change and intensified anthropogenic interference in subtropical integrated agriculture-aquaculture (IAA) watersheds have substantially disrupted riverine biogeochemical cycles, yet the dynamics of carbon-nutrient stoichiometry under seasonally contrasting hydroclimatic and land-use conditions remain insufficiently characterized. This study integrated seven years (2018–2024) of monthly in-stream hydrochemical monitoring across 20 subcatchments of the Neikeng River watershed, southern China, employing an exploratory five-tier analytical framework to examine dissolved organic carbon (DOC), total nitrogen (TN), total phosphorus (TP) concentrations, as well as their stoichiometric molar ratios. Results revealed pronounced seasonal stoichiometric imbalance. Dry-season baseflow conditions, coinciding with aquaculture pond drainage, induced co-occurring carbon-limitation, with approximately 70% of subcatchment observations falling below DOC:TN = 5 and 40% below DOC:TP = 20, while the wet seasons exhibited co-occurring nitrogen and phosphorus enrichment and pseudo nitrogen-limitation, with more than 90% of subcatchment observations falling below TN:TP = 20. PLS-PM modeling indicated that chemical indices, particularly TN, TP, and NH3-N, as well as land-use composition, primarily suppressed DOC:TN and DOC:TP molar ratios, while hydroclimatic factors appeared to regulate TN:TP stoichiometric shifts. Convergent multi-method evidence supported a working hypothesis of a seasonal source-sink inversion of aquaculture ponds, challenging the temporally invariant assumptions of current export coefficient models. Hydrologic–anthropogenic mismatch, rather than absolute carbon-nutrient loading, emerged as the primary structural correlate of stoichiometric instability. These findings provided a stoichiometrically grounded basis for the development of seasonally adaptive drainage management of rural watersheds, advocating ratio-based intervention strategies over conventional concentration-reduction approaches.

title: Assessing compound drought-heatwave events in Oman using non-stationary copula models
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part A Author(s): Malik Al-Wardy, Erfan Zarei, Mohammad Reza Nikoo, Maha Al-Balushi
abstract: Compound drought-heatwave (CDHW) events have severe ecological and socioeconomic consequences, particularly in Oman’s arid environments, where higher temperatures and increased aridity amplify their impacts. This study analyzes the frequency, duration, and severity of drought, heatwave, and CDHW events and the non-stationary joint probability of them in Oman using ERA5-Land data. Drought was measured using the Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI), and heatwaves were identified using relative temperature thresholds. Compound events were defined as coincident drought and heatwave events. Spatial trends were assessed using the Mann-Kendall test and the Theil-Sen slope estimator, and k-means clustering classified regions by hazard exposure. Non-stationary copula models (Gaussian and Clayton) were employed to analyze dependencies between heatwaves and drought, with model performance evaluated by ΔAkaike Information Criterion (AIC). Results show pronounced spatial patterns: the interior and west of Oman experienced the highest incidence of drought, while heatwaves dominated the northern coasts. CDHW events were most common in central-western and northern regions, with 2023–2024 being record-breaking in severity. Trend analysis indicated an increasing drought frequency but stationary heatwave trends, while copula modeling indicated stronger dependencies in coastal regions. The location–scale non-stationary model, incorporating both joint location and scale parameters, provided the best fit, highlighting the dynamic behavior of compound extremes. The joint probabilities were highest in the southern and eastern coastal regions (up to 87%), while dependency strength ranged from −41% to 58%. These findings point to Oman’s growing vulnerability to CDHW events, particularly in coastal and desert areas.

title: Enhanced chlorophyll- a concentration prediction in coastal waters using transformer networks with multivariate water quality parameters
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part A Author(s): Xiaoyao Sun, Lichen Xu, Jiayu Hong, Yijun Chen, Yuanyuan Wang, Hangjian Feng, Sensen Wu, Zhenhong Du
abstract: The accurate prediction of chlorophyll-a (Chl-a) concentrations in coastal waters is critical for mitigating the ecological and economic impacts of harmful algal blooms (HABs). Despite advancements in machine learning and deep learning methods, challenges remain in capturing the complex, time-varying dependencies of environmental factors and ensuring model interpretability. To address these gaps, we propose an innovative Transformer-based deep learning framework for Chl-a prediction using multiple exogenous variables, termed ExoCaT (Exogenous variable-integrated Chlorophyll-a prediction Transformer network), which integrates Variable Selection Networks (VSN) with a Hierarchical Encoder–Decoder (HED) architecture to enhance both forecasting accuracy and feature interpretability. The VSN offers insights into the temporal importance of environmental drivers and enables a better understanding of how key features influence Chl-a variability. To validate the proposed framework, ExoCaT is tested using data from two hydrological monitoring stations in the Ningbo and Zhoushan coastal areas. Compared to five state-of-the-art models in multistep-ahead predictive accuracy, our proposed model demonstrates substantial performance enhancements across both short-term and medium-term horizons, achieving a reduction of over 15% in the short-term prediction. Particularly under extreme bloom conditions, ExoCaT shows superior forecasting capability, effectively capturing Chl-a dynamics. Furthermore, interpretability analysis attests that electrical conductivity and water temperature are the most important factors for short-term prediction. By addressing the dual challenges of interpretability and temporal complexity, ExoCaT provides a useful operational tool for buoy-derived Chl-a prediction, supporting proactive decision-making in HABs management and marine conservation.

title: Enhanced data-based analysis introducing a previously unidentified empirical hydrological benchmark: baseflow dominance threshold
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part A Author(s): Yonca Cavus
abstract: Enhanced understanding of baseflow dynamics is critical for effective water resources management, especially in regions experiencing significant climatic variability. This study systematically investigates baseflow characteristics using an extensive daily streamflow dataset from 94 streamflow gauging stations across five climatically distinct river basins in Turkey. Employing the Recursive Digital Filter to separate baseflow, the study demonstrates that Baseflow Index (BFI) and streamflow have a unique relationship, where, from zero up to a given value of streamflow, BFI is unity, decaying exponentially afterward towards zero as streamflow increases. Significant variations were observed in the relationship between BFI and streamflow, reflecting local geomorphological and hydrological conditions, and clearly influenced by the presence or absence of zero-flow periods, and highlighting the importance of considering stream intermittency in hydrological analysis. However, the point where BFI starts to decay was found consistent over river basins, and this is the novel concept introduced as the Baseflow Dominance Threshold (BDT). The analysis revealed that this threshold exhibits a consistent normally distributed exceedance probability of approximately 0.05 basin-wide, underscoring a previously unidentified empirical hydrological benchmark.
