Another robust finding of the study is that streamflow is fully composed of baseflow in 20% of days on average consistently over the river basins studied. Extensive testing of probability distributions demonstrated that parametric approaches inadequately represent BFI variability, prompting the adoption of non-parametric methods. These methods revealed distinct hydrograph phase-specific differences, with recession limbs exhibiting higher and more stable baseflow contributions compared to ascension limbs. The findings emphasize the critical role of zero-flow conditions, seasonal variability, and regional hydrological characteristics in shaping baseflow dynamics. By providing a comprehensive, data-driven analysis framework and introducing the BDT, this study advances hydrological modelling practices and supports adaptive, informed water management strategies.

title: Beyond prediction accuracy: using differentiable hybrid models as a tool for hydrological knowledge discovery
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part A Author(s): Yuqian Hu, Wenhao Chu, Yuxuan Wang, Chunxiao Zhang, Rongrong Li, Heng Li, Yazhou Qi
abstract: Differentiable hybrid modelling has dramatically improved streamflow prediction, yet its potential as a tool for genuine scientific discovery remains largely untapped. This study introduces a closed “diagnosis-extraction-improvement” framework that repurposes differentiable hybrids to identify, correct, and theoretically advance structural deficiencies in traditional process-based hydrological models. Using a fully differentiable implementation of the widely used EXP-HYDRO model across 476 diverse CAMELS catchments, we report three primary findings: (1) Quantitative Diagnosis: Systematic replacement of individual process modules with neural surrogates quantitatively identified the temperature- and daylength-based Hamon potential evapotranspiration (PET) formulation as the dominant structural bottleneck at the continental scale, underscoring the limitations of temperature-only empirical approaches. (2) Knowledge Extraction: Symbolic regression successfully distilled the high-performing neural PET surrogate into a parsimonious analytical expression. This discovered equation, explicitly incorporating shortwave radiation and a nonlinear self-regulating term, recovered >85% of the predictive skill originally provided by the complex neural surrogate under both basin-specific and fully regionalised calibration strategies. (3) Theoretical Improvement: Reintegration of the discovered equation into the original EXP-HYDRO model fundamentally enhanced physical realism. The new formulation eliminated long-standing radiation-related systematic biases, substantially reduced long-term water balance errors, and restored consistency with the Budyko hypothesis across diverse hydroclimatic regimes. Importantly, these three findings form a framework that unlike previously reported improvements by (i) objectively ranking structural deficiencies, (ii) extracting an interpretable equation directly from constrained neural surrogates, and (iii) proving physical-bias elimination without compensation, a combination not previously achieved at continental scale. Collectively, these results demonstrate that differentiable hybrid systems combined with symbolic regression can serve as powerful tool for accelerating theory-guided discovery and systematic modernisation of hydrological process representations.

title: Stability of physical and hydraulic characteristics of biochar- and rockwool-based growing media under wetting and drying processes
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part A Author(s): Shahrokh Shahmansouri, Mohammad Reza Mosaddeghi, Hossein Shariatmadari, Jean Caron
abstract: Growing medium plays an important role in providing water, air, and mechanical support for plants in soilless culture. There is little information about the stability of physical and hydraulic characteristics of growth media in consecutive cultivations and wetting–drying (W/D) cycles. It is evident that superior substrates are those with characteristics remaining stable over time and reusable for several cultivation cycles. Therefore, this study was conducted to investigate the effects of W/D cycles on physical and hydraulic characteristics of 14 growing media including biochar- and rockwool-based substrates and Coir pith-Perlite (as reference). Ten W/D cycles were applied on the substrates, and subsidence, mass reduction, water retention, saturated hydraulic conductivity, and some physical indicators were monitored. The W/D cycles significantly changed the physical and hydraulic characteristics which were related to fragmentation of particles, alteration of particle/pore size distribution and particle arrangement, swelling/shrinking and subsidence. The W/D cycles increased the frequency of micropores and saturated water content (θ s, 0.694 → 0.742 cm3 cm⁻3). Besides, the W/D cycles had a positive effect on easily available water (EAW, 0.194 → 0.204 cm3 cm⁻3), water holding capacity (WHC, 0.603 → 0.615 cm3 cm⁻3), and air-filled porosity (AFP, 0.103 → 0.141 cm3 cm⁻3) in most substrates. However, the increase in pore tortuosity and micropores upon W/D cycles significantly decreased saturated hydraulic conductivity (K s, 121 → 65.7 cm h⁻1) in most substrates. Intensive/dynamic quantities (such as K s) are superior due to their importance in air/water relations and sensitivity to microstructure and pore size distribution. The increase of AFP and the decrease of residual water content showed that adsorbed water decreased due to the W/D cycles in most substrates. Water repellency (WDPT, 5.7 → 20.2 s) increased in most growing media upon W/D cycles, which could be due to the rearrangement of particles and decomposition of organic matter into hydrophobic particles. The properties of inorganic substrate RW(0.1)-Perlite (0.1 v/v rockwool and 0.9 v/v perlite) did not change after W/D cycles. Whereas the organic-based growing media altered greater upon the W/D cycles. Almost all substrates having biochar and rockwool showed comparable stability/suitability with Coir pith-Perlite. Our results would be valuable to recommend alternative stable substrates to greenhouse growers for long term use, provided the economic stands.

title: Tidal hydrology drives the spatial distribution of aphids and their herbivorous effects on the Suaeda salsa seeds in the saltmarshes of the Yellow River Delta
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part A Author(s): Dongdong Qiu, Yanpeng Zhu, Zhichao Xu, Baoshan Cui
abstract: Tidal hydrological intensity and connectivity affect the community structure and processes in many coastal ecosystems. However, reports of how tidal hydrology drives the spatial distribution of aphids and their herbivorous effects on saltmarsh plants in saltmarshes are lacking. We therefore conducted field investigations and field manipulation experiment to study the associations between tidal hydrology, aphids and the native key plants Suaeda salsa along land-sea gradient in the saltmarshes of the Yellow River Delta, China. The results of two investigations demonstrated that the extent of aphid infestation on S. salsa plants (including the aphid egg density per individual S. salsa plant and the aphid egg density per unit dry biomass of S. salsa) gradually lessened along land-sea gradient. The potential germination rate of S. salsa seeds, tidal erosion rate and soil moisture content progressively increased along the land-sea gradient. The extent of aphid infestation on S. salsa plants exhibited negative correlations with soil moisture content and tidal erosion rate, while the potential germination rate of S. salsa seeds showed positive correlations with those. The potential germination rate of S. salsa seeds was negatively correlated with the extent of aphid infestation on S. salsa plants. The results of manipulation experiment showed that the extent of aphid infestation on S. salsa plants was significantly higher in both the procedural control and aphids present treatments than in the aphids absent treatment. The potential germination rate of S. salsa seeds was significantly lower in both the procedural control and aphids present treatments than in the aphids absent treatment. Thus, the results demonstrated that the herbivory of aphids damaged the S. salsa seeds, and the stronger tidal hydrology could reduce seed damage by suppressing aphid infestation. This study provides empirical evidence supporting hydrological management as a strategy to enhance saltmarsh ecosystem resilience and promote vegetation restoration.

title: Forensic hydrological assessment of flood response under land use/land cover (LULC) change using ANN and HEC–HMS
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part A Author(s): Seyed-Mahdi Salar-Khorasani, Omid Bozorg-Haddad, Hugo A. Loaiciga
abstract: This study develops an integrative methodological framework that combines forensic hydrology, artificial neural networks (ANNs), and physically-based hydrological modeling to assess the cascading impacts of projected land use/land cover (LULC) changes on future flood dynamics in the upstream watershed of Golestan Dam, Iran. A large-magnitude flood event analogous to the destructive 2019 flood was simulated under evolving LULC scenarios for three future horizons: 2030, 2040, and 2050. The curve number (CN) and lag time (Tlag) were reconstructed using linear and nonlinear interpolation and projected with ANN-based regression modeling. Mann-Kendall trend analysis was applied to assess the temporal consistency of ANN-predicted CN and Tlag series and support the selection of the most reliable synthetic datasets. The simulations revealed highly non-linear growth in peak discharges, with the Qarah Shur sub-basin projected to experience a 163.78% increase in flood intensity by 2050, resulting from a substantial increase in the contribution of barren land to flood intensification (from 22.89% to 78.88%) and a threefold increase in the contribution of sparse vegetation (from 9.04% to 31.13%). These two factors, individually and in combination, were identified as the most critical contributors to flood amplification in this sub-basin. The Galikesh sub-basin followed with a 68.99% increase by 2050, being the only sub-basin where the contribution of road expansion (from 8.88% to 27.41%) emerged as the dominant factor driving flood intensification. The Tamar Gorgan and Tangerah sub-basins demonstrated more moderate increases in discharge, 13.89% and 10.44%, respectively, driven by modest land degradation and road building. This work’s findings underscore growing risks to infrastructure, including embankment instability, bridge scour, and urban inundation, and to groundwater recharge, aquatic ecosystems, and water quality through the mobilization of pollutants and sediments under increasing flood risk. The spatial comparison of sub-basin-level responses captures the heterogeneity of flood vulnerability and the urgency of instituting adaptive land use policies grounded in hydrological sensitivity, riparian corridor protection, and nature-based flood mitigation.

title: How to overcome hydrologic data scarcity in assessing potential groundwater risk to subterranean infrastructure: a finite-difference modelling approach
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part A Author(s): Nejat Zeydalinejad, Akbar A. Javadi, Mark Jacob, David Baldock, James L. Webber
abstract: Groundwater infiltration (GWI) in sewer networks is an increasing challenge under climate change and human pressures, threatening the sustainability of sewer infrastructure. However, data scarcity and complex hydrogeology complicate its risk assessment. This study develops a finite-difference groundwater flow model (MODFLOW) to identify GWI susceptibility hotspots in non-pressurised sewer networks in Dawlish, southwest United Kingdom. To address limited hydrological data and hard-rock hydrogeology, several transferable approaches were integrated into the modelling framework. Fracture flow was represented using a porous-medium approximation, while borehole logs were interpreted to define the bedrock surface and estimate hydraulic properties. Groundwater recharge was derived from land-cover data, missing river stages were estimated from discharge–stage relationships, and initial node heads were assigned from river-network connectivity and upstream–downstream positions. These inputs, together with hydraulic properties and recharge, were refined through calibration. The model was calibrated for October 2007 to September 2020 and validated over the following four years using monthly time steps, achieving a mean error of − 0.05 m, a mean absolute error of 0.94 m, and a root mean square error of 1.62 m. Then, sewer sections were classified as having high (groundwater level (GWL) above the sewer), intermediate (GWL within 2 m below the sewer), or low (GWL more than 2 m below the sewer) GWI susceptibility. More than 85% of storm overflow spills occurred in sewers classified as highly susceptible. The resulting hotspot maps provide a practical decision-support tool for prioritising sewer inspection, maintenance, and rehabilitation, supporting more sustainable sewer network management.

title: Quantifying hydrological responses to climate change and associated canopy variability using an integrated LSTM-SWAT modeling framework
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part A Author(s): Kunhao Jiang, Hui Ran, Xinyi Chen, Yingnan Wei, Yuanxin Dai, Qiang Yu, Hao Feng, Xiaotao Hu, Ning Yao
abstract: Climate change and climate-driven canopy variability jointly influence terrestrial hydrological processes, while their combined effects on individual water-balance components across complex terrains remain insufficiently quantified. This study integrated a modeling framework by coupling a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network with the Soil and Water Assessment Tool (SWAT) to assess scenario-based hydrological responses in the Weihe River Basin (WRB) through 2100. The LSTM model was employed to predict grid-level Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) trajectories under Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 scenarios, including Shared Socioeconomic Pathway 2–4.5 (SSP245) and Shared Socioeconomic Pathway 5–8.5 (SSP585). The predicted NDVI trajectories were then converted into Leaf Area Index (LAI) and incorporated into SWAT as seasonal canopy constraints. The LSTM-based approach reasonably represented climate-driven canopy variability (R2 > 0.90), projecting increasing canopy density under future climate scenarios, particularly under SSP585. Climate change was projected to intensify simulated hydrological fluxes. In the diagnostic climate-change perturbation scenarios, mean streamflow increased by 12.0% under SSP245 and 21.2% under SSP585, whereas the integrated climate-canopy scenarios moderated these increases to 10.7% and 19.4%, respectively, through enhanced evapotranspiration (ET). Terrain-dependent variations in hydrological sensitivity were identified. Specifically, plain regions exhibited stronger responses in surface runoff (SURQ) and groundwater flow (GWQ), plateau regions (PLT) demonstrated larger changes in water yield (WYLD), and mountainous regions (MTN) displayed more pronounced responses in lateral subsurface flow (LATQ). These findings provide scenario-based diagnostic evidence for assessing how climate-driven canopy variability may moderate hydrological responses in topographically diverse watersheds.

title: Advancing seasonal water supply forecasting for lakes and reservoirs using copulas
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part A Author(s): Alexander VanDeWeghe, Andrew D. Gronewold
abstract: The future of water storage dynamics in lakes around the world is increasingly uncertain due to a changing climate and evolving anthropogenic demands. Now, more than ever, it is necessary to quantify the uncertainty in forecasts of future water supply and water levels. However, classical ensemble forecasting systems that rely on weighted repetitions of historical water flux sequences, or independently resampled then post-processed sequences, often fail to capture either the dependence between hydrological variables across space and time or the full range of plausible outcomes for these variables. In this paper, an alternative statistical approach is outlined for using high-dimensional distributions described by copulas to generate water supply ensembles which preserve the correlation structure among hydrological variables. This new approach is outlined in detail to support dispersed operational modeling efforts, demonstrated by one implementation of a copula-based model for seasonal to annual forecasting on the Laurentian Great Lakes. This model implementation performs similar to or better than current operational forecasts while extending the forecast horizon from 6 to 12 months.

title: Increasingly diverse allochthonous input promote recalcitrance and homogenization of dissolved organic matter along the land-sea continuum
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part A Author(s): Liyin Qu, Mingxing Ren, Dezhong Wang, Ting Wang, Randy A. Dahlgren, Shengyao Sun, Jixin Chen, Xuwen Fang, Penghui Li, Weidong Guo
abstract: Estuaries are receiving increasingly diverse allochthonous dissolved organic matter (DOM) with variable reactivities as global change intensifies, yet the ultimate fate of this mixed-source DOM along the dynamic land-sea interface remains poorly constrained. Herein, we investigated spatiotemporal variability in DOM molecular composition along the Zhangjiang river-estuary-bay continuum, characterizing eight anthropogenic and wetland DOM endmembers. Dissolved organic carbon (DOC) and DOM chemodiversity increased along the continuum and peaked in the upper estuary across all hydrological periods. DOC addition from urban sewage, aquaculture effluent and mangrove creek runoff was comparable to riverine DOC input during the intermediate and dry seasons, whereas submarine groundwater discharge only contributed to elevated DOM chemodiversity. A thermodynamically-related biotransformation model further revealed that allochthonous aliphatics were stepwise transformed into recalcitrant islands of stability (IOS) molecules during seaward transport through successive dehydrogenation, denitrogenation and oxidation, with reactions shifting from thermodynamically favorable to increasingly constrained conditions. Nonetheless, over 70% of in situ produced RDOM molecules showed net removal along the estuary via adsorption/flocculation and sedimentation, potentially contributing to estuarine carbon burial. Ultimately, 26–56% of DOM molecules from different endmembers were removed during export, highlighting the estuary as a hotspot of carbon transformation and burial through efficient processing of diverse allochthonous DOM. These processes ultimately promoted homogenization of estuarine DOM pools. These findings provide mechanistic insights for predicting/constraining the carbon budgets of estuaries under ongoing environmental change.

title: Disentangling precipitation forcing and parameter uncertainty in a multi-objective surface–subsurface hydrologic modeling framework
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part A Author(s): Salam A. Abbas, Jeremy T. White, Ryan T. Bailey, Michael J. White, Natalja Čerkasova, Jeffrey G. Arnold
abstract: Precipitation forcing uncertainty can substantially influence parameter estimation and predictive performance in coupled surface–subsurface hydrologic models, yet practical strategies for explicitly representing this uncertainty during calibration remain limited. Here, precipitation forcing was parameterized to represent precipitation uncertainty and aspects of model misspecification, thereby reducing compensatory adjustment of hydrologic parameters during calibration. We constructed coupled surface–subsurface hydrologic models (SWAT+ gwflow) for two humid-region watersheds, the Winnebago River basin (Iowa, USA) and the Monocacy River basin (Maryland, USA), and employed the Iterative Ensemble Smoother (iES) for calibration using monthly mean streamflow and remotely sensed evapotranspiration (ET). Three calibration configurations were evaluated: streamflow-only, ET-only, and joint streamflow–ET calibration. Two precipitation parameterization schemes were evaluated: Precipitation-Variable (PV), where daily precipitation inputs were adjusted using time-varying precipitation multipliers, and Precipitation-Fixed (PF), where precipitation remained constant during calibration. In the Winnebago River basin, PV resulted in significant improvement in streamflow simulation during simultaneous streamflow–ET calibration, increasing NSE from 0.48 to 0.79 during calibration and from 0.25 to 0.81 during testing relative to PF, while also decreasing groundwater head bias at several monitoring wells. In contrast, the Monocacy River basin exhibited similarly strong streamflow performance under both PV and PF experiments, demonstrating that the benefits of precipitation parameterization were watershed-dependent rather than universal. Simulated ET performance showed only insignificant variation among PV and PF experiments in both watersheds, with R2 values generally near 0.90. Water-balance partitioning differed significantly between experiments, with PV notably decreasing simulated groundwater recharge in the Winnebago basin relative to PF, showing how precipitation forcing uncertainty influences coupled surface–subsurface hydrologic fluxes and affects parameter sensitivity patterns. The proposed framework extends precipitation-uncertainty analysis to coupled surface–subsurface hydrologic modeling, providing insight into how precipitation forcing uncertainty interacts with parameter estimation, sensitivity patterns, and water-balance partitioning across contrasting watershed settings, with implications for uncertainty-aware model calibration and interpretation.

title: Physics-guided urban flood modeling: spatial heterogeneity and diagnostic attribution via CMoE-HDAF
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part A Author(s): Shaoxu Zheng, Ziwu Fan, Xuan Huang, Guang Yang, Yipeng Liao, Yunfei Hong, Jingxiu Wu, Guoqing Liu, Chen Xie
abstract: Urban flood forecasting in high-density cities requires models that can represent complex hydrodynamic responses while remaining computationally efficient. Conventional hydrodynamic models provide detailed simulations but are often too time-consuming for rapid scenario screening or ensemble analysis. This study develops CMoE-HDAF, a physically structured surrogate modelling framework that integrates a Cluster-based Mixture-of-Experts architecture with a Hierarchical Dominance Attribution Framework for the Longgang River Basin in Shenzhen, China. A calibrated InfoWorks ICM model was used to generate simulation-based reference inundation data for 45 rainfall scenarios over 243,944 computational nodes. The CMoE component partitions the basin into 25 hydrological regimes using static terrain, pipe-network, and hydrographic attributes, and regime-specific expert models are trained to represent local rainfall–inundation relationships. HDAF organizes feature-level contributions into subsystem-level diagnostic indicators for Terrain, Pipe Network, and Hydrography, supporting multi-scale interpretation of terrain, drainage, and hydrographic controls on inundation response. Compared with hydrodynamic simulations, the surrogate achieved a Nash-Sutcliffe Efficiency of 0.9761 and reduced basin-wide inference time to 32 s. The attribution analysis further characterized how the relative influence of terrain, pipe-network, and hydrographic conditions varied across rainfall scenarios and hydrological regimes. Overall, CMoE-HDAF provides a calibrated-model emulator and diagnostic attribution tool for rapid analysis and spatially structured interpretation of heterogeneous urban inundation responses.

title: Environmental and physiological regulation of evapotranspiration key parameters and subsequent modeling in a rain-fed maize field, Northeast China
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part A Author(s): Rongxuan Bao, Haofang Yan, Jianyun Zhang, Guoqing Wang, Chuan Zhang, Desheng Zhang, Yudong Zhou, Biyu Wang, Yujing Han, Youwei Liu, Xuanxuan Wang, Rui Zhou
abstract: Accurate estimation of crop evapotranspiration (ETc ) is crucial for yield prediction, irrigation management, and agricultural water resource assessment. A major challenge in applying widely used models such as the Penman-Monteith (PM), Priestley-Taylor (PT), and crop coefficient (Kc) models is the reliable calibration of key parameters, including canopy resistance (rc ), Priestley-Taylor coefficient (α), and crop coefficient (Kc ), under complex environmental and physiological dynamics. In this study, we evaluated the three models in a rain-fed maize field in Northeast China using meteorological data from 2020 to 2023, with a focus on the seasonal variations of rc , α, and Kc and their environmental and physiological drivers. The results indicated that daily α and Kc exhibited similar temporal patterns and were both linearly correlated with air temperature (Ta ) and relative humidity (RH). In contrast, rc showed a significant exponential correlation with net radiation (Rn ) and RH, and the curvature of the relationship between rc and Rn increased with increasing RH. All three parameters were linearly correlated with leaf area index (LAI), but these correlations weakened significantly when LAI > 3 m2·m−2. Filtering out days influenced by strong advection effectively eliminated most extreme values of rc , α, and Kc , thereby substantially improving the robustness of parameter calibration and model evaluation. Among the tested models, the Kc model performed best (average R 2 = 0.76, NSE = 0.74, MAE = 0.48 mm·d−1, RMSE = 0.68 mm·d−1), whereas the PT model exhibited the poorest performance (R 2 = 0.76, NSE = 0.52, MAE = 0.56 mm·d−1, RMSE = 0.77 mm·d−1). The performance of the three models was relatively high when LAI > 3 m2·m−2, and generally improved with increasing RH and Ta .In particular, LAI = 3 m2·m−2 was identified as a critical structural threshold marking the physical transition from soil-dominated to canopy-dominated evapotranspiration. These findings provide a rigorous basis for improving ETc estimation in rain-fed agroecosystems and informing the refinement of land surface models under diverse climatic conditions.

title: Climate network-based synchronized structural identification of extreme drought and pluvial events in cross-basin regions
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Wenyu Li, Jun Xie, Juan Cao, Kaiwen Li, Kai Liu, Ming Wang
abstract: Global warming has intensified the frequency and intensity of synchronous climate extremes, posing severe threats to the water‒food‒energy‒ecosystem nexus and challenging regional sustainability. In previous studies, scholars have often overlooked the inverse symbiotic relationship between drought and pluvial events and the complex, nonlinear spatiotemporal correlations underlying transregional climate extremes. Here, by using a complex network, we systematically identify the synchronous structure of drought, pluvial, and drought–pluvial dipole (DPD) events along the western route of the South-to-North Water Diversion Project in China. Our analysis reveals a distinct wet‒dry co-variability between the Yangtze and Yellow River Basins and elucidates the physical coupling between extreme hydroclimatic events and circulation anomalies, as well as the moisture transport pathways. Remote coupling zones of DPD events are identified alongside a pronounced spatial asymmetry in cross-basin hydroclimatic behavior. Compared with DPD events, which exhibit robust cross-basin teleconnections, drought and pluvial synchronicity are predominantly characterized by short-to-medium spatial scales. Notably, the signal sources for these extremes are anchored in the southwestern portion of the study area. We show that positive geopotential height anomalies, airflow subsidence, and monsoon disruption drive drought conditions, whereas the transport of warm, moist air generates pluvial events, together forming a “drought‒pluvial seesaw” at the climatic scale. Our findings offer valuable insights into adaptive strategies for cross-basin water resource management and pluvial–drought risk assessment.

title: AIFL: A global daily streamflow forecasting model using deterministic an LSTM pre-trained on ERA5-Land and fine-tuned on IFS
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Maria Luisa Taccari, Kenza Tazi, Oisín M. Morrison, Andreas Grafberger, Juan Colonese, Corentin Carton de Wiart, Christel Prudhomme, Cinzia Mazzetti, Matthew Chantry, Florian Pappenberger
abstract: Reliable global streamflow forecasting is essential for flood preparedness and water resource management, yet data-driven models often suffer from a performance gap when transitioning from historical reanalysis to operational forecast products. This paper introduces AIFL (Artificial Intelligence for Floods), a deterministic LSTM-based model designed for global daily streamflow forecasting. Trained on 18,588 basins curated from the Caravan dataset, AIFL utilises a two-stage transfer-learning strategy to bridge the reanalysis-to-forecast domain shift. The model is first pre-trained on 40 years of ERA5-Land reanalysis (1980–2019) to capture robust hydrological processes, then fine-tuned on operational Integrated Forecasting System (IFS) forecasts (2016–2019) to adapt to the specific error structures and biases of operational numerical weather prediction. Ablation experiments confirm that this two-stage approach outperforms both a naive IFS-only baseline and a mixed-forcing single-stage alternative. To our knowledge, this is the first global model trained end-to-end within the Caravan ecosystem. On an independent temporal test set (2021–2024), AIFL achieves high predictive skill with a median modified Kling–Gupta Efficiency ( KGE ′ ) of 0.66 and a median Nash–Sutcliffe Efficiency (NSE) of 0.53. Benchmarking results show that AIFL achieves comparable accuracy to current state-of-the-art global systems. The model provides a streamlined and operationally robust baseline for the global hydrological community.

title: IrriTwin: Integrating reinforcement learning with soil water and crop models toward digital-twin-oriented irrigation scheduling
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Menghua Xu, Xiujuan Wang, Mengzhen Kang, Fangle Chang, Jing Hua, Haoyu Wang, Philippe de Reffye
abstract: Improving agricultural water-use efficiency under increasing water scarcity is a central challenge for sustainable agriculture. However, intelligent irrigation control is constrained by the high cost of trial-and-error interaction in real fields, while purely reinforcement-learning-based approaches have limited ability to explicitly represent soil water dynamics and crop physiological processes. To address these limitations, this study proposes IrriTwin, a digital-twin-oriented irrigation scheduling framework that couples the Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) algorithm with a soil water model and the GreenLab crop growth model, thereby establishing a model-in-the-loop virtual soil–crop–water environment for policy learning under water resource constraints. Experimental results show that, under the same total irrigation amount, the SAC-based strategy achieves higher fruit biomass than baseline methods. The learned policy exhibits dynamic adaptability to soil moisture conditions and crop phenological stages, effectively balancing vegetative growth and reproductive demands. Additional comparisons with reinforcement learning baselines further indicate that the proposed dual-action SAC achieves more stable convergence and higher final returns in the representative maize case. Stability analysis further shows that the strategy remains effective under simulated rainfall and irrigation-failure disturbances. Experiments on sunflower and maize demonstrate the effectiveness of IrriTwin. These results indicate that integrating reinforcement learning with mechanistic soil–crop–water models provides a promising foundation for digital-twin-enabled, precise, and water-efficient irrigation management.

title: Characterizing water quality responses to connectivity frequency and flow magnitude in a regulated river–lake system
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Su Yang, Guishan Yang, Rongrong Wan, Xijun Lai, Luhua Gu, Bing Li, Hengpeng Li, Chen Xu
abstract: The construction of large-scale hydraulic projects has disrupted hydrological connectivity between rivers and lakes, directly affecting water quality and posing profound risks to water security. However, the quantitative understanding of how different modes of connectivity affect water quality in the sluice-controlled river network area remains limited. In this paper, we proposed a novel scenario-based framework to assess the water quality responses to connectivity from the dual perspectives of temporal frequency and flow magnitude, which is regulated by hydraulic facilities’ operation. Regional water quality was simulated under a series of connectivity frequency scenarios using connectivity–water quality response formulas. Meanwhile, the water quality of major rivers under varying discharge conditions was evaluated by the hydrodynamic–water quality model. Results indicate that continuous operation of recession and regulating sluices, together with extending the nonflood operation of pumping stations to 3–41 days, significantly reduces TP, TN, NH3-N, and CODMn concentrations by 1% to 4%. Besides, increasing inflow discharge results in moderate improvements in water quality, with a discharge of 50 m3/s reducing the mean TN concentration by approximately 1.4 mg/L compared with baseline conditions. Maintaining stable low-flow discharge at outflow sluices prevents prolonged stagnation and supports overall nutrient export. These findings demonstrate that water quality changes in regulated river–lake networks are jointly governed by connectivity timing and flow intensity, providing an analytical framework for adaptive water management in urbanized plain river networks.

title: Responses of soil physicochemical properties to land preparation measures revealed by fractal parameters of soil particle size distribution: effectiveness and limitations
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Zhuo Tian, Kangye Deng, Qinxue Xu, Xin Jin, Shuaipu Zhang
abstract: Rocky desertification slopes are characterized by shallow soil layers and limited water and nutrient storage, which severely restrict plant growth. The construction of reverse slopes (RS) and flat terraces (FT) can alter the redistribution processes of soil particles by modifying surface microtopography, thereby improving soil moisture and nutrient conditions. However, the application of RS and FT on rocky desertification slopes remains limited. Moreover, the critical role of soil particle redistribution in regulating soil physicochemical properties has not yet been fully elucidated. Therefore, RS and FT were innovatively constructed on rocky desertification slopes in this study, and fractal parameters of soil particle size distribution (SPSD) were employed to reveal the responses of soil hydraulic properties and nutrient contents to different land preparation measures. Results demonstrated that SPSD under different land preparation measures were predominantly concentrated within the range of 0.07–93.95 μm, accounting for 92.75% of the total particle distribution. RS exhibited the highest values of symmetry degree Δf, capacity dimension D(0), information dimension D(1), correlation dimension D(2), and D(1)/D(0), reaching 0.64, 0.95, 0.92, 0.90, and 0.96, respectively. The construction of RS simultaneously improved soil hydraulic properties and nutrient conditions on rocky desertification slopes, and their coupled regulation processes revealed the underlying mechanisms governing changes in soil hydraulic properties and nutrient dynamics. Among them, the construction of RS produced the most pronounced improvements in soil saturated hydraulic conductivity (Ks) and organic matter (OM). Relative to natural slopes (NS), Ks and OM under RS increased by 330.43% and 94.85%, respectively. Fractal parameters are important indicators for characterizing SPSD and can reflect soil physicochemical properties to a certain extent. However, soil properties are simultaneously influenced by external environmental conditions, internal pore structures and biogeochemical processes, resulting in inherent limitations when fractal parameters are used alone to characterize soil properties. This study highlights the effectiveness and limitations of fractal parameters in revealing soil physicochemical properties, while providing scientific guidance for sustainable cultivation and ecological management on rocky desertification slopes.

title: Effect of landslide location on glacial lake outburst flood at Badongcuo, Tibetan Himalaya
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Yangli Zhou, Shuai Zhang, Cong Dai, Chenxu Su, Yunhong Lv, Martin Mergili, Ashim Sattar, Limin Zhang
abstract: The current highest glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs) risk level is centered in the eastern Himalaya. Climate change-driven glaciers retreating and glacial lakes expanding will continue enhancing such GLOFs, which represent a serious threat to downstream inhabitants and ecological environment. This study evaluates such hazards of Lake Badongcuo located in the southeastern Tibetan Plateau. Drawing upon field investigations, 3D unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) modeling, and satellite images, we model a series of scenarios. These scenarios assume three hazard levels (high, moderate and low) and two potential landslides plunging into the lake, generating impulse waves, triggering dam-breach erosion, then resulting outburst floods that propagate downstream along the flow channel. Field evidence of seepage in the terminal moraine dam prompted us to consider the combined effects of piping and overtopping in breach formation. A multi-phase depth-averaged model was employed to simulate the entire GLOF process chain. Particular attention is given to the hydraulics of flood propagation at six downstream locations, including the planned Luolong Station of the Sichuan-Tibet Railway. For the high- and moderate-magnitude GLOF events, the maximum modeled breach outflow peak reaches 87,345 m3 s−1, the inundation can affect downstream up to 16 km from the lake, and the earliest flood arrival time is about 44 min at the Luolong Station. The low-magnitude GLOFs, though the more frequent type, have limited volume and peak discharge, causing less impact downstream. Further discussion reveals that the dynamics of impulse waves by landslides are pivotal to the GLOF process. The landslide entry position, water depth, and lakebed morphology are important factors governing GLOF intensity. Therefore, the proposed comprehensive methodology offers valuable support for local governments and hazard-management authorities in GLOF-prone regions to develop hazard magnitude-based mitigation measures and emergency response plans, thereby substantially reducing potential loss of life and infrastructure damage. Moreover, our findings can assist GLOF researchers to increase their understanding of key challenges they are facing regarding GLOF mechanisms.

title: Intensifying negative asymmetry in gross primary productivity response to precipitation anomalies across the Northern Hemisphere: evidence and drivers
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Jiaxuan Chen, Zongsen Wang, Zijun Wang, Yangyang Liu, Tingyi Xue, Zhongming Wen, Haijing Shi, Zhenqian Wang, Ercha Hu, Stephen Sitch, Wenping Yuan
abstract: Asymmetry index of Gross Primary Productivity (GPPAI) is a key metric characterizing the asymmetric response of ecosystem productivity to precipitation anomalies, defined as the difference between Gross Primary Productivity (GPP) increase in wet years and GPP decrease in drought years. Investigating the spatiotemporal patterns of GPPAI and its response to environmental changes deepens our understanding of ecosystem carbon cycle processes. This study integrated multi-source remote sensing data (1982–2018), TRENDY dynamic global vegetation model outputs, and CMIP6 future scenario simulations (2015–2100) to systematically examine the spatiotemporal characteristics and driving mechanisms of asymmetric GPP responses to precipitation anomalies across the Northern Hemisphere. The results indicate: (1) Negative asymmetry (GPP reduction in drought years exceeding GPP increase in wet years) prevailed in 75.71% of the Northern Hemisphere. During 1982–2018, the overall GPPAI declined significantly at a rate of –3.68 × 10−3 year−1 with the most rapid decreases observed in semi-arid regions (slope = –3.59 × 10−3year−1) and grasslands (slope = –3.77 × 10−3year−1) based on multi-source remote sensing data. (2) Multi-factor attribution analysis using dynamic vegetation models revealed that climate change, CO2, and land-use change contributed 58.99%, 34.89%, and 6.11% to GPPAI variations, respectively, with climate change being the dominant driver. Random Forest attribution analysis showed that increased radiation, precipitation, temperature, vapor pressure deficit (VPD), and decreased wind speed all positively contributed to GPPAI changes. Temperature and precipitation were identified as primary drivers, while VPD played a relatively minor role. PCMCI causal analysis indicated that precipitation directly influenced GPPAI in humid and shrubland regions but exerted indirect effects in semi-arid and forest areas. Temperature impacts were region-specific, indirectly regulating GPPAI through other climate factors in forest and shrubland ecosystems. (3) High-emission scenarios (SSP3-7.0 and SSP5-8.5) exhibited higher mean GPPAI values than low-emission scenarios (SSP1-2.6 and SSP2-4.5), primarily reflecting stronger modeled CO2 fertilization effects. However, this does not necessarily indicate enhanced ecosystem resilience, as asymmetry trends continued to decline more rapidly under high-emission pathways.

title: Evaluating the impact of climate change on water supply system reliability – a robust assessment framework using stochastic data
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Zitian Gao, David E. Robertson, Tze Ling Ng, Patrick Russell, Francis H.S. Chiew, John Frdelja
abstract: This study presents a stochastic data-based framework that enables dynamic and uncertainty-aware evaluation of water supply system performance under climate change and climate variability, and supports the determination of optimal timing for system augmentation. Stochastic climate data were generated for 12 sensitivity scenarios with varying projected trends in rainfall, temperature and evaporation. The sensitivity analysis enables evaluation of system performance across a wide range of climate conditions, supporting robust decision-making to ensure system reliability under diverse future pathways. Stochastic runoff was generated from stochastic climate data, and both were used in a case-study water supply system model. Results showed that the water supply system became less reliable under two different climate pathways: 1) a large increase in evaporation and temperature (8 % and 2 °C) coupled with a moderate decrease in rainfall (5 %), and 2) a substantial decrease in rainfall (10 % or 15 %). Under these pathways, system restrictions and shortfalls increased rapidly over time, and the system became more expensive to operate due to increased reliance on groundwater and the need to draw water from a reservoir that may have quality issues. Under an extremely hot and dry climate scenario, the proposed augmentation, framed as a 20 % reduction in annual demand, helped to alleviate system restrictions, and early augmentation was more effective than late augmentation. The modelling and assessment approach presented here is transferable to different water supply systems, providing a valuable tool for understanding current and future system performance and evaluating probabilistic risk-reward trade-offs of system augmentation.

title: Hydrology-driven transport-storage dynamics, metals interaction, and ecological risk of downstream riverine microplastics
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Sarbanee Mahapatra, Jyoti Prakash Maity, Gobinda Dey, Tanisha Mishra, Shuvendu Singha, Alok Chandra Samal, Sourasis Chattopadhyay, Sutanu Mangal, Prosun Bhattacharya
abstract: The occurrence of microplastics (MPs) in monsoon-dominated rivers is influenced not only by the source inputs but also by seasonal hydrological shifts that regulate their transport to storage in downstream regions of the riverine system. The present study investigated MPs in surface water and bed sediments of the downstream riverine system during the pre-monsoon, monsoon, and post-monsoon periods to determine how discharge influences abundance, sediment–water partitioning, polymer-density sorting, metal association, and screening-level ecological risk. The results showed that MPs in surface water followed the order: monsoon (1169.8 ± 68.81 items/m3) > pre-monsoon (951.9 ± 45.42 items/m3) > post-monsoon (598.4 ± 69.42 items/m3), indicating enhanced runoff-driven mobilization and downstream transport under high-discharge conditions. In contrast, sediment MPs showed the trend: post-monsoon (1251.5 ± 32.04 items/kg) > pre-monsoon (976.1 ± 30.67 items/kg) > monsoon (971.9 ± 36.09 items/kg), reflecting a transition from monsoon-driven export to post-monsoon depositional storage. This pattern was further supported by the sediment–water enrichment index, which increased from 0.83 in the monsoon to 2.09 in the post-monsoon, confirming greater sedimentary retention under reduced hydrodynamic forcing. White/transparent particles, fragments, and fibres dominated both matrices, indicating mainly secondary and weathered MPs. Raman analysis identified polymers in the order PP > PE > PET > PS > PVC, and showed density-driven sorting between water and sediment. FESEM–EDX revealed weathered surfaces and associated potentially toxic elements, suggesting that MPs may act as carriers of co-contaminants. This findings highlight that monsoon hydrology strongly regulates MPs transport, storage, and ecological risk in tropical river systems.

title: Synthetic DNA fragments enable improved characterization of specific storage heterogeneity through multi-source data fusion
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Xinlin Li, Zhaofei Duan, Xiaoting Xie, Jirka Šimůnek, Renkuan Liao
abstract: Characterizing the spatial heterogeneity of aquifer specific storage (Ss) at high resolution remains a major challenge in subsurface hydrology. This study developed a novel precision-weighted fusion framework that combines hydraulic conductivity (K) estimates obtained from steady-state hydraulic tomography (SSHT) and synthetic DNA tracer tomography (TT), along with diffusivity (D) estimates generated from travel-time hydraulic tomography (TTHT), to enable high-resolution characterization of Ss through the decoupled relationship Ss = K/D. The framework was further evaluated through controlled laboratory sandbox experiments with known layered heterogeneity, comparing homogeneous (same-source) and heterogeneous (cross-source) fusion scenarios. Results demonstrated that the heterogeneous fusion of structurally independent data sources (pressure-field hydraulic tomography and tracer ray-path tomography) is critical for accurate Ss characterization. Uncertainty analysis revealed that, relative to the individual tracer arrays, homogeneous fusion reduced the mean K-field uncertainty σ(ln K) by 29.6%, whereas heterogeneous fusion reduced it by 44.0%; the corresponding reductions in Ss uncertainty σ(ln Ss) were 11.5% and 15.9%, respectively. Synthetic DNA tracers, whose virtually unlimited unique sequences enable simultaneous multi-array tomographic surveys without cross-interference using qPCR detection, proved particularly effective in this framework. The synthetic DNA-based heterogeneous fusion achieved improved predictive accuracy (R 2 = 0.81, MAE = 0.54 cm) compared to dye-based fusion (R 2 = 0.71, MAE = 0.57 cm), preserving stronger structural fidelity throughout the fusion chain. The findings offer the potential for high-resolution characterization of the spatial and temporal characteristics of aquifer specific storage, providing a prerequisite for accurate prediction and effective management of groundwater.

title: Preserving forecast accuracy with reduced ensemble size: A framework for optimal ensemble selection
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Kalakuntla Nikhil Teja, N.V. Umamahesh
abstract: The utilization of Ensemble Prediction Systems (EPS) from multiple Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) models for hydro-meteorological analyses, can significantly increase computational requirements. The quest for optimal ensemble size while maintaining comparable accuracy as a full ensemble has been an ongoing area of investigation. In this study, conducted over the Godavari River Basin in India, ensemble precipitation forecasts from the ECMWF and NCEP EPS available in the THORPEX Interactive Grand Global Ensemble (TIGGE) archive for the period 2006–2020 are utilized, while IMD gridded precipitation data for the same period are used as reference observations. The precipitation EPS data are combined into a Grand Ensemble (GE) to evaluate the optimal ensemble size. This was achieved by creating subsets of this GE, also called reduced ensemble sets, using various selection criteria such as correlation, Kling-Gupta Efficiency (KGE), and Probability of Detection (POD) for both 1 mm and 10 mm thresholds. Subsequently, the reduced ensemble sets are post-processed for bias and dispersion correction using the Quantile Regression Forests (QRF) machine-learning model. The results indicate that post-processing effectively achieves the same level of forecast accuracy as the full ensemble but with fewer ensemble members. Spatial plots and boxplots are generated to analyse the results in order to identify the optimal ensemble size. The analysis demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed framework in identifying reduced ensemble subsets that preserve forecast accuracy while significantly reducing computational cost. The results further indicate that the choice of selection criteria does not substantially influence the optimal ensemble size. The proposed framework is transferable across river basins, alleviating computational burden without compromising predictive performance.

title: Introducing IQR–DEMO for precipitation network design optimization
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Assefa Hayelom Hailu, Paulin Coulibaly
abstract: This study introduces an integrated Information Quality Ratio (IQR) and Dual Entropy Multiobjective Optimization (DEMO) framework for optimizing precipitation network design. In the proposed IQR–DEMO framework, IQR analysis is directly embedded within the DEMO algorithm. Although entropy-based methods such as DEMO effectively maximize information content and minimize redundancy among selected stations, they often overlook spatial imbalances across the basin and generate a large set of non-dominated solutions that can hinder practical decision-making. IQR, which quantifies station redundancy within a network, has been used as a post-design evaluation method, thereby limiting its influence on the optimization itself. To address this gap, the proposed framework incorporates IQR as a spatial penalty during the evolutionary search. For each candidate solution, an IQR analysis is performed, and the resulting values are interpolated over a high-resolution grid. The fraction of the basin falling outside a predefined IQR range is then used to penalize spatially imbalanced configurations through the objectives. This integration guides the algorithm toward network layouts that are both information-rich and spatially representative of the entire basin. The framework is demonstrated using three contrasting case studies, and the results show that the IQR–DEMO generally improves spatial coverage, reduces clustering of stations, and enhances basin-wide information quality. Sensitivity analyses further highlight how variations in the upper IQR threshold and penalty coefficient can influence network spatial coverage. Overall, the proposed approach offers a practical, adaptive, and spatially sensitive tool for designing efficient and spatially representative precipitation monitoring networks.

title: Hydrogeochemical dynamics of boron associated with groundwater discharge in river and lake basins
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Shen Qu, Lijuan Hu, Wei Bao, Le Qiao, Chuntao Zhao, Wengeng Cao, Limin Duan, Xiaomin Liu, Ruihong Yu
abstract: Boron (B) is a trace element widely distributed in nature and actively participates in biogeochemical cycles in aquatic systems. However, the mechanisms governing B enrichment and migration associated with groundwater discharge across different basin types remain insufficiently understood. In this study, a hybrid isotopic approach integrating multiple isotopic tracers (D, 18O, 11B, and 222Rn) with quantitative models was used to elucidate and quantify the sources and transport dynamics of B in the Bahannao Lake Group Basin (BLGB) and the Xiliugou River Basin (XRB) in Inner Mongolia, China. The results indicated that the average B concentration in surface water of the BLGB (4.03 mg/L) was substantially higher than that in the XRB (0.64 mg/L). In the BLGB, B enrichment was jointly regulated by relatively balanced contributions from natural processes (evaporation, mineral dissolution, and desorption) and anthropogenic inputs. In contrast, B enrichment in the XRB was predominantly driven by anthropogenic inputs. Moreover, lacustrine groundwater discharge (LGD) and riverine groundwater discharge (RGD) exerted a potential influence on B enrichment in both systems. The B flux associated with groundwater discharge in the BLGB (3.83 × 104 g/d) was markedly higher than that in the XRB (1.47 × 104 g/d). This study elucidates the different mechanisms underlying B enrichment in lake and river basins and provides a scientific basis for B risk management in similar regions.

title: The application of geospatially-integrated machine learning models for flood prediction: A review
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Christopher Atta Amponsah, Barnali Dixon, Yi Qiang, Eugene Y. Yan
abstract: With the increase in flooding events globally, Artificial Intelligence (AI) approaches, particularly geospatially integrated machine learning (ML), have emerged as a viable tool for flood modeling. This review systematically analyzed 100 peer-reviewed articles published between 1990 and 2024 to examine trends in ML applications across different flood types, their performance, opportunities, and limitations, and to identify gaps between research activity and flood occurrence, highlighting the need for capacity building in some regions. Results show that ML models are most frequently applied to pluvial floods (44%), followed by fluvial (40%), compound (9%), and coastal (7%) floods, while applications for pluvial, coastal, and compound flooding continue to increase. ANN-based models were the most commonly applied approaches, particularly in fluvial and compound flood studies, followed by SVM and RF models. Reported model performance varied substantially across studies depending on flood type, data availability, and validation strategy, with several localized studies reporting very high predictive accuracy under controlled validation conditions. The geographical distribution of 2,395 flood occurrences from the EM-DAT database revealed disparities between research output and flood occurrence. Publications align relatively well with Asia (50% of publications; 1,450 flood events), Europe (22%; 336 events), and North America (17%; 207 events), whereas Africa (5%; 97 events) and South America (5%; 244 events) remain underrepresented despite significant flood exposure. These findings highlight the need for improved data access, capacity building, and transferable ML approaches to support flood prediction research in underrepresented but flood-prone regions.

title: Sustainable water management in an upstream watershed under transboundary eco-compensation policy: a bi-level robust optimization model
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Linhuan He, Yee Van Fan, Yuhong Shuai, Liming Yao, Petar Sabev Varbanov, Ting Pan
abstract: Transboundary water pollution poses persistent challenges for river basin sustainability due to spatial externalities and mismatched environmental responsibilities between upstream and downstream regions. This study develops an allocation and trading framework for wastewater emission permits (WEPs) in the upstream watershed by integrating a cross-provincial watershed eco-compensation scheme (CpWES). A bi-level robust optimization model with uncertain parameters is established, in which the Bureau of Ecology and Environment as the upper-level seeks to maximize eco-economic benefits under uncertainty, while lower-level governments allocate WEPs across sectors to optimize local environmental-economic benefits. The model is applied to the Xin’an River Basin, and the results show that: (1) The eco-compensation policy exhibits an inverted U-shaped impact on the upstream economic benefits, suggesting the need for moderately calibrated compensation levels; (2) Huizhou County exhibits the highest emission reduction potential, with an annual load reduction of up to 394 tons; and (3) Under hydrological uncertainty, urban and industrial sectors achieve 4.5%-11.7% and 10%-16% annual reductions in pollutant loads, respectively, contributing to improved compliance with basin water quality targets. Overall, breaking administrative barriers and establishing basin-wide emission trading mechanisms can markedly enhance the sustainable development in upstream regions of transboundary river basins, providing practical support for upstream water pollution management under cross-provincial eco-compensation policies.

title: Quantifying the contributions of moisture recycling to precipitation in the monsoon transition zone: Insights from stable isotope data
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Cong Xie, Liangju Zhao, Ninglian Wang, Keke Ma, Yuye Qin, Weiwen Yi, Yue Lu
abstract: Quantifying the moisture recycling ratio derived from surface evaporation and plant transpiration to local precipitation is critical for understanding hydrological processes and land–atmosphere interactions in a changing climate, particularly in the Asian summer monsoon transition zone with complex moisture sources. This study employed a Bayesian three-component isotopic mixing model, combined with stable hydrogen and oxygen isotope data from precipitation and surface water at six sites in the north of the Qinling Mountains during 2020 to 2024, and the simulation data from Isotope-incorporated Global Spectral Model to quantify seasonal variations in the moisture recycling ratio from March to November. Results demonstrate that advected vapor serves as the dominant source of precipitation, with the mean moisture recycling ratio ranging between 32.9% and 40.5%, equivalent to 173.86 to 299.40 mm of local annual precipitation. During the monsoon season (June to October), the ratio varied from 32.5% to 36.0%, compared to 26.5% to 41.5% during the non-monsoon season. Spatially, the recycling ratio exhibited a distinct increasing gradient eastward reflecting the influence of the summer monsoon gradually weakening as it transports from east to west. The proportional contributions from transpiration (21.8 to 29.8%) consistently surpassed those from surface evaporation (7.8% to 13.4%), with the latter showing significantly lower values in summer than in spring and autumn. Temperature emerged as the primary driver of moisture recycling during the monsoon season, while vapor pressure deficit dominated during the non-monsoon period. These findings highlight the importance of recycled moisture to precipitation across the monsoon transition zone and reveal systematic spatiotemporal variations shaped by diverse moisture sources, providing crucial insights for understanding regional hydrological processes.

title: Pore-scale quantification of interfacial mixing and reaction during radial injection in porous media
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Zhipeng Du, Kaiyu Shi, Haixu Duan, Xianghua Yan, Xingrun Wang, Jiajun Chen
abstract: Understanding pore-scale mixing and reaction during radial injection is essential for evaluating the efficiency of in situ remediation processes. However, the influence of the continuously decaying radial velocity field (v ∝ 1/r) on interface dynamics remains poorly understood. This study used a microfluidic radial-flow platform featuring controlled cylindrical pillar arrays and a high-resolution colorimetric reaction system to capture transport-regime transitions across three orders of magnitude in Péclet number (Pe) and Damköhler number (Da) by systematically adjusting injection conditions, and to investigate the spatiotemporal evolution of the reactive front. The results showed that, as Pe increased across this range, the cumulative product mass, MC(t), decreased by nearly half. Under these conditions, due to the limitation of pore-scale mixing, the growth kinetics shifted from a t1/2 trend to a slower type behavior, indicating a transition to mixing-limited kinetics. Furthermore, increased porosity improved average reaction rate by approximately 35% by enhancing pore accessibility and interfacial exchange, whereas increased particle size enhanced the effective pore throat size and streamline length. Finally, the dynamic variation of apparent dispersion parameters demonstrated that a single constant dispersion parameter is insufficient to describe the complete radial reactive-transport process. These findings provide pore-scale insights into radial amendment delivery and highlight the need to balance delivery radius, injection rate, and local mixing efficiency in in-situ remediation design.

title: Global changes in precipitable water vapour during 1980–2100 and its spatial, temporal, radiative and causal insights for enhanced climate warming
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): S. Sarkar, J. Kuttippurath, G.S. Gopikrishnan
abstract: Understanding the spatial and temporal variability and trends in precipitable or total column water vapour (TCWV) is crucial for assessing climate change and hydrological processes. This study utilises European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) reanalysis v5 (ERA5) data from 1980 to 2020 to analyse global and regional TCWV and its key drivers, by applying a combined multi-linear regression (MLR) and Peter and Clark Momentary Conditional Independence (PCMCI) causal framework. Equatorial regions (Amazon, Central Africa, and Southeast Asia) show the highest TCWV (> 50 mm), with seasonal peaks during JJA (June–August) and DJF (December–February) linked to monsoon circulation and ITCZ migration, indicating the role of monsoon-driven atmospheric moisture transport in regulating regional precipitation and the global hydrological cycle. Long-term trends show increasing TCWV, particularly over oceans, with strongest seasonal increases over the western Pacific and Indian Oceans (up to 0.18 mm/yr in DJF) and enhanced monsoon-region moisture convergence during JJA (up to 0.16 mm/yr). Our study identifies Amazonia, Central Africa, and West Pacific Warm Pool (WPWP) as critical moisture hubs (35–50 mm) that govern the global hydrological cycle, while Sahara, Sahel, and Third Pole as regions of persistent atmospheric aridity (5–15 mm) with distinct climatic sensitivities. PCMCI identifies regionally distinct drivers of TCWV (φ ≈ 0.12–0.23), with evaporation and Sea Surface Temperature dominating WPWP, wind divergence controlling Sahel and Sahara, moisture export and evapotranspiration – temperature feedbacks regulating Amazon humidity, while El Niño Southern Oscillation, Pacific Decadal Oscillation, and Arctic Oscillation exert significant teleconnected influences. CMIP6 model future projections show a rising TCWV (5 – 25 mm), serving as a major driver of enhanced latent energy, extreme weather events, and regional climate feedback mechanisms. Additionally, projected increase in TCWV-driven radiative-flux equivalent forcing intensifies regional warming, which ranges from about 0.006 W/m2 (SSP2-4.5) to 0.012 W/m2 (SSP5-8.5) by 2100.

title: Influence of extensive gold mining in the southwestern Amazon on the spatial and temporal dynamics of suspended sediment transport in the Madre de Dios River
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Leo Guerrero, Kory M. Konsoer, Lei Wang, Yulissa Estrada, Pedro Rau, Clinton S. Willson
abstract: The Madre de Dios (MDD) watershed in the southwestern Amazon has experienced extensive environmental degradation and mercury (Hg) contamination due to rapid gold mining expansion. Previous studies documented increased suspended sediment concentration (SSC) using satellite-derived estimates at river inlets and outlets. However, the spatial and temporal variability of SSC along the MDD River, as well as cross-sectional patterns and grain-size distribution, remain insufficiently quantified. This study integrated harmonized surface reflectance data from Sentinel 2 and Landsat 7 and 8, combined with field campaigns, to investigate spatial and temporal SSC dynamics along the MDD River and their response to flow conditions and mining activity. The analysis focused on two phases: the initial mining expansion (1999–2009) and the subsequent floodplain mining intensification (2010–2024), across two reaches influenced by the Colorado and Inambari tributary confluences. Results revealed pronounced daily-to-weekly SSC fluctuations associated with peak flow conditions and mining activity, particularly in the upper reach, with marked attenuation downstream. Gold mining altered floodplain hydrology by reactivating tie channels and paleochannels, leading to elevated sediment inputs and atypical sediment exchange between the river and oxbow lakes. Furthermore, the vertical distribution of sediment, dominated by cohesive material representing approximately 60–90% of total SSC and remaining relatively uniform throughout the water column, provided key insights into the potential enhanced transport of Hg along the MDD River system, driven by the strong adsorptive capacity of fine sediment. These findings support improved sediment management and sustainable mining practices aimed at preserving geomorphological stability and ecological integrity in tropical environments.

title: Morphological optimization of urban small watershed blue–green infrastructure to enhance stormwater management benefits: a case study of the Xuanwu Lake Watershed, Nanjing
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Xin Chen, Xiaojun Wang
abstract: Climate change combined with high density urban development has continuously intensified stormwater risks in small urban watersheds, placing increasing pressure on drainage systems. The morphology of blue-green infrastructure (BGI) is widely recognized as a critical determinant of stormwater performance, yet a clear framework for morphological optimization is still lacking. This study develops an innovative methodological framework that integrates type, configuration, distribution, and network to guide BGI morphological optimization. The river network was first optimized, followed by the design of multiple BGI types and connection paths schemes that incorporate river corridors, bioretention systems (BSs), and green roofs (GRs). These were combined with several configuration levels to generate a series of scenarios. Using the 33 km2 Xuanwu Lake watershed in Nanjing as a case study, 26 scenarios were evaluated with the Storm Water Management Model (SWMM) and the Australian National University and Geoscience Australia hydrodynamic model (ANUGA). The analyses focused on total flood volume, peak flow at watershed outlets, maximum water depth, unit scale average water depth, and unit scale peak flow. The efficiency patterns associated with each configuration level were examined, and based on these observations, a composite strategy of “an overall appropriate configuration level with interventions in high-risk units” was proposed. The results indicate that optimizing the river network alone can reduce total flood volume by 35.86% under the 10-year return period (RP10) event. Under the RP10 event, increasing green-space configuration substantially improved system performance. At the 25% level, peak flow and total flood volume were reduced by an average of 26.64% and 59.54%, respectively. When configuration reached 100%, the corresponding reductions increased to 53.41% and 92.91%. Converting BS installations from isolated distribution to connected distribution with surrounding pervious and impervious surfaces provided an additional 15.9%–45.35% reduction in total flood volume. Linking the GR and BS in series improved regulation by a maximum of 2% and enhanced system stability. Marginal efficiency exhibited clear stage-dependent characteristics. The 0%–25% configuration interval achieved the highest reduction in total flood volume, while the 25%–50% interval showed an improvement in peak flow reduction. Beyond 50%, the benefits declined markedly. Efficiency responses at the watershed and unit scales were generally consistent. These findings provide a solid evidence base for spatial BGI morphological planning and offer a scalable methodological framework for strengthening the resilience of urban watersheds.

title: Effects of aquifer heterogeneity and anisotropic conductivity on non-Darcian flow to partially penetrating wells
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Qing Wang, Zhenming Shi, Yong Zhi Zhao
abstract: This study investigates non-Darcian flow to a partially penetrating well in confined aquifers, considering the stratification of the aquifer. A layered computational model is developed based on the transformed differential quadrature method (TDQM) and the Izbash equation. The continuity equation governing groundwater flow under Izbash’s law is first linearized through an approximation technique. The proposed solution is derived under the adopted linearization approximation and is therefore expected to provide the most reliable predictions during intermediate and late pumping periods. The Laplace transform is then applied, and the radial and vertical directions across multiple layers are discretized using the TDQM scheme, leading to a system of algebraic equations. By incorporating boundary conditions and enforcing inter-layer continuity, a global system matrix is constructed. Solving this matrix system and performing the inverse Laplace transform yield the non-Darcian drawdown solution for the multi-layered confined aquifers. After two validations, case studies are designed to analyze the effects of various parameters on drawdown, including non-Darcian index, comparisons between layered model and the equivalent homogeneous model, sensitivity analysis of hydraulic conductivities, effect of well partial penetration and the influence of well skin.

title: An attention-enhanced hybrid physics-informed neural network for multi-parameter inversion of heterogeneous reservoirs in CO 2 geological storage
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Zhankui Liu, Peixue Jiang, Ruina Xu, Zhen Wang
abstract: Accurate characterization of heterogeneous reservoir properties and robust prediction of CO2 plume migration are critical for the safety assessment and monitoring of geological carbon storage. Geological parameter inversion in high-dimensional heterogeneous reservoirs under limited observations remains a strongly ill-posed problem. In this study, an attention-enhanced hybrid physics-informed neural network inversion framework is developed. This framework integrates multiphase flow governing equations, rock-physics constraints, observational data, low-dimensional geological priors, and attention-enhanced neural-network representations into a unified inversion architecture and loss formulation. A hybrid attention mechanism combining parallel sub-networks, self-attention, and cross-attention is designed to improve the network’s ability to learn complex nonlinear features. Karhunen-Loève expansion (KLE) is employed to construct a low-dimensional and geologically constrained prior parameter representation. Gaussian kernel feature mapping is also used to improve the caption of localized variations. The proposed framework is validated using a two-dimensional single-well CO2 injection scenario in a heterogeneous reservoir. Numerical results demonstrate that the framework can accurately reconstruct pressure and saturation fields, as well as heterogeneous distributions of porosity and permeability. A systematic ablation study further confirms the critical roles of attention mechanisms and KLE-based prior representations in improving inversion accuracy and stability. This study provides a promising tool for prediction and risk assessment in CO2 geological storage applications.

title: Coupled hydrological and public health risks from urban flooding: integrated remote sensing, machine learning, and hydrodynamic–ecological modelling
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Rahul Deopa, Vaibhav Tripathi, PS Nandana, Mohit Prakash Mohanty
abstract: Urban flooding poses concurrent threats to infrastructure, human safety, and public health, particularly in densely populated megacities around the globe, where floodwater often acts as a mobile pathway for microbial contamination. This study develops an integrated remote sensing–machine learning–hydrodynamic modelling framework to quantify coupled flood and microbial health risks. Water surface temperature retrieved from Landsat thermal infrared imagery was used as a predictor in a Support Vector Regression model to estimate spatio-temporal variations in E. coli concentration. These predicted microbial loads were subsequently incorporated into a 3-way coupled MIKE + Flood–ECO Lab framework to simulate flood inundation, contaminant transport, and exposure pathways under flood conditions. Hydro-meteorological forcings, including rainfall, streamflow, and urban drainage flow, together with spatial inputs such as topography and land use–land cover, were used to drive the hydrodynamic simulations. The predicted E. coli concentrations were used to parameterize microbial loading, and infection risks for adults and children exposed to contaminated floodwater were quantified using the β-Poisson dose–response model. Experimenting with the proposed framework over Delhi (India)- a city highly prone to flooding and waterborne health hazards, reveals that ∼ 63% of floodplains faced “high” to “very high” flood hazards, with E. coli levels consistently exceeding safe bathing thresholds (500 MPN/100 mL). Estimated annual infection risks surpassed the USEPA benchmark, with children being the most vulnerable. The study provides actionable recommendations for holistic flood management and emphasizes the urgent need to integrate microbial water quality into flood risk assessment and public health planning, particularly in rapidly urbanizing, climate-sensitive regions.

title: Toward coordinated water allocation in urban agglomerations under joint supply-demand uncertainty: A distributionally robust bi-level multi-objective framework
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Yan Tu, Qian Li, Yiqian Ding, Yongzheng Lu, Benjamin Lev
abstract: Coordinated water allocation is vital for urban agglomerations where high inter-city dependence amplifies systemic risks. However, traditional management faces strains from climate change and urbanization alongside conflicting interests across management levels. To this end, this study develops a distributionally robust bi-level multi-objective water allocation (DRBMWA) framework to facilitate coordination by integrating a Wasserstein-based distributionally robust representation of joint supply-demand uncertainty. The model features a bi-level multi-objective structure balancing economic cost, environmental load (COD), equity between cities (Gini coefficient), and systemic coordination, with lexicographic priorities (Living > Ecology > Production) reflecting social mandates. The original bi-level model is solved through a tractable single-level reformulation that embeds the lower-level lexicographic responses while preserving the hierarchical decision logic. Applied to the Shandong Peninsula urban agglomeration, results show that: (1) The DRO results reveal a robustness premium, as increasing the conservatism parameter α , which reflects the decision maker’s preference for uncertainty protection, from 1.0 to 1.5 raises the compromise cost by 34.88% while reducing the Gini coefficient from 0.034 to 0.018. (2) Under joint supply-demand stress, the deterministic compromise solution reaches a maximum city–sector shortage rate of 85.64 % , whereas the DRBMWA solution maintains sectoral shortage levels within a more controllable range. (3) Compared with the single-level model, the bi-level model reduces the maximum city shortage rate from 21.16% to 14.19% and strengthens the protection of living and ecological water, although at higher transfer cost and COD discharge. (4) Scenario analysis shows that worsening supply-demand conditions substantially increase transfer costs and weaken coordination performance, indicating a greater need for earlier transfer activation and larger fiscal reserves.
