Event-scale Peak Flow Reduction for CI approaches (PFR-CI) ranged from ∼20% to 80% across exceedance probabilities, with only marginal evidence of reduced attenuation for higher-magnitude events (≤5% exceedance probability), highlighting potential hydraulic and storage-related constraints. Collectively, these findings provide robust empirical evidence that well-integrated NFMs can deliver measurable flood-risk benefits in small, rapidly responding catchments, highlighting the importance of catchment-specific design, long-term monitoring and consideration of antecedent conditions to optimise NFM performance.

title: Embedding geological realizations in global sensitivity analysis: a Morris-based screening approach for complex aquifer systems
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Davide Furlanetto, Rodrigo Pérez-Illanes, Daniel Fernàndez-Garcia, Matteo Camporese
abstract: Global sensitivity analysis (GSA) is increasingly used for interpreting complex hydrogeological models and identifying the relative importance of different sources of uncertainty. Although classical methods focus primarily on parameter uncertainty, the role of geological uncertainty, arising from incomplete knowledge of the spatial arrangement of the hydrogeological facies, may be equally relevant. In this study, we propose an extension of the Morris’ Elementary Effects Test to incorporate geological uncertainty represented through multiple geostatistical facies realizations in a GSA framework. This general approach enables a combined assessment of the influence of parametric and geological uncertainty within a computationally parsimonious diagnostic framework, identifying the factors that most strongly affect different model outputs. The methodology is applied to a complex regional-scale aquifer system located in northern Italy, with integrated modeling of river–aquifer interactions. Across all investigated outputs, the saturated hydraulic conductivity of the gravelly aquifers consistently emerges as the dominant source of uncertainty. However, the spatial arrangement of the facies and the hydraulic properties of the confining units can locally influence hydraulic heads and advective particle tracking as much as aquifer parameters. We also show that parameters controlling river–aquifer exchange processes can affect advective transport pathways even in deep confined aquifers. The proposed approach provides actionable guidance for model refinement, data prioritization, and sensitivity-informed parameter selection.

title: Hindcasting compound coastal-inland flood events caused by post-tropical storms
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Quan Van Dau, Rana Ali Nawaz, Xiuquan Wang
abstract: This study presents a hindcasting framework for reconstructing compound coastal-inland flooding in Prince Edward Island (PEI) during post-tropical storms Fiona (2022) and Dorian (2019). Using observed rainfall and high-water marks (HWMs), with a high-resolution terrain model enhanced with hydro-infrastructure, we simulated flood extents at municipal and island-wide scales using HEC-RAS 2D. The hindcasting results show spatially varying impacts across the island, with Fiona producing greater inundation in eastern PEI and Dorian in the northwest. Fiona’s flood extent exceeded Dorian’s by up to 7.32% in parts of Kings County, while Dorian produced more than twice the inundation of Fiona in portions of Prince County (9.94%). This study advances previous PEI flood modeling efforts by explicitly integrating observed coastal HWMs with inland hydrological forcing within a unified 2D hydrodynamic framework, enabling more accurate reconstruction of compound flooding processes. The HRDEM breaching approach further improved hydraulic connectivity by identifying 2,895 hydraulic structures, more than twice the number contained in the official inventory, thereby enhancing island-scale flood routing. This hindcasting framework demonstrates the value of integrated coastal and inland data for accurately reproducing real flood events and supports future climate adaptation planning in storm-prone regions.

title: High-resolution floodplain topography mapping from ICESat-2 and Sentinel-2 using slope-corrected inundation frequency
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Ju Ma, Ming Zhong, Shengmei Yang, Song Ye, Xuan Ban, Qinchuan Xin, Feng Ling
abstract: Accurate representation of floodplain topography is essential for hydrological modeling, ecosystem assessment, and flood risk estimation. This study proposes a novel approach to produce high-resolution floodplain topography maps, integrating inundation frequency map derived from Sentinel-2 imagery and river cross-sectional terrain from Ice,Cloud, and Land Elevation Satellite-2 (ICESat-2). While satellite-derived inundation frequency (IF) maps provide indirect elevation information, they are susceptible to slope-induced bias in river floodplains. To eliminate the spatial heterogeneity introduced by gradient along the river channel, a quantitative relationship between floodplain elevation and inundation frequency was established, incorporating slope correction. Specifically, we calculated the slope gradient sequence of the river in the study area to construct a slope correction lookup table (LUT). Then, we calibrated the elevation of each sample point by eliminating the slope gradient based on the correction origin. This study uses the lower Han River floodplain as a case study, covering approximately 100 km of river reach with an elevation variation of about 5 m. The proposed method yielded RMSEs of 1.039 m, 1.364 m, and 1.375 m for the Han River, Mississippi River, and Han River in-situ validation, respectively, indicating high predictive accuracy and strong robustness across validation settings. The stable model performances were present by comparing the algorithmic accuracy across 10- meter, 5- meter, 2.5-meter spatial resolutions of inundation frequency. Different slope data is also suit for this slope-corrected method, such as SWORD-derived slope information. The model error. This method requires no in-situ measurements, making it broadly applicable to data-scarce or inaccessible floodplains worldwide.

title: A decision-making framework for the trade-off between water conservation and water supply functions in the Wei River basin
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Dongdong Wang, Yangwen Jia, Cunwen Niu, Jiajia Liu, Yaobing Sui, Chunfeng Hao
abstract: It remains a major challenge to determine the suitable spatial extent of vegetation restoration within a watershed to balance upstream water conservation (WC) and downstream water supply. To address this trade-off, we propose a novel framework that integrates scenario analysis with multi-objective decision-making methods. The framework primarily consists of three key steps. Firstly, the Water and Energy process in Large River Basin (WEP-L) model is employed to identify the most suitable Land Use/Land Cover (LULC) conversion type to enhance the main WC functions in each sub-basin. Secondly, a multi-objective decision-making approach was developed to simultaneously maximize upstream WC and downstream water supply, incorporating a food security constraint for the study area. Finally, the ideal point method was applied to determine the optimal extent of vegetation restoration that best balances these competing objectives. The framework is implemented in the water conservation area of the Wei River Basin (WCA-WRB), a critical region in the Wei River Basin of China. The results indicated that converting 28% of the study area to the LULC type most suitable for the function of decreasing floods would be the most effective strategy. This corresponds to a vegetation restoration area of approximately 3757 km2, of which approximately 3092 km2 of cropland was converted to vegetation, representing 5% of the total study area. This proposed framework offers a valuable reference for guiding vegetation restoration projects in similar semi-arid and semi-humid regions.

title: Projecting flood exposure in China under future climate and population change: an age-structured analysis based on the SSP-RCP scenarios
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Qian Yao, Can Lu, Mengya Li, Jiangyang Lin, Hanqing Xu, Dai Yamazaki, Jun Wang
abstract: Accurate projecting future flood exposure requires accounting for both climatic drivers and population structure. However, most assessments overlook age-related disparities in exposure, focusing on total population or economic losses. Here, we present age-structured flood exposure projections in China under future climate and population changes, based on SSP scenarios. We integrate multi-model climate projections, a physically-based hydrodynamic model, and age-structured population data to assess future flood exposure among children, working-age adults, and the elderly. Results show that, although the total population may decline, climate-driven flood hazards will dominate, with overall flood exposure projected to increase by 2.9 (2.4–6.5) times by 2100. The elderly will face the most dramatic increase—up to 6.9 (6.7–18.8) times—potentially surpassing working-age adults. Decomposition analysis reveals that the interaction of climate and population change accounts for up to 53% of the increase in elderly exposure, exceeding the independent effect of climate alone. Our findings highlight the urgency of integrating population structure into multiscale flood exposure assessments, and call for targeted adaptation strategies to address age-related vulnerabilities under future scenarios.

title: Decoupling geogenic and anthropogenic drivers of groundwater natural background levels using machine learning and high-resolution maps
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Yunhui Zhang, Rongwen Yao, Domenico Cicchella, Ming Luo, Md. Galal Uddin
abstract: Accurate determination of natural background levels (NBLs) of groundwater hydrochemistry is critical for setting water quality standards, yet traditional approaches often fail to capture spatial heterogeneity, particularly in large-scale regions with uneven monitoring networks and human activities. To bridge the gap, this study proposes a novel framework that integrates machine learning models (TabPFN and XGBoost) with spatial grid resampling to model NBLs and their controlling factors (strata, land use/land cover, topographic slope, population, and nitrogen fertilizer use), thereby generating high-resolution NBL maps. A total of 1250 groundwater samples from the northwest Sichuan Basin, China, were used to validate this framework. The results showed that TabPFN outperformed XGBoost in NBL prediction across all parameters, yielding higher R2 (0.933–0.979) and reduced uncertainty by 15%–44%. The high-resolution NBL maps revealed that, although lithology remained the primary control on geogenic indicators (e.g., Ca2+, Mg2+), anthropogenic drivers reshaped the baseline patterns of hydrochemical parameters (e.g., NO3-N, Cl−, and Na+). The dissolution of mirabilite, dolomitic strata (Cretaceous), and calcareous formations (Jurassic) explained the elevated SO4 2−/Na+ in the groundwater environmental unit (GEU) Ⅰ, Mg2+ in GEU Ⅱ, and Ca2+ in GEUs Ⅲ–Ⅵ, respectively. Slow groundwater runoff increased hydrochemical concentration in GEUs Ⅰ and Ⅲ–Ⅵ. Domestic sewage and nitrogen fertilizer application were identified as the primary sources of elevated Na+/Cl− and NO3-N levels, respectively, which notably affected GEUs Ⅰ and Ⅲ–Ⅴ. The maps characterized the spatial heterogeneity of NBLs, thereby enhancing the understanding of baseline hydrochemistry. Contemporary NBL should be regarded as a present-day baseline modified by modern human activities. These findings provide an effective approach for determining groundwater NBLs across large, unevenly sampled areas.

title: An improved grout bag–secondary grouting (GBSG) method with time-dependent viscosity modeling for hydrodynamic sealing in karst groundwater conduits
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Miao Piao, Qiao Wang, Fusheng Zha, Dongmei Zhang, Long Xu, Bo Kang, Shixian Ren
abstract: Large-scale karst conduits pose persistent challenges for underground sealing because of strong groundwater flow, highly irregular geometries, and severe grout loss. In this study, an innovative grout bag-secondary grouting (GBSG) methodology is introduced. The sealing mechanisms and construction design principles of the GBSG method are investigated using a newly developed extensible time-dependent viscosity model (ETDVM) implemented in OpenFOAM. The ETDVM incorporates a modified Herschel-Bulkley formulation to simulate the time-dependent rheological behavior of grout. The results showed that: (1) in the GBSG method, the grout bag acts as a hydrodynamic buffer, reshaping the internal flow field and generating low-velocity recirculation zones that markedly reduce grout loss; (2) among the investigated variables, water-flow velocity and grout ratio are the dominant factors controlling sealing performance, and the grout with the R3 ratio exhibited the best performance because its higher viscosity and faster setting rate provided the strongest resistance to flow-induced washout; and (3) the combination of a circular bag, an R3 grout ratio, and a relative bag diameter of 1.5 m yielded the best overall performance. Overall, by developing a new numerical viscosity model capable of capturing time-dependent grout rheology, this study enables the optimization of a novel grouting method for large-scale karst conduits and provides a generalizable numerical framework for process innovation and optimization of non-Newtonian grouting in complex hydrogeological environments.

title: A comprehensive assessment and comparison of streamflow simulations performance between the national water model versions 3.0 and 2.1 across the continental United States
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Ashish Ojha, Haowen Yue, Kendra Dresback, Long Jiang, Tiantian Yang
abstract: The National Water Model (NWM) has undergone several updates since its inception. The performance of its latest release, version 3.0, has yet to be comprehensively evaluated. This study presents the first comprehensive CONUS-wide evaluation of NWMv3.0 retrospective streamflow simulations (1979–2020) and compares them against the preceding NWMv2.1. Using observed streamflow from over 4300 United States Geological Survey (USGS) gages, we jointly evaluated both daily flow and annual peak-flow performance across spatial, seasonal, and categorical dimensions. Results showed that NWMv3.0 generally outperformed NWMv2.1 in both daily flow and peak flow statistics. For daily flow, the mean Kling-Gupta Efficiency (KGE) improved from −0.15 to 0.07, while the mean Percent Bias (PBIAS) dropped from 70.98% to 42.19%. For peak flows, mean Average Annual Peak Flow Bias (AAPFB) decreased from 690% to 234%, and mean Average Annual Peak Timing Error (AAPTE) reduced from 0.62 to 0.27 h from v2.1 to v3. Geographically, the Eastern U.S. generally showed better performance than the Central and Western regions, although the latter showed the greatest relative improvements despite overall lower performance. Seasonally, both versions performed best in spring and worst in winter in terms of mean KGE, with the most substantial statistical improvements observed in winter. Additionally, we also found that the natural gages consistently outperformed human-impacted gages for both versions. Despite overall statistical gains in NWMv3.0, spatial variability in performance still highlights the need for region-specific refinements in future NWM development to better capture diverse hydrologic conditions.

title: Thermal effects on aquifer storage and recovery in brackish aquifers
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Hongkai Li, Zhilin Guo, Zidong Pan, Yang Zhan, Sichen Wan, Hua Zhong, Chunhui Lu, Chunmiao Zheng
abstract: Aquifer storage and recovery (ASR) implemented in brackish aquifers is commonly analyzed within a variable-density framework that accounts for salinity contrast between injected and native groundwater. While previous ASR studies commonly assumed isothermal conditions, the thermal characteristics of recharge water vary widely in practice and may alter buoyancy-driven mixing and freshwater recoverability. Using an axisymmetric SEAWAT model, we explicitly simulate coupled heat and solute transport to quantify how injection temperature governs flow dynamics, freshwater-saltwater interface evolution, and recovery efficiency (RE) of injected freshwater across multiple ASR cycles and hydrogeological settings. Results show that cold injection suppresses density-driven convection, producing near-vertical freshwater-saltwater interfaces and yielding RE values of 47–77% over the first five cycles even in high-permeability, strongly brackish aquifers where isothermal systems fail. We introduce a thermally adjusted convection index (TACI) that integrates salinity- and temperature-induced buoyancy effects and provides a unified diagnostic framework for interpreting interface tilting, mixing, and RE. Hydrogeological factors (e.g., vertical confinement and localized permeability deviations) influence thermal dissipation and circulation patterns but are secondary to injection-temperature control. Multi-cycle simulations demonstrate that cooling-assisted ASR (i.e., lowering injection temperature to mitigate buoyancy instabilities) remains effective under mild, short-lived warming but becomes increasingly fragile under stronger or prolonged temperature excursions. These findings highlight the previously underappreciated role of thermal processes in ASR performance and demonstrate that lowering injection temperature offers a simple and effective strategy to enhance ASR performance in brackish aquifers.

title: A probabilistic prediction model based on uncertainty quantification and interpretable deep learning: Application to runoff prediction in the Yellow River mainstream
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Liang Mu, Junxi Chen, Zhiguo Yu, Hong Zhao, Zhibo Yang
abstract: Accurate and reliable runoff prediction is essential to water resources planning and management. Runoff in the Yellow River mainstream is influenced by both climate change and human activity, leading to pronounced nonlinearity, non-stationarity, and predictive uncertainty. Conventional deterministic forecasting models generally provide only point estimates and therefore cannot fully reflect runoff uncertainty. To address this limitation, we develop a probabilistic runoff prediction method that integrates uncertainty quantification with interpretable deep learning for both point and probabilistic runoff forecasting. First, a directed adjacency matrix is created by combining spatial features such as the topological structure of the Yellow River mainstream and tributaries, spatial distances between hydrological stations, and station elevation. This matrix enables the spatio-temporal graph convolutional network (STGCN) to capture runoff-related spatial dependencies. Second, we use predictive variance and the Gaussian negative log-likelihood function to quantify data uncertainty, and MC Dropout to quantify model uncertainty. The two uncertainty components are incorporated into the training objective to guide uncertainty model learning. The sampled predictive outputs are further transformed into runoff probability distributions using Gaussian kernel density estimation, yielding both deterministic point forecasts and probabilistic prediction function. Finally, SHAP is introduced to interpret the influence mechanism of multiple input features on runoff prediction. A case is conducted using daily observations from hydrological stations along the Yellow River mainstream. Compared with benchmark models, the proposed model improves RMSE, MAE, and MAPE for point prediction by at least 11.46%, 13.21%, and 15.45%, respectively, and improves CRPS and PICP for probabilistic prediction by at least 10.42% and 7.32% respectively. The results demonstrate that this study can provide reliable runoff prediction information for water resources planning in the Yellow River Basin.

title: Development and optimization of a multifunctional sensor for measuring soil thermal properties, water retention characteristics and electrical conductivity
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Xiangwei Wang, Jiagui Hou, Yaohui Cai, Chaoyue Zhao, Junru Chen, Zuyao Chen, Francis Zvomuya, Miles Dyck, Hailong He
abstract: Soil water content, matric potential, thermal properties, and electrical conductivity are fundamental and interrelated properties required by a variety of applications in soil science, hydrology, agriculture, and engineering. However, the measurements of the properties are affected by the temporal and spatial variability of soil due to employment of a variety of sensors, which hinders the research and modeling of coupled water, heat and solute transport. In addition, the laborious, costly and time-consuming sensor optimization is always a challenge for traditional sensor development. The objective of this study was to develop a multifunctional sensor integrating heat pulse, time domain reflectometry and porous ceramic matrix and optimize the sensor with COMSOL based numerical simulations. COMSOL simulated ceramic properties (e.g., thermal conductivity, volumetric heat capacity, dielectric permittivity, electrical conductivity) and soil properties (e.g., thermal conductivity and volumetric heat capacity) with different scenarios of sensor dimensions (e.g., the radius and length of the ceramic and extended rod length) were systematically evaluated and verified with experimental data. Our results show that the optimal radius and length of the ceramic are 18 mm and 40 mm, respectively, and the optimal rod length extended out of the ceramic is 50 mm. The optimized results indicate low estimation errors for dielectric permittivity (±1%), electrical conductivity (±1%), thermal conductivity (±2%), and volumetric heat capacity (±1%) of the ceramic as well as thermal conductivity (±3%) and volumetric heat capacity (±1%) of soil. The new multifunctional sensor can provide accurate measurement and modeling of soil hydrothermal properties.

title: Hydrogeochemical evolution in a semi-arid basin: coupled effects of hydrogeological processes, mineral weathering, and biogeochemical processes
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Deshuai Ji, Wenke Wang, Jie Li, Ning Liu, Manhong Xia, Xiaoqin Huang
abstract: Large sedimentary basins in semi-arid regions typically develop hierarchically nested groundwater flow systems. Their large spatial scales challenge the elucidation of hydrogeochemical evolution within thick aquifers. This study aims to reveal the coupled control mechanisms of hydrogeological processes, mineral weathering, and biogeochemical transformations on hydrochemical evolution and nutrient cycling. Relying on a representative multi-level monitoring transect to collect vertically discrete samples along flow paths in the Yinchuan Plain, China, we systematically elucidated hydrogeochemical evolution by integrating hydrodynamics, multivariate statistics, and multi-isotope tracers (3H, 15N, 34S, 18O, 13C, 14C, and 87Sr/86Sr). Results indicate that hydrodynamics drives geochemical environment and hydrochemical evolution. From recharge to discharge zones, decreasing flow velocities and progressive electron acceptor consumption shift groundwater from oxidizing conditions dominated by nitrification and sulfide oxidation to reducing conditions where Fe/Mn reduction and DNRA occur. Concurrently, prolonged residence times alter mineral thermodynamic equilibria, shifting dominant water–rock interactions from silicate/carbonate weathering to evaporite dissolution. Notably, the mechanisms controlling groundwater quality evolution vary across different hierarchical flow systems. Local flow systems are controlled by the combined influence of anthropogenic activities and biogeochemical processes, with anthropogenic inputs contributing up to 76.2% of nitrate pollution. In contrast, intermediate and regional flow systems are primarily impacted by evaporite dissolution and DNRA. Furthermore, geological faults in the discharge zone force the upwelling of the regional flow system, which has a contribution rate of 52%–57% to the groundwater quality in the mixing zone, leading to anomalous solute enrichment. Ultimately, this study establishes a conceptual model of hydrogeochemical evolution driven by coupled hydrogeological processes, mineral weathering, and biogeochemical processes. These findings provide a crucial scientific basis for groundwater resources and water quality management in semi-arid basins under anthropogenic pressures.

title: TCE redistribution and inferred entrapment in loess under groundwater table fluctuation patterns
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 678 Author(s): Yaoxiang Li, Ningjie He, Xiaoqian Li, Aiguo Zhou, Lei Zhao, Yuxuan Fang
abstract: Groundwater table fluctuations (GTF) regulates the multiphase distribution and mass transfer of trichloroethylene (TCE) through the coupling amplitude and velocity, which determine moisture content redistribution and hydrodynamic forcing. This study quantified TCE redistribution in metastable loessial silt under various GTF patterns using soil column experiments. Results demonstrate that fluctuation amplitude determines the vertical range of elevated moisture content, while velocity dictates the moisture content distribution within the affected zones. From a transfer perspective, high moisture content facilitates TCE desorption in the source zone but inhibits adsorption in surrounding soil layers due to competitive site occupancy. Hydrodynamic conditions and moisture content also govern the mass transfer processes: high-amplitude fluctuations generate a stronger piston effect that drives vapor-phase TCE toward surface, whereas low-amplitude fluctuations provide insufficient hydrodynamic force to break through the upper buffer zone. Furthermore, fluctuation velocity regulates the rate and magnitude of concentration changes in both the vapor and aqueous phases. Capillary moisture content regulates vapor-phase entrapment and aqueous-phase transport efficiency. Mechanistically, we propose a conceptual link wherein high-moisture-triggered structural collapse of metastable soil skeleton reduces pore size and enhances physical entrapment. These results highlight the necessity of integrating medium metastability into environmental risk assessment to avoid underestimating vapor intrusion and secondary release hazards driven by physical entrapment.

title: From magnetic anomaly to geothermal resource: An updated Curie depth map for the geothermal assessment of Colombia
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 142 Author(s): Sergio González-Posada, Carlos A. Vargas
abstract: The study estimates the Curie Point Depth (CPD) of the Colombian territory using magnetic anomaly data and two inversion methods, providing insights into crustal thermal structure. The availability of new magnetic information from the Geological Survey of Colombia and EMAG2V3 satellite data updates the Curie isotherm for northwestern South America. This development represents a significant asset for geothermal energy engineering. The calculation uses the centroid and fractal nonlinear curve adjustment methods, with results compared to tectonic features, ANH geothermal gradients, and element concentrations. The average CPD value was determined to 65.7 km ± 37.8 km (centroid method) and 21.0 ± 9.1 km (nonlinear adjustment method). Following ANH bottom hole temperature data integration, cokriging interpolation refines the nonlinear fractal results and heat flow estimates. This allows direct comparison between three thermal indicators: heat flow derived from CPD centroid calculations, cokriging-based estimates, and direct bottom hole temperature measurements. Shallow CPD values (18–23 km) are observed in the Southern Andes, aligning with high volcanic density and geothermal anomaly areas including Las Animas-Chiles, Cerro Bravo-Cerro Machín, San Diego, and Huila-Sucubun. Deeper values (>30 km) are found in the Northern Andean sector, particularly in the Magdalena Basin, Caldas Tear zone, Bucaramanga's seismic nest, Paipa-Iza regime, and aged geologic bodies. These correlate with the convergence of the Nazca, South American, and Caribbean plates. CPD results show a NE-SW trend controlled by the orogenic system of the three Andean Cordilleras. Moderate correlations exist for calcium (Ca) and potassium (K) in active sediments, but not for iron (Fe), titanium (Ti), and magnesium (Mg).

title: Wet and dry faults at thrust fronts as indicators of paleofluid flow in the carbonates of the Geneva Basin (Switzerland, France)
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 142 Author(s): G.L. Cardello, M. Lupi, E. Carminati, C. Doglioni, M. Sartori, E. Samankassou, M. Meyer
abstract: Thrust fronts are common targets for geothermal exploration in foreland basins because they contain fractured reservoirs made of a floor thrust and a frontal anticline, eventually crossed by high-angle transfer faults, and minor thrust splays. Although regional fluid flow is also controlled by petrophysical properties and the geothermal gradient, the tectonic contribution is best understood through outcrop analogs. We investigate tectonic controls on paleo-circulation across the carbonate-rich thrust front systems surrounding Geneva to better understand present-day hydrothermal pathways. Structural mapping and mesostructural analysis identify high-angle “wet” (mineralized) and “dry” (non-mineralized) faults, revealing where paleofluids circulated and sealed voids. Fault geometry defines a hierarchical network. First-order faults (>2.5 km long), mainly NW-oriented tear faults, accommodated thrust front curvature and acted as primary conduits for mineralizing fluids, except where E-W and WNW faults intercept the thrust front. Second-order faults, which are 0.4–2.5 km long, are less continuous and rarely mineralized. This suggests limited fluid migration in such gregarious faults. The fabric of mineralizations ranges from syn-kinematic slickenfibers to post-kinematic vadose cements, depending on fault orientation, kinematics, offset, and segmentation. The presence of rebrecciated fabrics and multiple generations of syn-thrusting veins and polygenetic calcite in NW-striking faults at thrust fronts suggests that these faults represent fossil examples of transient builds-up of paleofluid overpressure and deformation. Conversely, W- to WNW-tear faults mostly represent alternated pressure-solution and discrete faulting. These findings provide a framework for identifying permeable zones in carbonate thrust fronts, offering practical guidance for assessing geothermal exploration in deformed foreland basins.

title: Temperature field and assessment methodology for a low-medium temperature geothermal field: 3D geological-geophysical modeling in the Xiong'an Area, Northern China
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 142 Author(s): Na Peng, Yihao Wu, Hanqing Qiao, Jiangtao Han
abstract: Mid-low temperature hydrothermal systems are widely distributed in continental intraplate basins, and accurately characterizing their deep thermal structures is crucial for understanding regional geothermal genesis. As a typical intraplate field, the Xiong'an Area in North China possesses significant deep potential. However, previous studies focused on localized assessments of isolated shallow fields, lacking regional 3D simulations based on fine structural constraints, which restricts the understanding of deep heat transfer mechanisms.In this study, we integrated three deep seismic reflection profiles, one magnetotelluric (MT) profile, regional geological, and well-log data to construct a high-resolution 3D geological-geophysical model. Constrained by petrophysical data, we employed a Multi-source data integration approach to solve the 3D steady-state heat conduction equation, achieving high-precision geothermal simulation down to 5 km depth, validated by measured well temperatures.Our results reveal significant spatial differentiation in the regional thermal structure, primarily controlled by varying "caprock-reservoir" configurations. The northern region (e.g., Rongcheng and Niutuozhen fields) exhibits a "thin caprock-shallow reservoir" pattern ( 3 km). The 3D model indicates the southern deep system possesses a significantly higher geothermal gradient, forming a promising target for deep exploration. Furthermore, we identify a concealed deep geothermal prospect near the Raoyang depression. This study delineates reliable exploration targets and provides a universally applicable framework for modeling Multi-source data integration in intraplate geothermal systems.

title: Field demonstration and integrated productivity-economics assessment of multi-lateral geothermal wells enabled by directional steel shot drilling
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 142 Author(s): Paromita Deb, Andreas Reinicke, Jan Jette Blangé, Morteza Esmailpour, Carlo Guarnieri Calo’ Carducci, Martin O. Saar
abstract: This study explores the potential of multi-lateral slim-hole drilling to enhance reservoir access and connectivity in fractured geothermal reservoirs. At the core of this work is Directional Steel Shot Drilling (DSSD), a technology that combines conventional mechanical drilling with the erosive action of pressure-accelerated steel shots. This approach enables the cost-effective construction of multi-directional boreholes from a single wellbore. The DSSD technology was piloted at the VersuchsStollen Hagerbach underground research facility in Switzerland. The test site provides access to fractured hard rock formations under realistic stress and pore-fluid pressure conditions. Two horizontal wellbores, each 125 m long, were drilled. Rates of penetration (ROP) increased up to 2–5 times depending on the steel shot concentration in the drilling mud. Controlled building rates under steering (∼ 3.8–6.6°/30 m) and stable trajectories under non-steering conditions (∼ 0.3° /30 m) were achieved. The pilot demonstrated several key aspects: straightforward retrofitting of DSSD on conventional drill rigs, effectiveness of the steering concept, efficient transportation of steel shots in the mud, and the resulting enhanced bit performance in hard rock. To assess field-scale implications, reservoir simulations and a techno-economic assessment were performed using a fractured carbonate reservoir case. A set of 1000 geological realizations was generated to capture uncertainty in permeability distribution. These models were used to evaluate thermal energy production for 20 years, employing single-, dual-, and triple-lateral well architectures. Median results indicated that adding a second lateral boosts production by 45 – 50%, while a third lateral leads to an additional 25 – 30% gain. The techno-economic evaluation shows corresponding reductions in the levelized cost of heat by ∼20% when moving from single- to dual-lateral configurations, and by a further ∼25% when a third lateral is added. Similarly, the specific capital cost declines by ∼24% from single to dual laterals and by an additional 16% for triple laterals. Results remain conditional on assumptions of geology, well design, economics, and scalability to greater depth.

title: A GIS-based geothermal heat cost index (GHCI) map for efficient energy planning in Europe
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 142 Author(s): Younes Noorollahi, Steffen Nielsen, Bernd Moller, Amir Naseri
abstract: In the present society, sustainable energy system development is a vitally important issue receives considerable attention. Central district heating systems supported by renewable energy sources would play an essential role in future energy systems. Geothermal energy, as a renewable energy source, can provide a reliable baseload energy supply for direct uses of heat, such as space heating. For future energy system planning the economic feasibility of such a geothermal district heating system is very important for its viability among other available renewable and nonrenewable energy resources. In this regard, the Levelized Cost of probable hydrothermal geothermal resources of European countries is evaluated using a modified GIS-based GEOPHIRES code. The cost of geothermal heat varies over a wide range according to the many local and global parameters that are affecting the produced heat cost. The results show that, for the resources at a depth of 1000 m the geothermal heat can be provided by 3.7–18 USD/GJ. Furthermore, for deeper geothermal resources (a depth of 2000 m) the heat can be provided at a lower cost and it is more widely available in most of the countries with a cost of 3.4-17 USD/GJ around Europe.

title: Comprehensive characterization of drill core, and geochemical alteration pathways of drill core from the Humu’ula groundwater research project, Hawaii, USA: II. Keamuku maneuver area
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 142 Author(s): Pooja Sheevam, Wendy M. Calvin, Eric Haskins, Thomas Bristow
abstract: In 2013–2015, two deep wells, PTA-2 and KMA-1, were drilled in the Humu‘ula Saddle region of Hawai‘i for groundwater and geothermal exploration as part of a broader effort to understand the geological history and resource potential of subsurface environments on the island of Hawai‘i. This study focuses on the alteration mineralogy of the KMA-1 drill hole, complementing similar investigations conducted on PTA-2. Mineralogical analysis of KMA-1 involved a multi-scale characterization of aqueous alteration using bulk and high-resolution visible and short-wave infrared (VIS-SWIR) and long-wave infrared (LWIR) spectral imaging, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and X-ray fluorescence (XRF). Several types of secondary phases, including alunite, jarosite, secondary hematite, and smectites, were identified. This study shows distinct zones of alteration interspersed with largely unaltered sections and that alteration is not progressive with depth. Field surveys showed widespread alteration and abundant sulfates, while high-resolution techniques like XRD and XRF detected smaller quantities in bulk rock. This discrepancy suggests that spectroscopic methods are highly sensitive to strongly absorbing, albeit minor, mineral phases. Sulfates are not correlated with confined groundwater units suggesting possible fumarole systems buried over time or acid-steam alteration during post-shield volcanic phases. This study contributes to ongoing efforts to characterize the mineralization associated with geothermal and groundwater systems in the Hawaiian subsurface, providing further insight into hydrothermal processes and alteration pathways.

title: Uncertainty quantification under data worth for the Delft campus geothermal project
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 142 Author(s): Yuan Chen, Guillaume Rongier, James Robert Mullins, Denis Voskov, Alexandros Daniilidis
abstract: Low-enthalpy geothermal doublets for direct-use heating are highly sensitive to subsurface heterogeneity and operational uncertainty. This study quantifies these uncertainties for the Delft campus geothermal system using an integrated workflow that couples geological modeling with GPU-accelerated, high-spatial-resolution reservoir simulation. Ensembles of three-dimensional regional-scale facies models of the Delft Sandstone Member, with and without conditioning to Geothermie Delft (GTD) well data, were generated using object-based modeling and sequential indicator simulation. Porosity was modeled by sequential Gaussian simulation, and permeability was derived from a nuclear magnetic resonance-based porosity–permeability correlation calibrated to GTD well data, yielding higher permeability than core-based correlations for porosity below 15%. Lorenz coefficients indicate strong variability in property distributions, resulting in a wide spread of production temperatures. In total, 2000 geological realizations were simulated over 50 years using the GPU-enabled open-source Delft Advanced Research Terra Simulator (open-DARTS) under maximum and 2025-demand production schemes. Conditioning to GTD wells adds considerable data worth by constraining uncertainty in production well bottom-hole temperature (BHT) and pressure (BHP), while keeping injection pressure within Dutch regulatory limits. SIS models exhibit greater temperature and pressure variability than OBM models due to lower sand-body continuity. Despite large 80% confidence intervals, P50 production temperatures remain comparable for conditioned models. Distance-based generalized sensitivity analysis identifies net-to-gross ratio and the porosity–permeability correlation as dominant controls on thermal response. The 2025-demand scheme delays cold-front propagation. Results demonstrate that ensemble-based, GPU-accelerated high-spatial-resolution simulations enable robust and efficient uncertainty quantification for direct-use geothermal systems, highlighting the importance of well conditioning and reservoir heterogeneity characterization in constraining thermal responses.

title: A survey-based investigation of key challenges in advancing the implementation of energy geostructures
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 142 Author(s): A. Insana, F. Szymkiewicz, E. Khamis, R. Da Re, B. Cao, A. Gluchowski, T. Badinier, J. de Sauvage, Ö. Çinicioğlu, J. Josifovski, A. Minto, J. Pieczyńska-Kozłowska, R. Vasilescu, H.J.L. Witte, H. Mroueh
abstract: The urgent requirement to decarbonise the construction sector and reduce building-related fossil fuel consumption has positioned energy geostructures as a pivotal multipurpose solution for climate change mitigation. However, despite a growing body of scientific literature and knowledge-sharing initiatives, global adoption remains disproportionately low. This paper aims to identify which issues and barriers remain to be overcome in order to enable the widespread implementation and use of energy geostructures. Such aim is obtained through the analysis of the results of a survey sent to actors in the construction industry and academia. The survey, involving 155 international participants, reveals that the primary barriers are perceived to be economic factors and a lack of specialised expertise, training, and guidelines, rather than fundamental technical limitations. Notably, the data indicate that economic barriers appear dominant during the initial feasibility stages, highlighting an urgent need for improved dissemination of economic viability studies; however, during the implementation of energy geostructures, additional challenges are reported, diminishing the relative weight of economic constraints. Indeed, a lack of expertise and guidelines is widely acknowledged by respondents, regardless of whether projects are ultimately implemented, emphasising the need for targeted educational initiatives to foster the adoption of energy geostructures. Legal aspects as well as coordination between the different actors during energy geostructures deployment also appear among the difficulties linked to the implementation of energy geostructures. By identifying and comparatively assessing these multifaceted challenges through survey responses, this paper provides a strategic evidence base for policymakers and industry leaders to develop the frameworks necessary to foster the deployment of energy geostructures in the transition to net-zero.

title: Thermal structure and geothermal potential of the onshore Gippsland basin inferred from 3D conductive heat flow modelling
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 142 Author(s): Belay Gulte Mino, Graeme Beardsmore, Mark A McLean
abstract: Understanding spatial and depth-dependent variations in thermal conductivity is essential for accurate geothermal modelling in sedimentary basins. This study investigates the thermal structure and geothermal potential of the onshore Gippsland Basin, southeastern Australia, by integrating published thermal-property datasets with 3D steady-state conductive modelling using the open-source Underworld3 framework. Lithology-dependent mean thermal conductivity values for the Latrobe Valley Subgroup were derived from borehole lithological proportions and ranged from 0.56 to 1.21 W/m·K, reflecting strong lateral heterogeneity associated with variable coal content. The thermal model incorporates spatially variable land surface temperature (LST), interval temperature logs, bottom-hole temperature data, and laterally varying basal temperatures extrapolated using one-dimensional conductive heat flow models and interpolated across the basin. Model results predict surface temperatures ranging from approximately 11.54 to 20.68°C and laterally variable basal temperatures of approximately 120 to 256°C at 5,000 m depth, reflecting the combined influence of thermal conductivity, heat flow, and surface temperature variability. Temperatures at the top of the Cenozoic-aged geothermal source rock range from approximately 14 to 65°C, indicating favourable conditions for low-enthalpy geothermal applications. Model constraining against borehole temperature data demonstrates good agreement between measured and modelled thermal profiles. Volumetric heat-in-place calculations indicate that the Cenozoic-aged geothermal source contains maximum values of approximately 31 exajoules (EJ) of stored thermal energy. These results highlight the importance of incorporating spatially variable thermal conductivity and non-uniform basal boundary conditions into geothermal models and provide a refined framework for geothermal assessment in the onshore Gippsland Basin and other coal-bearing sedimentary basins.

title: Mapping hydrothermally altered minerals using Landsat-8 satellite data, along bambam-billiri-kaltingo axis, in Upper Benue Trough, Northeastern Nigeria
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 142 Author(s): Bello Yusuf Idi, Mukaila Abdullahi
abstract: The Northeastern Nigerian Upper Benue trough is characterized by hydrothermal and geothermal manifestation features. In this work, the hydrothermally altered mineral deposits are mapped as a reconnaissance survey of the most feasible regions for geothermal energy and oxide mineral exploration in the trough. Bands 2, 4, 5, 6 and 2, 5, 6, 8 of the Landsat-8 OLI are respectively used to highlight iron-oxide and clay/hydroxide-bearing minerals. Band-ratio composites are used to map the relative spatial distribution of the alteration zones. The Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is been used to identify the desired spectral bands for Crosta analysis. Based on the eigenvector loadings of the PC components, PCA bands with the highest eigenvalue loadings of the opposite signs are used to map the spatial distribution of iron-oxide and clay/hydroxyl minerals. The plot of delineated zones of hydrothermal alteration indicates the occurrence of iron oxide predominantly within the Keri-Keri Formation in the Northwestern region of the area. The clay and hydroxyl‑bearing minerals occur mostly within the alluvium sediment of the Bima Formation in the Southern region of the area. The work is a guide for geothermal and hydrothermally altered solid mineral explorations.

title: Characteristics and constitutive model of segmented damage and fracture in granite under thermo-hydro-mechanical (THM) condition
description: Publication date: December 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 142 Author(s): Luping Cheng, Chun Wang, Yi Tan, Hao Li, Zonghong Zhou, Yumeng Ren, Juanjuan Li, Taihao Cui
abstract: Rock damage induced by uneven heating, stress, and water supply (three-uneven) from exothermic minerals and geothermal exploitation remains a critical challenge. Four controlling factors (heating temperature, immersion water temperature, heated section height ratio, and heating-immersion water cycle times) were used to simulate the three-uneven conditions. Cyclic heating-immersion water and segmented heat treatment mechanical tests were conducted on granite. Additionally, the concept of "segmented damage" is introduced to describe regionally differentiated physicochemical damage. Results show four stages in axial stress-strain curves: upward concave, linear, nonlinear post-peak, and downward rebound. The first two stages are significantly influenced by the four factors. Both compressive strength and elastic modulus decrease with increasing four factors, and the dominant failure mode is compression shear. The heating boundary is a tensile stress concentration zone, revealing tensile crack initiation. A smaller heated section height ratio causes more severe fracturing in the unheated section, and vice versa. Positioned acoustic emission method reveals crack initiation from tensile thermal damage at the heating interface, and damage fractures morphologies (V-shaped, Y-shaped, single inclined planes). Damage evolution exhibits phased characteristics similar to biological population growth: slow accumulation, accelerated development, and stabilization. Based on this, a damage variable for granite under THM conditions is defined using biological population growth theory, and a segmented damage constitutive model is established. Theoretical curves match experimental data, showing the model effectively describes and predicts pre-peak mechanical behavior and strength characteristics under THM conditions, especially in the compaction and elastic stages.

title: Quantifying geothermal heat loss at the Dayoukeng crater using UAV thermal imaging and comparison with Landsat-derived estimates
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Hai-Po Chan, Yu-Chang Chan, Cheng-Wei Sun
abstract: This study quantifies geothermal radiative heat flux (RHF) and geothermal radiative heat loss (RHL) at the Dayoukeng (DYK) crater of Tatun Volcanic Group (TVG) in Taiwanusing both UAV thermal imaging and Landsat thermal infrared data. A dawn UAV survey minimized solar effects, acquiring 782 thermal images at 13 cm resolution. Land surface temperatures from both datasets were used to estimate RHF accounting for surface emissivity, atmospheric transmittance, and ambient temperature. Both datasets consistently delineate geothermal anomalies, while UAV imagery uniquely resolves fine-scale thermal heterogeneity. Maximum temperatures reach 84.4 °C in UAV data and 44.4 °C in Landsat, corresponding to peak RHF values of 214 and 62.6 Wm⁻², respectively. Despite differences in spatial resolution and peak values, geothermal heat loss estimates are comparable, with RHL of 210 MW derived from UAV data and 217 MW from Landsat observations, and are of similar order of magnitude to previous geochemical estimates based on the volumetric method. These results demonstrate that satellite thermal imagery provides an efficient tool for regional geothermal heat loss assessment, whereas UAV thermal imaging offers substantially enhanced detail on localized heat flux variability. This study presents the first UAV-based geothermal heat loss assessment at DYK within the Tatun Volcanic Group, northern Taiwan, and highlights the complementary strengths of UAV and satellite thermal observations for geothermal exploration and volcanic monitoring.

title: Influence of fluid-rock interactions on mechanical, thermal and transport properties of sandstone reservoir during geothermal waste fluid reinjection
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Jieqin Xia, Hong Tian, Sadiq J. Zarrouk, Eylem Kaya, Jun Zheng, Bin Dou, Yan Qin, Yanting Zhao, Sen Zhang
abstract: The Guantao formation sandstone geothermal reservoir (SGR) suffers from low reinjection efficiency, severely limiting its sustainable utilization. Reinjection of geothermal waste fluid (GF) back into the SGR triggers intense fluid-rock interactions (FRIs) driven by the coupled effects of mechanical stress, mineralogical composition, and the injected fluid’s physicochemical properties. In this study, we conducted core-scale reactor experiments (25 days) and a batch numerical model (360 days) consistent with experimental parameters to explore the FRI and its influence on rock mechanical, thermal, and transport properties. Results showed that during the initial 25 days, the rock mass loss rate, diameter increase rate, and porosity all exhibited a trend of first increasing and then decreasing. Thermal conductivity varied inversely with porosity, whereas permeability declined sharply within the first 5 hours, then increased, and then declined again. The peak strength and elastic modulus of the rocks showed a fluctuating trend, initially decreasing and then increasing. The combined experimental and simulation results revealed that, before 90 days, the evolution of porosity and permeability was primarily controlled by feldspar dissolution, clay precipitation, and secondary calcite formation. Then, the FRI system gradually approached chemical equilibrium. Building upon the core scale results, a THC-coupled Near-Wellbore model was developed using well-logging data and reinjection conditions. The simulation predicted that after 50 years, reinjection of GF induced a permeability-damaged zone in the near-well region extended to approximately 50 m, while the porosity-affected zone extended to about 100 m. These findings provide valuable engineering insights for similar SGR reinjection operations.

title: Nigorikawa and Otake – Pioneering geothermal binary plants in Japan: Historical perspective, performance assessment, and lessons learned
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Ronald DiPippo
abstract: In the 1970′s in the wake of two Oil Shocks, the countries of the world began a quest for indigenous sources of energy. In particular, alternative means were sought to generate electricity without the need to burn fossil fuels. Japan started its Sunshine Program and included, among several technologies, geothermal energy of which their country has an abundance of potential. Two pilot geothermal binary power plants were created conceptually, designed, and built at locations at opposite ends of the country, and tested for a year. These plants, the Nigorikawa and Otake pilot plants, pioneered some of the features now common at binary plants that have spread across the world, but the technical details of these plants have not yet been published in the mainstream literature. This article describes the plants in technical detail, including their locations, assesses the test results on the basis of thermodynamic First Law and Second Law principles (including exergy), and discusses the implications for future plants. As test plants, their economics was not a priority and this article does not address that facet of the projects.

title: Experimental study of anisotropic behavior of biotite-ordered granite under thermally-coupled true triaxial compression conditions in deep geothermal boreholes
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Yongping Li, Houyu Wang, Hongyuan Zhou, Ming Wu, Zaobao Liu
abstract: The anisotropic mechanical behavior of granite under thermal-mechanical coupling remains poorly understood for the design of deep wellbores in high-temperature geothermal reservoirs, such as those in the Tibetan Plateau. This study experimentally investigates the biotite-induced anisotropy in strength, deformation, and failure modes of granite subjected to true triaxial compression under coupled thermal–mechanical conditions. Experiments were conducted at temperatures of 20, 100, 150, and 190 °C, with minor principal stresses ranging from 10 to 40 MPa, reflecting typical in-situ reservoir conditions. Two loading configurations were designed to examine the effect of the orientation between the intermediate principal stress and the biotite foliation. The results reveal that the orientation of the intermediate principal stress significantly governs the anisotropic behavior. As the minimum principal stress increased, the strength anisotropy coefficient decreased from 0.29 to 0.07. Increasing temperature from 20 °C to 190 °C reduced the strength by approximately 42%, while the strength anisotropy coefficient decreased from 0.18 to 0.02, suggesting a progressive weakening of the controlling effect of the dominant biotite foliation under thermo-mechanical conditions. These findings improve the understanding of the thermo-mechanical anisotropic behavior of biotite-ordered granite and provide useful insights for the design and stability evaluation of deep geothermal wellbores.

title: Integrated geothermometry for mixed-fluid carbonate geothermal systems under structural and hydrochemical constraints: Insights from the Yichuan Basin, central China
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Rudan Zheng, Gaoli Zhao, Jianhua Ping, Wei Leng, Joshua Mahwa, Jichang Zhao, Chengding Huo, Jiaqi Liu
abstract: Reliable characterization of reservoir temperature is an important step in geothermal resource evaluation, engineering design, and long-term utilization in sustainable subsurface energy systems. In groundwater-dominated geothermal systems hosted by fractured–vuggy carbonate reservoirs, conventional geothermometers often yield a wide range of temperature estimates owing to the combined effects of shallow groundwater mixing, re-equilibration, and hydrochemical buffering. These uncertainties hinder the interpretation of subsurface thermal regimes and groundwater circulation processes. In this study, we integrated hydrochemical indicators and environmental isotopes from the Yichuan Basin to constrain the fluid sources, circulation pathways, and mixing processes in a fault-controlled carbonate geothermal system. Building on hydrochemical and isotopic constraints on recharge, circulation, and mixing, we applied a multi-index-weighted geothermometer (MIWG) within a structure- and mixing-informed framework to estimate the reservoir temperatures in the Yichuan Basin. The results indicate that geothermal fluid evolution is jointly controlled by deep water–rock interactions and variable shallow groundwater mixing. Compared with individual geothermometers, the MIWG reduces the influence of method-specific extremes and yields more internally consistent well-specific temperature estimates. The MIWG-derived temperatures ranged from 78 to 157 °C across the study area, with the principal geothermal upflow system most plausibly concentrated at 128–157 °C. This study outlines a structure-informed interpretive framework for integrated geothermometry in mixed-fluid carbonate geothermal systems, distinguishing the indicative reservoir temperature range from the mixing-biased apparent temperatures. The proposed framework may help reduce the uncertainty in reservoir temperature assessment in structurally complex carbonate geothermal systems.

title: Unveiling the hidden heat potentiality of the caledonian and mourne granites, Northern Ireland: A geochemical recalibration of suppressed airborne radiogenic heat signals
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Mahmoud Abdellatif, Ulrich Ofterdinger
abstract: Airborne Gamma-Ray Spectrometry (AGRS) serves as an essential tool for geothermal exploration; nevertheless, its efficiency in peat-covered, till (glacial deposits), and high-moisture soils remains poorly quantified. This study investigates one such example and assesses the discrepancy between airborne-derived Radiogenic Heat Production (RHP) and bedrock geochemistry of the Caledonian and Mourne granites in Northern Ireland. The utilised dual analysis approach (Rybach in 1988 and Carmichael in 1989) indicated that a considerable surface attenuation due to the saturated organic overburden masks the actual capacity of RHP. This is evidenced by the determined low median RHP values of 0.9 µW m–3 (σ± 0.27) and 2.4 µW m–3 (σ± 0.80) for Caledonian and Mourne granites, respectively. Analysis of published whole-rock geochemical data of the Mourne suite contributed to addressing this environmental interference and facilitated the determination of correction factors (CF), enabling the reclassification of Mourne granites. For instance, the derivational regional CF =2.52 resulted in a median RHP of 6.3 µW m–3 (σ± 2.3), significantly categorising Mourne granites as a high heat-producing granite. Moreover, applying this CF to the Caledonian granites yields an average RHP of 2.27 µW m–3(σ± 0.68), precisely reflecting its bedrock characteristics and highlighting a significant regional tendency to underestimate geothermal resources by >50%. These results prove that existing regional RHP maps in peat-covered, glacial and high-moisture regions are notably underestimated and provide a transferable workflow for recalibrating airborne surveys to identify concealed high-heat content targets.

title: Thermo-hydraulic drivers of superhot geothermal well performance
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Samuel W. Scott
abstract: Geothermal wells drilled into superhot (>375 °C) conditions have the potential to produce substantially more power than conventional geothermal wells. However, the interplay between reservoir pressure, temperature and permeability in controlling deliverable power remains poorly understood. Using a coupled reservoir-wellbore modeling framework calibrated against IDDP-1 discharge data, this study quantifies single-well power generation potential across a wide spectrum of superhot conditions, ranging from low-pressure ( 15 MPa) preserves single-phase conditions, reducing risks resulting from liquid condensation in the wellbore and enabling more efficient power conversion. Reservoir temperatures of 450–500 °C maximize power output, beyond which declining mass flows due to lower fluid density overwhelm enthalpy gains. Moreover, achieving power generation >30 MWe per well requires reservoir transmissivities on the order of 1000 md·m. Calibration against IDDP-1 discharge data indicates that values of this magnitude can occur in superhot rock, although they have yet to be deliberately engineered. These findings provide quantitative guidance for targeting and developing superhot resources, demonstrating that reservoir pressure and permeability may be more critical than simply pursuing maximum temperature, though realizing the pressure advantage requires sufficient permeability to sustain flow.

title: Depth-dependent thermal management of a medium-deep coaxial borehole heat exchanger using segmented inner-pipe insulation and enhanced grout conductivity
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Jianjun Sun, Yiming Li, Guiqiu Song
abstract: Medium-deep coaxial borehole heat exchangers are limited by internal thermal short-circuiting, especially in shallow sections where the upward return flow loses heat to the colder descending flow. This study develops a depth-dependent wellbore thermal management strategy that combines segmented inner-pipe insulation, enhanced grout thermal conductivity, and flow-rate optimization for a 2500 m coaxial geothermal well in Shenyang, China. A semi-analytical heat-transfer model was established and validated against field tests at flow rates of 15.5, 20.5, and 26.0 m³/h, which measured heat extraction rates of 242.2, 309.7, and 353.2 kW, respectively. Baseline diagnosis shows that the shallow section contributes little useful heat gain while intensifying return-flow heat loss. A three-zone inner-pipe configuration, with insulation in the upper 750 m, increases heat extraction to approximately 385 kW and maintains a performance evaluation coefficient above 1.0. Increasing grout conductivity from 2.70 to 4.0 W/(m·K) further improves heat output, and combining it with segmented insulation yields a positive non-additive gain. A recommended flow-rate range of 24–27 m³/h is identified by balancing heat extraction and pumping power. Thermal recovery analysis indicates that the formation recovers to 32–33°C after 6–7 days of rest, with a projected annual recovery ratio above 76% over 20 years. These results show that depth-dependent coordination of pipe insulation, grout conductivity, and circulation flow can improve the performance and sustainability of medium-deep coaxial geothermal heating systems.

title: Damage evolution of thermal shock in granite for enhanced geothermal systems
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Liuke Huang, Guolin Rong, Xingchuan Liao, Nailing Xiu, Haifeng Fu, Dingwei Weng, Ling Yu
abstract: Cold-fluid injection in enhanced geothermal systems (EGS) can induce transient thermal shock in hot dry rock, thereby altering the mechanical behavior of the reservoir. However, the coupled influence of thermal shock and confining pressure on granite, as well as the associated microstructural damage mechanisms, remains insufficiently understood. In this study, outcrop granite from the Sichuan Basin was subjected to multi-level high-temperature treatment followed by transient thermal shock tests with different temperature differences. A combination of macroscopic mechanical testing and microstructural characterization using scanning electron microscopy was used to investigate thermal damage evolution from the grain scale to the sample scale. The results show that thermal shock significantly reduces granite strength. After heating to 200 °C and subsequent cooling to 25 °C, the uniaxial compressive strength drops by approximately 38.4%, a reduction far exceeding that caused by heating alone. This weakening effect was markedly suppressed by confining pressure. At 20 MPa confining pressure, the specimen shocked from 400°C to 25°C retained a compressive strength of 395.2 MPa, comparable to that of the room-temperature specimen, 392.4 MPa. Microstructural observations indicate that thermal damage evolves through four stages, from initial crack closure and grain-boundary adjustment to crack propagation and thermally induced degradation. These findings contribute to a better understanding of the thermo-mechanical damage mechanisms in granite and provide a reference dataset for similar parametric studies and numerical model calibration.

title: Machine learning-driven optimization of production-injection scheme: A case study of geothermal doublet system in Yangling, Guanzhong Basin
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Jia Liu, Sen Li, Yi Xue, Chenyang Duan, Shi-Tong Li, Yin Wang, Zhen-Kun Liu
abstract: As a sustainable clean energy source, geothermal energy is widely distributed with large reserves, which can be used in diverse applications. The optimization of the well production-injection scheme is crucial for the efficient production of this type of energy. This case study focuses on a geothermal development project in the Yangling District, Guanzhong Basin. Geological exploration and well data collection are first conducted to understand the occurrence characteristics and geological structure background of the geothermal resource in the district. Using the 1D line element theory for the analysis of 3D wellbore structure, a coupled thermo-hydro-mechanical (THM) model is established in the finite element software, COMSOL. The numerical model can accurately simulate the production-injection process of the geothermal doublet system. Subsequently, a surrogate model is developed to relate production-injection parameters to reservoir responses. Trained through the deep neural network (DNN) of machine learning, the surrogate model’s validity and accuracy are demonstrated by comparing its predicted values with 500 numerically obtained (“true”) values, where larger data sets result in better predictive performance. Further, combining machine learning with 4 optimization algorithms, the production-injection scheme is optimized based on production-injection parameters and objective functions. The revenues (final objective function) obtained by these optimization algorithms are nearly identical, outperforming 95% of true value samples, which shows the reliability and efficiency of the proposed method in determining the optimal production-injection scheme. The study insightfully promotes the intelligent transformation of geothermal energy development.

title: Experimental investigation on energy mechanical evolution and damage model of red limestone subjected to high-temperature water cooling cycling
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Haopeng Jiang, Hui Wang, Fengrui Zhang, Wei Yin
abstract: In geothermal development and high-temperature rock engineering, sedimentary geothermal surrounding rocks are prone to mechanical deterioration and damage accumulation under long-term high temperature effects, cold water recharge, and thermal-water circulation disturbances. In this study, red limestone collected from Ya’an, Sichuan Province, was investigated through a series of triaxial compression tests after exposure to different temperatures (200 °C, 400 °C, 600 °C, and 800 °C) and varying numbers of water-quenching cycles (0, 5, and 10). The degradation of the physical and mechanical properties of the limestone was systematically evaluated, and its energy evolution characteristics, including energy input, storage, dissipation, and release, were analyzed within the framework of energy dissipation theory. The results show that both the peak strength and elastic modulus of the red limestone decrease noticeably with increasing temperature and quenching cycles. The repeated action of thermal stress and rapid cooling promotes crack initiation and propagation between mineral grains, increases porosity, and leads to pronounced deterioration of the internal microstructure. In terms of energy behavior, the progressive accumulation of damage weakens the rock energy storage capacity and significantly raises the proportion of dissipated energy. Based on the experimental results, a statistical damage constitutive model incorporating a modified energy dissipation function was established. The validation results indicate that the proposed model can effectively characterize the nonlinear deformation behavior and strength response of red limestone after high-temperature water-cooling treatment. These findings provide an important theoretical basis for the efficient development of geothermal resources and the stability evaluation of high-temperature rock engineering.

title: Limited heat connectivity across the Northeastern Segment of the Tanlu Fault, China: Implications for low–temperature geothermal systems
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Jingyu Lin, Xuelian Huang, Shuai Wang, Shihua Qi, Xu Wang
abstract: The northeastern segment of the Tanlu Fault (NTLF) hosts predominantly low–temperature geothermal systems, contrasting with the high–temperature resources in the central and southern segments. To elucidate the factors controlling the low–temperature characteristics in the NTLF, we combined geochemical and isotopic analyses of geothermal and cold groundwater with numerical simulations. The results indicate that the geothermal waters are primarily recharged through meteoric water infiltration, with reservoir temperatures ranging from 60 °C to 110 °C and circulation depths extending from 1539 to 2972 m. Hydrogeochemical and isotopic evidence suggests prolonged water–rock interaction, relatively slow groundwater renewal, and limited contribution from high–temperature magmatic or deep hydrothermal fluids. Numerical simulations show that, under limited effective fault permeability, upward heat transfer from deeper thermal domains to shallow and intermediate reservoirs remains weak, and the temperature field is mainly controlled by conductive heat transfer. Sensitivity analyses further support that fault permeability strongly influences the efficiency of upward heat transfer. This study highlights that the geothermal significance of major fault zones depends not only on their structural scale, but also on effective fault connectivity that enables upward heat transfer.

title: Distribution characteristics and controlling factors of the thermal field and geothermal resource potential on the southern margin of the Junggar basin
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Junji Chen, Yingchun Wang, Haozhu Zhang, Yi Wang, Pengfei Chen, Guangzheng Jiang, Jie Hu
abstract: The existing heat flow measurement points in the southern margin of the Junggar Basin are unevenly distributed, with notable gaps in certain areas, resulting in insufficient spatial constraints on the regional geothermal field. Meanwhile, the deep temperature distribution remains poorly characterized and the genesis of geothermal systems has not yet to be fully elucidated. To address these issues, static well temperature data from 16 boreholes were collected and integrated with previously published rock thermophysical parameters to obtain 7 new high-quality terrestrial heat flow values, increasing the total number of measurement points from 31 to 38 and effectively filling the gaps in heat flow coverage. Building on these results, one-dimensional steady-state heat conduction equations were applied to calculate and analyze the planar distribution of the geothermal field at depths shallower than 2000 m, and a comprehensive assessment of geothermal resource potential was conducted in conjunction with regional geological data. The results show that the geothermal gradient ranges from 11.4 to 22.4 °C/km, with a mean of 17.8 ± 2.3 °C/km, and the terrestrial heat flow ranges from 23.4 to 44.5 mW/m², with a mean of 36.2 ± 4.7 mW/m². At burial depths of 500–2000 m, localized high-temperature thermal anomalies are identified in the Sikeshu Depression, the central Qigu Fault-Fold Belt, and the central Huomatu Anticline Belt, which are interpreted as local thermal anomaly zones on the southern margin of the Junggar Basin. The overall low heat flow background is primarily attributed to the combined effects of groundwater circulation, basement relief, structural configuration, and sedimentation rate. The total geothermal resources are estimated at 3823.6 × 10¹⁸ J, equivalent to 123.8 billion tons of standard coal; the Jurassic system contains the most abundant resources at 1066.1 × 10¹⁸ J, while the Quaternary and Neogene reservoirs have the least at 44.8 × 10¹⁸ J. The new heat flow data are consistent with previously published results, together corroborating the low geothermal background of the southern Junggar Basin. These findings provide an important reference for understanding the present-day geothermal field and for geothermal resource exploration and development in the study area.

title: Thermal conductivity evaluation using an integrated method: An example from the Horn River Basin, Canada
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Kezhen Hu, Wanju Yuan, Xiaojun Liu, Stephen E. Grasby, Zhuoheng Chen
abstract: The Horn River Basin in northeastern British Columbia, Canada, hosts significant unconventional shale-gas resources and geothermal potential within the Devonian Horn River Group (HRG). The organic-rich HRG shale is highly heterogeneous due to complex mineralogy and matrix variability across the basin, posing challenges for accurate thermal conductivity (TC) prediction. This study presents an integrated approach to evaluate spatial TC variability by combining comprehensive petrophysical characterization with two-phase mixing models: the Voigt–Reuss–Hill (VRH) average approach and the geometric mean (GM) method. Machine learning techniques were applied to extensive mineralogical data to predict mineral compositions from well logs, while total organic carbon (TOC), porosity, and fluid saturation were quantified through core–log calibrations and statistical analysis. TC profiles were then calculated using the VRH and GM models, incorporating calculated component volumes and mineral TC values adjusted for in situ temperature and pressure conditions. Both measured and modeled results indicate that TC in the low-porosity shale is predominantly controlled by mineralogy/lithology, increasing with quartz and carbonate content and decreasing with higher clay volume. Notably, the VRH approach performs better for lower TC values (<2.5 W/m·K) associated with higher clay and lower quartz and carbonate contents, whereas the GM method is more accurate at higher TC values (≥2.5 W/m·K), corresponding to lower clay and higher quartz and carbonate contents. Given the heterogeneous mineralogy and high TOC content of the HRG shale, integrating both models effectively captures the full range of TC variability and enhances predictive accuracy.

title: Reactive viscous fluid fracturing of volcanic rocks: Chemical weakening offsets viscosity-induced pressure increase
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Geothermics, Volume 141 Author(s): Eko Pramudyo, Nagi Obata, Luis Salalá, Jiajie Wang, Noriaki Watanabe
abstract: Hydraulic stimulation of volcanic reservoirs can be hindered by strong fluid infiltration into pores, vesicles, and microfractures, which suppresses pressure build-up and limits the formation of conductive fractures. Increasing fluid viscosity can reduce fluid loss, but typically at the cost of higher fracturing pressure. Here, we tested whether this viscosity–pressure trade-off can be mitigated by combining viscosity control with chemical weakening of the rock matrix. Triaxial fracturing experiments were conducted at 180 °C on volcanic rocks using water-like fluids, non-reactive viscous fluids, and reactive viscous fluids composed of the biodegradable chelating agent N,N-bis(carboxymethyl)- L -glutamic acid (GLDA) and the biopolymer scleroglucan. Water-like fluids showed strong matrix infiltration and were ineffective at generating large-aperture fractures. Increasing viscosity suppressed infiltration and promoted wider fractures, but increased fracturing pressure. When GLDA was added to the viscous fluid, fracture aperture and fracture-network complexity increased further, while fracturing pressure in the benchmark andesitic tuff experiments remained comparable to that during water injection despite the much higher fluid viscosity.
