Here we present high-precision δ 51/50V data (hereafter δ51V) for volcanic rocks from the Rindjani suite in the Sunda arc that span compositions from high-Al basalts to trachydacites, investigating how V isotopes respond to amphibole-controlled magma differentiation. At the crust–mantle boundary, amphibole-forming peritectic reactions transform H2O-rich magma into Si-rich melt and induce minor δ51V variation of approximately 0.08‰. H2O-rich magmas that bypass the peritectic reaction ascend to the shallow crust and differentiate from high-Al basalts to high-K andesites, showing limited δ51V variation from −0.76‰ to −0.66‰. Shallow-level differentiation of the Si-rich melt from andesites to trachydacites produces a sharp increase in δ51V from −0.62‰ to −0.04‰, consistent with an average mineral-melt fractionation factor Δ51Vmineral–melt ≈ −0.30‰. Published Fe−Ti isotope data show that δ56Fe remained constant, whereas δ49Ti responded to differentiation throughout the compositional range of the Rindjani suite. The decoupled Fe–Ti–V isotope systematics reveal differences in elemental mass balance and mineral–melt isotope fractionation during magma differentiation. These results show that amphibole-forming peritectic reactions fundamentally modify melt chemistry, thereby enabling significant V isotope fractionation associated with magnetite crystallization at shallow levels. Our findings highlight the depth–dependent differentiation framework of arc magmas and advance understanding of the V isotopic pathways involved in continental crust formation.

title: Observational and experimental constraints on iodine cycling in low oxygen waters
description: Publication date: 15 August 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 427 Author(s): Keyi Cheng, Colleen M. Hansel, Ian Carley, Maren Voss, Michaela A. TerAvest, Matthew O. Schrenk, Dalton S. Hardisty
abstract: Iodine is widely applied as a paleoredox proxy for ancient atmospheric and seawater O2 accumulation because marine iodine is redox sensitive and its dissolved speciation is preserved in carbonate rocks. However, while the oxidized iodate (IO3 -) is observed to become depleted relative to the reduced iodide (I-) in modern and ancient low oxygen settings, the mechanisms and relationship with oxygen, if any, remain unclear. To provide constraints on potential O2 controls on the iodine biogeochemical cycle, we collected depth profiles and investigated iodine cycling in 2 sub-basins of the Baltic Sea (Fårö and Gotland Deep) and performed laboratory IO3 - reduction experiments in cultures of the facultative bacterium Shewanella oneidensis at variable O2 levels. Like other stratified euxinic systems, I- increases and IO3 - declines at or below the chemocline. The Baltic Sea, however, has complex patterns between iodine species that are decoupled from O2, likely reflecting the unique hydrological and biogeochemical conditions of this stratified system. Notably, we observe significant IO3 - depletion in the fully oxygenated surface layers of the Baltic Sea, a phenomenon uncommonly reported elsewhere. Our culture experiments provide evidence that S. oneidensis preferentially reduces O2 over IO3 - until O2 levels are < 0.1 µM, which are only relevant in anoxic and suboxic (nitrogenous and manganous) zones of the Baltic Sea. We suggest that instead of in situ reduction in the sampled surface waters, the depleted surface water IO3 - is a legacy effect of previous hypoxia either within surface waters and/or along the flow path sourcing surface waters. Since I- oxidizes relatively slowly, such legacy effects may reflect past shoaling of the oxycline or be at least partially the result of the frequency since the last Major Baltic Inflow (MBI) (in this case 7 years), which intermittently introduce oxygenated, IO3 --rich seawater from the North Sea. Together, our findings have important implications for secular IO3 - and O2 accumulation throughout Earth history. The microbial reduction experiments provide refined constraints on atmospheric O2 accumulation at the Paleoproterozoic Great Oxidation Event (∼4 × 10-4 of the present atmospheric level, or PAL), when IO3 - initially accumulated. Further, comparison to the Baltic Sea provides evidence that O2 and IO3 - may become decoupled in redox-stratified and restricted basins even after atmospheric O2 increases, which may contribute to observations of widespread muted IO3 - accumulation even throughout the Phanerozoic.

title: Rubidium isotopes reveal no sub-arc melting of altered oceanic crusts in a cold subduction zone
description: Publication date: 15 August 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 427 Author(s): Zi-Qiang Zhong, Ding-Sheng Jiang, Saskia Erdmann, Yi-Xiang Chen, Xia Hu, Zheng Xu, Wei Zhang, Jia-Ru Sheng, Wang-Ye Li, Fang Huang
abstract: The extent to which partial melting of subducting slabs contributes to arc magmatism beneath sub-arc regions in cold subduction zones remains highly debated. Traditional models emphasize that altered oceanic crust (AOC) undergoes dehydration, while subducted sediments undergo partial melting. However, an increasing number of studies have argued that partial melting of AOC may also be required to account for the trace-element budgets of arc lavas, particularly their elevated Sr concentrations. To investigate whether AOC undergoes partial melting beneath sub-arc regions, we report Rb isotope (δ87Rb) data for the Cretaceous arc basalts and back-arc basalts associated with the cold subduction zone of the Izanagi plate in Eastern China. The δ87Rb values of the basalts show clear variation across the subduction zone, increasing from −0.31 ± 0.45‰ (2SD, N = 9) for the arc basalts to −0.19 ± 0.07‰ (2SD, N = 22) for the back-arc basalts. This across-arc variation in δ87Rb indicates that while partial melting of subducted sediments occurs across the sub-arc and back-arc regions, partial melting of AOC is only evident in the back-arc region, not beneath the sub-arc region. Moreover, negative correlations between δ87Rb and Sr concentrations strongly suggest that the elevated Sr concentrations (385–913 μg/g) of the arc basalts resulted from the subduction input from sediments, rather than AOC melts as has recently been proposed for global data. Similar compositional relations are observed in arc lavas from other cold subduction zones (Izu-Bonin-Mariana and Tonga-Kermadec), which typically exhibit a negative correlation between Sr/Y and 143Nd/144Nd or Nb/U ratios. Together with recent δ87Rb data from the Mariana arc, our results indicate that in cold subduction zones, AOC may not necessarily undergo partial melting beneath the sub-arc region—even though subducted sediments do. Partial melts of metasomatic pyroxenites formed by interaction between sediment melts and the sub-arc mantle peridotites can carry a significant budget of trace elements, including Sr, contributing to arc magmas. The lack of partial melting in AOC beneath sub-arc regions permits the deep transport of water, carbon, and trace elements, with significant implications for mantle heterogeneity, carbon flux imbalance, and global geochemical cycling.

title: Elevated silicon content facilitates carbon precipitation within Mercury’s core
description: Publication date: 15 August 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 427 Author(s): Juliana G. Peckenpaugh, Meryem Berrada, Peng Jiang, Bin Chen
abstract: Mercury’s highly reduced formation conditions likely promoted the incorporation of silicon into its metallic core during planetary differentiation. The resulting Si-rich core composition would reduce the capacity of the metallic liquids to dissolve carbon, making carbon saturation more likely as the core cooled and crystallized. Determining the solubility of carbon in Fe-Si liquids under Mercury’s core conditions is therefore essential for evaluating whether graphite or diamond could precipitate from the core and influence Mercury’s thermal and magnetic evolution. In this study, high-pressure and high-temperature experiments were conducted on carbon-saturated Fe-Si alloys with varying silicon content from 4 to 27 wt% using a multi-anvil press at 5–20 GPa and 1673–1873 K. The analyses of the recovered samples by Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) and Raman spectroscopy show the Fe-Si-C liquids with precipitated carbon phases in the form of graphite or diamond. Quantitative electron probe microanalysis (EPMA) results demonstrate a trend of decreasing carbon content in the Fe-Si-C alloys with increasing silicon content, described by the following equation: CFe-Si = 8.45–0.663[Si] + 0.0134[Si]2 . Higher initial silicon content within Mercury’s core due to the highly reduced conditions may result in lower solubility of carbon, suggesting a potential mechanism for the preferential exsolution of carbon-rich materials, such as graphite or diamonds. This finding suggests that carbon could precipitate within Mercury’s cooling, solidifying core under Mercurian core compositions and conditions. The segregation and accumulation of carbon could modify heat flux across the core-mantle boundary, affecting both the strength of Mercury’s early magnetic field and the longevity of dynamo action. Such compositional convection could sustain a dynamo, contributing to Mercury’s present-day magnetic field.

title: Inclusion evidence for melt-fluid evolution and rare earth element mineralization in deep intrusive carbonatites
description: Publication date: 15 August 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 427 Author(s): Xueyin Yuan, Qi Li, Xiaochun Li, Yang Yu, John A. Mavrogenes
abstract: Carbonatite-associated Rare Earth Element (REE) deposits have been the primary source of REEs for decades, yet the melt-fluid evolution and REE mineralization processes in these systems remain enigmatic. In this study, we successfully characterize the REE mineralizing liquids from two large carbonatite REE deposits, based on microscopic analyses of primary REE-rich multi-phase inclusions from pegmatitic ore dykes, and acquisition of their homogenization pressure–temperature (P-T) conditions by using a Raman spectrometer and a hydrothermal diamond anvil cell. The inclusions studied here consist mainly of sulfate, carbonate and REE daughter minerals (65 – 75 vol%), along with subordinate aqueous liquid (20 – 30 vol%) and vapor (<5 vol%). Their homogenization P-T conditions reach 470 – 600 °C and 5.0 – 7.0 kbar, with sulfate and carbonate concentrations being estimated to exceed 50 wt% and 20 wt%, respectively. By referring to the thermodynamic properties of aqueous-salt systems involving carbonates and sulfates, we conclude that such liquids are neither magmatic nor hydrothermal in the conventional sense, but rather transitional brine-melts, or supercritical fluids formed by complete miscibility between aqueous fluids and salt melts under high P-T conditions. More importantly, the identification of REE daughter minerals (burbankite) in these inclusions, along with their dissolution at 450 – 520 °C during heating, provides direct evidence that such brine-melts have a remarkable capacity in transporting and concentrating REEs, hence shall be responsible for the primary mineralization of REEs in carbonatite systems.

title: Chondrule formation in the outer disk from the primary three-dimensional chemical composition of CM chondrules
description: Publication date: Available online 2 August 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Poula Eyðbjørnsdóttir, Anders Johansen, Elishevah van Kooten
abstract: Chondrules and their associated fine-grained rims (FGRs) record fundamental processes operating in the early protoplanetary disk, yet the relationship between chondrule chemistry, morphology, and matrix complementarity remains incompletely understood. Here we investigate the major, minor, and trace element compositions of 66 chondrules and associated FGRs from relatively unaltered CM carbonaceous chondrites Asuka 12236, Paris and Maribo in relation to their three-dimensional morphology, using a multi-analytical approach including femtosecond LA-ICP-MS and X-ray tomography. Our results show that CM chondrules record a systematic process of metal loss and evaporation of Si-rich mesostasis, driving initially CI-like precursor compositions toward more Mg- and Si-rich bulk compositions along the CI ratio line and toward increasingly Si-poor forsteritic mineral assemblages. GEMS-like materials in pristine CM matrices appear to mirror chondrule compositions and likely represent complementary condensates derived from evaporated Si-rich mesostasis. The dust accreted to chondrules is dominantly CI-like but incorporates ∼ 14 wt% complementary condensate material represented by chondritic amorphous silicates, reconciling the observed Mg/Si complementarity between chondrules and matrix with the preservation of primordial organics and presolar grains. Morphological observations further reveal no significant sectioning bias in chondrule size or plane, consistent with CM chondrule populations being dominated by agglomerates of ∼ 100 μm sized microspherules rather than larger primary melt droplets. Many chondrules display grape-bunch textures formed by welding of smaller primary chondrules with metal-rich or CI-like rims. This structure may explain the moderate volatile element plateau at ∼ 0.3 × CI observed for average CM chondrule compositions, reflecting incorporation of primary fine-grained rim material into these aggregates. We propose a “micro-chondrule-first” formation scenario in which localized heating events produced small molten droplets that subsequently accreted CI-like dust and ice, aggregated, and experienced limited in situ aqueous alteration. These observations place new constraints on chondrule formation mechanisms in the outer disk and highlight the importance of localized melting and aggregation processes.

title: In situ Raman spectroscopic observation of thiol transformation in hydrothermal fluids: implications for hydrocarbon decomposition and reservoir desulfurization
description: Publication date: Available online 28 July 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Qian Wan, Xiaolin Wang, Wenxuan Hu, Binbin Xi, Xuesong Lu, Ye Wan, Junjia Fan, Zhen Li, I-Ming Chou
abstract: Thiols play important roles in global carbon and sulfur cycling, hydrocarbon alteration and metal mineralization. However, their transformation pathways and thermal stability in hydrothermal systems remain poorly constrained. Here we use an in situ approach combining fused silica capillary capsules with Raman spectroscopy to investigate the fate of thiols during hydrous pyrolysis and thermochemical sulfate reduction (TSR). Our results show that thiols are sequentially transformed into alcohols, aldehydes/ketones, and carboxylic acids, which subsequently decarboxylate or oxidize to form light hydrocarbons and CO2. Complex OSCs—including sulfides, disulfides, sulfones, and thiophenes—are also generated, and their formation can be explained by radical mechanisms. Thiol hydrous pyrolysis proceeds more slowly than anhydrous pyrolysis at high temperatures (e.g., >247.5 °C for 1‑propanethiol) but faster at lower temperatures. Notably, thiols significantly enhance the rate of sulfate reduction, providing direct kinetic evidence that they can promote TSR. Even in the absence of external sulfate, thiol formation and hydrous pyrolysis can still promote hydrocarbon decomposition while transferring H2S from formation fluid into solid bitumen, serving as a critical but previously overlooked reservoir desulfurization mechanism. Because TSR-derived H2S reacting with hydrocarbon is a major pathway for thiol formation, the overall impact of TSR on hydrocarbon decomposition may be substantially underestimated. These results establish a kinetic and mechanistic framework for thiol-mediated C-S cycling in hydrothermal systems, with implications for hydrocarbon decomposition and reservoir desulfurization.

title: Indium diffusion in rhyolitic melts: Implications for In enrichment in magmatic-hydrothermal systems
description: Publication date: Available online 25 July 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Zewei Zhang, Li Zhang, Renzhi Zhu, Wan-Cai Li, Huaiwei Ni
abstract: Indium, a critical metal primarily recovered as a byproduct from granite-related deposits, requires enrichment exceeding 100 times from magmatic sources to form ore deposits due to its exceptionally low crustal abundance. The In diffusivity in silicate melt is one of the most essential parameters controlling In transport and enrichment efficiency, but has yet to be experimentally determined. This study investigated In diffusion in rhyolitic melts with up to 7.0 wt% H2O at 1073–1873 K and 0.5–1.0 GPa in a piston-cylinder apparatus, employing both diffusion couple and In sheet dissolution techniques. Laser ablation ICP-MS analyses of recovered samples yielded concentration profiles, from which In diffusivities were derived via error function fitting. The In diffusivity was found to increase with elevated temperature and water content but to decrease with pressure. At 1 GPa, In diffusivity in granitic melt can be expressed by the following expression: log D In, 1 GPa = - 8.86 ± 0.69 - 6539 ± 1111 - 432 ± 61 w T , where D is the In diffusivity in m2/s, w is the water content in wt%, and T is the temperature in K. The pressure effect over 0.5–1 GPa gives an activation volume of 18.9 cm3/mol for In diffusion. Indium diffusion is sluggish compared to other ore-forming elements, with a diffusivity sequence of D Mo < D In ≈ D Sn ≪ D H2O < D Cu ≈ D Ag. The slow In diffusion in melt hinders the enrichment degree of In in the fluid phase to reach the thermodynamic equilibrium prediction. Given the striking similarity in diffusivities of In and Sn in rhyolitic melts, the enrichment ratio of In to Sn in the fluid falls within a narrow range, regardless of whether equilibrium is reached. This can be used to interpret the coupled enrichment of In and Sn observed in cassiterite-sulfide deposits. Our In diffusivity data are also consistent with the observation in fluid-melt partition experiments.

title: Hematite and siderite nanocrystals in ∼3.48 Ga Dresser Formation jaspilite: Implications for early atmospheric O 2 and CO 2
description: Publication date: Available online 24 July 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Tianyu Zhou, Huifang Xu, Seungyeol Lee, Eric E. Roden
abstract: Decoding the origin of Precambrian iron formations is essential for evaluating how these rocks record the evolution of early Earth’s surface environment. The ∼ 3.48 Ga jaspilite from Unit A3 of the lower Dresser Formation, Pilbara Craton, Western Australia, provides an exceptional insight to address this challenge based on the intimate association of redox-sensitive Fe(III) oxide (hematite) and Fe(II) carbonate (siderite). This study integrates petrographic observations and geochemical (PHREEQC) modeling to investigate the genesis of hematite and siderite embedded in chert. Nanoscale hematite crystals preserved within hematite-quartz clots formed through ferrihydrite dehydration with limited diagenetic overprinting. Their nanoscale morphology and the absence of relict Fe(II)-silicate (greenalite) precursors support an early authigenic origin rather than secondary oxidation. Two distinct siderite populations in the most Fe-rich jasper layers—partially dissolved crystals left within euhedral micron-scale voids and intact nanoscale rhombs sealed within chert—reflect two different recrystallization stages based on their spatial relationship with hematite-quartz clots. We propose that Dresser Unit A3 jaspilite formed during episodic hydrothermal discharges delivering dissolved Fe-Si, represented by Fe(H3SiO4)2 as a working aqueous metal complex supply, accompanied by abundant seawater/hydrothermal silica input, where comparable rates of Fe(II) oxidation and its combination with dissolved inorganic carbon promoted the simultaneous crystallization of ferrihydrite and siderite, followed by silica gel precipitation. PHREEQC geochemical simulations show that the observed coexistence of siderite and ferrihydrite with plausible Fe-Si source requires CO2-rich conditions (pCO2 ≈ 0.1–0.2 atm) and trace but non-negligible oxygen (pO2 ≈ 10−6 atm), indicating a transient redox state capturing the coprecipitation of Fe(II) and Fe(III) phases. Electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ferrihydrite and silica nanoparticles promoted micron-scale colloidal aggregation, later preserved through diagenesis as ∼30 μm hematite–quartz clots. These findings indicate a narrow window of early Archean regional pO2 – pCO2 conditions governing Fe-Si-C-O interplay on Earth’s surface. Our calculated relatively high pO2 level suggests that the Dresser Formation may record one of Earth’s earliest local “whiffs of oxygen” through oxygenic photosynthesis and tectonic oxygen production long before the first major worldwide rise in atmospheric oxygen during the Great Oxidation Event.

title: Particulate manganese shuttling shapes molybdenum and thallium isotope compositions in surface sediments of the Arabian Sea oxygen minimum zone
description: Publication date: Available online 24 July 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Xinming Chen, Niels A.G. M. van Helmond, Bing Xia, Hainan Lu, Zili Zhao, Yu Zhang, Lulu Wang, Yi-Bo Lin, Feifei Zhang, Gert-Jan Reichart, Caroline P. Slomp
abstract: Sedimentary molybdenum (Mo) and thallium (Tl) isotopes have recently been explored as proxies for reconstructing ocean oxygenation by tracking seafloor manganese (Mn) oxide burial. Although Mn oxides impart the largest isotope fractionations for Mo and Tl in modern oceans and can enhance authigenic accumulation of trace metals (e.g., Mo) in sediments via ‘Mn shuttling’, it remains poorly constrained whether such shuttling affects their isotope compositions in sediments. Here, we measured Mo and Tl isotope compositions in sediments within and below the Arabian Sea oxygen minimum zone (OMZ), where Mn shuttling is occurring. Authigenic Mo isotope compositions (δ98Moauth = 1.70 ± 0.13‰) in ferruginous sediments within the OMZ are similar to those in anoxic but non-sulfidic sediments in modern oceans. In contrast, we observed near-crustal Tl isotope compositions (ε205Tlleach = –1.8 ± 0.5‱) in these sediments, which are different from other modern anoxic sediments. This discrepancy likely results from limited sulfide minerals that host authigenic Tl. Both much lower δ98Moauth and higher ε205Tlleach values (–0.50 ± 0.14‰ and + 2.1 ± 1.1‱) in the Mn-oxide-rich sediments below the OMZ are identical to those of oxic sediments, suggesting a predominant control by particulate Mn shuttling. Post-depositional diagenesis of these sediments leads to a return of Mo and Tl concentrations to crustal levels observed downcore, imposing little effect on global mass balances for Mo and Tl isotopes on longer time spans

title: Magmatic-hydrothermal transition and lithium enrichment: Li–B isotope evidence of elbaite for fluid recirculation mechanisms
description: Publication date: Available online 23 July 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Tao Hong, Yin-Ce Ma, Ming-Guo Zhai, Zhang Zhang, Xing-Wang Xu, He Huang, Jun Gao, Gao-Bin Chu
abstract: The magmatic-hydrothermal transition in rare-metal pegmatites is crucial for understanding mineralizing processes, particularly for strategic resources like lithium and beryllium. Tourmaline, a common mineral in pegmatites, serves as an excellent geochemical tracer for this transition. This study examines the Bailongshan Li pegmatite deposit in the western Kunlun Orogen, northwestern China, through detailed textural and geochemical analyses of elbaite (Elb). By integrating data for major and trace elements and Li–B isotope compositions of Elb, the present study delineates the magmatic-hydrothermal transition and its role in ore formation. Elbaite in the Bailongshan Li pegmatite deposit crystallized progressively from Elb-1 (core, magmatic origin, dark green), through Elb-2 (mantle, late magmatic origin, dark green), to Elb-3 (rim, magmatic-hydrothermal transition origin, light green). Li and B isotopes of Elb show different evolutionary trends from Elb-1 to Elb-3: δ11B increases from Elb-1 to Elb-2, whereas no statistically significant variation is observed from Elb-2 to Elb-3.This pattern is interpreted to reflect fractional crystallization (the resolvable core-to-mantle increase) followed by the re-involvement of an early-exsolved, weakly fractionated hydrothermal fluid that imparts no resolvable δ11B change to Elb-3. In contrast, δ7Li remains stable from Elb-1 to Elb-2 but shows a “V”-shaped variation from the late-crystallized range of Elb-2 to Elb-3. This “V”-shaped δ7Li trend likely records a combination of fractional crystallization, melt-fluid separation, and Li diffusion. Boron isotope modeling indicates ≥80% fractional crystallization during Elb-1 and Elb-2 deposition, while Elb-3 formed from exsolved hydrothermal fluids derived from early melt-fluid separation that are re-involved in the crystallization of lithium-bearing minerals (elbaite) during the magmatic-hydrothermal transition with ∼25% fractional crystallization. Elevated δ7Li values (avg. + 14.1 ‰ to + 14.6 ‰) and an increase in mean Li content of ∼1800 ppm between Elb-2 (avg. 5723 ppm) and Elb-3 (avg. 7513 ppm) might reflect Li isotope diffusion driven by concentration gradients. Reintroduced, weakly fractionated exsolved fluids govern Li mineralization (increasing concentrations of Be, Sn, Ta, and Nb) in elbaite during the magmatic-hydrothermal transition at the Bailongshan Li pegmatite deposit. This study identifies that early-exsolved hydrothermal fluids are re-injected into pegmatitic magmas during pegmatite evolution, a phenomenon conducive to rare metal mineralization. Our work enhances understanding of pegmatite evolution and provides a new mechanistic explanation for pegmatite-hosted rare metal mineralization.

title: Stable isotope evidence for light Zn burial in an oxic coastal bay: Implications for the modern marine Zn budget
description: Publication date: Available online 23 July 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Yuchen An, Yi Liu, Sheng He, Wei Yuan, Hongming Cai, Wangcai Shuai, Yunchao Lang, Jun Sun, Jiubin Chen
abstract: Understanding zinc (Zn) cycling in coastal environments is crucial for constraining the global marine Zn budget and evaluating its impact on marine ecosystems. Here, we present the first detailed study of Zn isotope systematics across multiple environmental compartments (including surface sediments, sediment cores, riverine sediments, and aerosols) in the Bohai Bay (BHB), a shallow, semi-enclosed, oxic coastal system in northern China. Our results show that sedimentary Zn is derived from two dominant fluvial sources: Yellow River-derived detrital input representing natural lithogenic material and Haihe River particulates carrying an urban anthropogenic signature. By contrast, coastal industrial activities, atmospheric deposition, mariculture, and antifouling paints make only limited direct contributions to sedimentary Zn in BHB. Instead, up to ∼ 60% of sedimentary Zn is authigenic and exhibits an isotopically light signature (δ66Zn value varying from –0.87 to + 0.26‰). Multiple lines of evidences, including covariations in Fe and Zn enrichment factors, microscale mineralogical data, and contrasting Fe vs. Al distribution, indicate that seawater Zn burial is likely dominated by scavenging to reactive Fe-Mn (oxyhydr)oxides under oxic conditions. This interpretation is further supported by offshore core BHB16, which records the highest authigenic Zn fraction and yields the δ66Zn values (δ66Znauth = 0.07 ± 0.28‰, 2SD, n = 37) overlapping those of deep-sea dispersed Fe-Mn (oxyhydr)oxides reported previously (δ66Zn = –0.02‰ to + 0.34‰). Overall, our findings reveal a significant but previously under-constrained sink for isotopically light Zn in the modern marine Zn cycle.

title: Contrasting Mo isotopic signatures in basalts linked to distinct subduction processes in the North China Craton
description: Publication date: Available online 19 July 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Jian-Fang Guo, Qiang Ma, Liang Ma, Yi-Gang Xu, Jian-Ping Zheng, Chao Zhang, Hao Hu
abstract: Subduction is a fundamental process driving mantle evolution and material recycling, yet distinguishing the contributions of oceanic versus continental subduction to mantle heterogeneity remains a challenge. This study examines Mo isotopes, combined with elemental and Sr-Nd-Pb isotopic data of Early Cretaceous basalts in Sihetun (western Liaoning) and Feixian (western Shandong) in the North China Craton (NCC), regions influenced by distinct subduction processes. Sihetun basalts, exhibit light Mo isotopic compositions (δ 98/95Mo = -0.97 to −0.60‰), low Mo contents (0.32 − 0.41 ppm), high Ce/Mo ratios (292 − 426), and EMI-like Sr-Nd isotopic compositions. These characteristics suggest a mantle source containing dehydrated oceanic crust and pelagic sediments, possibly related to the oceanic subduction of the Paleo-Pacific plate. In contrast, Feixian basalts show heavier Mo isotopic signatures (δ 98/95Mo = -0.09 to 0.07‰), higher Mo contents (1.1 − 1.4 ppm), lower Ce/Mo ratios (137 − 197), and EMII-like Sr-Nd isotopic compositions. These features point to the contribution of recycled continental crust and terrigenous sediments in their mantle sources, suggesting that their sources were affected by both deep subduction of the Yangtze continent and subduction of the Paleo-Pacific plate. These distinct Mo isotopic variations across the NCC reveal that oceanic subduction leads to lighter Mo signatures, while continental subduction introduces heavier Mo isotopic signature to the overlying lithospheric mantle. This study highlights Mo isotopes as a powerful tracer for subduction-related processes and provides new insights into how oceanic and continental subduction regimes drive mantle enrichment and global geochemical cycles

title: The water isotope fractionation coefficient of hydrogen and oxygen in equilibrium with ice and supercooled water at -20°C and the role of supersaturation during ice formation
description: Publication date: Available online 18 July 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): P.P. Ebner, H.C. Steen-Larsen
abstract: Ice-vapor equilibrium fractionation factors are critical for using water stable isotopes to understand hydrological cycle processes and reconstruct past climate variability. However, significant disagreements in the equilibrium fractionation coefficients among previous works exist. Here, we present an experimental study to reconcile past findings by freezing out water vapor under a controlled environment in a glass flask. This was specifically designed to investigate the effect of supersaturation on the transient behavior of the fractionation coefficient at -20.4°C and to evaluate steady-state assumptions. Two phase transitions (1) vapor-supercooled water and (2) vapor-ice have been analyzed. In addition, a physical model is provided to evaluate the effect of supersaturation on the fractionation coefficient in an equilibrium chamber. The observed results showed transient variability during the experiments and a humidity concentration effect on the apparent fractionation coefficient of the vapor introduced into the equilibrium chamber. Based on the experimental data and model evaluation, the equilibrium fractionation coefficients at -20.4°C for vapor over ice are 1.0202 (±0.0013) for 1H1H18O and 1.1943 (±0.0054) for 1H2H16O. For vapor over supercooled water micro droplets at -20.4°C, the equilibrium fractionation coefficients are 1.0182 (±0.0015) for 1H1H18O and 1.1682 (±0.0097) for 1H2H16O. Our findings suggest that the previously estimated fractionation coefficients are influenced by kinetic processes driven by the humidity concentration gradient across the assumed equilibrium chamber. Therefore, previous works were not carried out under true equilibrium conditions.

title: Authigenic ε Nd offsets driven by sediment–pore water exchange: evidence from the Iberian margin
description: Publication date: Available online 18 July 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Sara Campderrós, Leopoldo D. Pena, Jaime Frigola, Luke Skinner, Dimitris Evangelinos, Ester Garcia-Solsona, Eduardo Paredes-Paredes, Albert Català, Isabel Cacho
abstract: Neodymium isotopes (εNd) preserved in authigenic phases are widely used as tracers of water mass provenance and mixing in paleoceanography. However, recent studies have questioned its reliability, as processes occurring at the sediment–seawater interface can introduce a distinct εNd signal into pore waters, potentially altering the signal preserved by authigenic phases. This study investigates whether εNd values recorded in different authigenic phases from the Atlantic Iberian margin reliably reflect the isotopic composition of overlying bottom waters. To this end, we present the first high-resolution core-top εNd dataset from this region, including εNd analysis from foraminiferal Fe-Mn coatings, fish debris, and sediment leachates. These results are compared with εNd values of present-day seawater compositions, detrital sediment fraction, and interface water (water immediately above the seafloor). Our results reveal a consistent offset between seawater εNd and the less negative values recorded in all authigenic phases. Interface waters also exhibit less negative εNd signatures, suggesting that a reactive sedimentary phase that constitutes a minor component of the sediment, with a less negative εNd dissolves into pore water. Consequently, both the isotopic composition recorded by authigenic phases and that of the seawater immediately above the seafloor are also modified to more positive εNd values. Differences between the εNd signal recorded by foraminiferal coatings, fish debris, and sediment leachates further suggest that εNd is incorporated through phase-specific diagenetic and geochemical processes. We also investigate how changing redox conditions in the sediment column affect the εNd signal recorded by foraminifera. Despite early diagenetic remobilization of Fe–Mn coatings evidenced by changes in U/Mn ratios measured in foraminiferal coatings, εNd values remain consistent downcore, suggesting that redox conditions do not substantially modify the εNd ratios. Altogether, our results suggest the presence of a reactive sedimentary phase that modifies pore water εNd. This altered signal is subsequently transferred to the authigenic phases, thereby compromising the reliability of εNd as tracer of past water mass provenance in the studied margin.

title: The evolution, migration, and transformation of dissolved organic matter in black shale regions: environmental destination and implications
description: Publication date: Available online 17 July 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Yinbo Xu, Guangxu Zhu, Pei Xu, Changqiu Zhao, Rongfei Wei, Usman Kaku Dawuda, Qingjun Guo
abstract: The weathering of black shales represents a critical yet poorly constrained pathway of petrogenic organic carbon release into the modern carbon cycle. Despite its potential importance, the molecular-level processes governing the fate of this ancient dissolved organic matter (DOM) remain elusive. In this study, integrated optical, ultra-high-resolution mass spectrometry (FT-ICR-MS), and thermodynamic analyses were employed to track the compositional shifts of shale-derived DOM across a spatially linked rock-soil–water continuum. Results reveal that the mobilized rock DOM exhibits an unexpected dual nature. While the pool is overwhelmingly dominated by formulas in the “lignin-like” stoichiometric space (∼64%, likely representing carboxyl-rich alicyclic molecules or oxidized kerogen fragments rather than vascular plant residues), it simultaneously releases bio-labile, aliphatic-rich signatures. Molecular network analysis unveils an active, bidirectional transformation hub centered around these moderately oxidized intermediate structures, demonstrating that petrogenic carbon is dynamically repackaged rather than entirely refractory. Although DOM oxidation is thermodynamically favorable across all media (ΔGcox ≈ −118 to −124 kJ/mol-C), distinct environmental filters dictate its fate. The relative enrichment of aliphatic/lipid-like formulas in the aquatic system (from 4.7% to 9.7%) is driven by in-situ microbial production and constrained by thermodynamic efficiency. Specifically, lower maximum energy transfer efficiencies (λ ≈ 0.041) in the stream limit the metabolic reward for microbial degradation, promoting the relative persistence of these aliphatic compounds. Conversely, highly oxygenated aromatic signatures (“tannin-like”) decline sharply (from 11.1% to 2.3%) due to preferential mineral sorption and microbial humification within the soil layer. Our findings suggest that the fate of petrogenic carbon undergoes complex molecular recycling—characterized by aliphatic mobilization, aromatic soil filtration, and aquatic biogenic reshaping. This dynamic view resolves the paradox of its apparent persistence and continuous molecular renewal, providing a mechanistic molecular framework for understanding the activation and fate of petrogenic carbon within the modern critical zone.

title: The solubility of Nd(OH) 3 (s) and thermodynamic optimization of Nd hydroxyl species in hydrothermal aqueous solutions from 25 to 300 °C
description: Publication date: Available online 14 July 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Yerko Figueroa Penarrieta, Alexander P. Gysi
abstract: The mobilization of rare earth elements (REE) is controlled in many geological systems by the transport in hydrothermal aqueous fluids. Geochemical models are needed to predict their subsurface behavior and speciation in high temperature and pressure fluids. The REE3+ and REE hydroxyl complexes are known to control the solubility of REE in a wide pH range. However, thermodynamic data for the REE hydroxyl complexes are scarce at hydrothermal conditions. In this study, we measured the solubility of Nd(OH)3(s) between 100 and 250 °C at acidic to mildly acidic pH using batch-type solubility experiments. These data were used in combination with new calorimetric data for the Nd3+ aqua ion and previous potentiometric measurements of Nd hydroxyl species from the literature to optimize the standard partial molal Gibbs energy of formation (Δf G°) and the cumulative formation constants (log β1-3) of Nd hydroxyl complexes using the GEMSFITS code package. The formation constants (Nd3+ + nOH– ⇌ Nd(OH)n 3-n, n = 1 to 3) are fitted together with available literature data as a function of temperature (T) in Kelvin between 25 and 300 °C: log β 1 = -46.38 + 0.06681·T + 9620/T; log β 2 = -50.62 + 0.08554·T + 1074/T; log β 3 = –23.92 + 0.05953·T + 6480/T. These thermodynamic data are implemented in the MINES database and the GEMS code package to model the speciation of Nd as a function of pH and the solubility of monazite in hydrothermal fluids. Differences of up to 2 orders of magnitude are observed between the models generated from the revised thermodynamic data and the calculated predictions based on the Helgeson-Kirkham-Flowers equation of state parameters for REE hydroxyl complexes. The optimized thermodynamic properties improve the modeling of Nd speciation and REE mineral solubility

title: Riverine Li isotopes response to a flood event on the Chinese Loess Plateau
description: Publication date: Available online 4 July 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Jianqi Man, Long-Fei Gou, Zheng Chen, Wenqi Zhang, Jiayuan Ren, Zhiyuan Zhao, Chengfan Yang, Haoqiang Dong, Chenyuan Kang, Jun Xiao, Zhi-Qi Zhao, Zhenhong Li, Zhangdong Jin
abstract: Silicate weathering is essential to supply nutrients from land to ocean and to sustain the long-term habitability of our planet via consumption of atmospheric CO2. Riverine Li isotopes (δ7Liriv) are proposed a promising silicate weathering tracer. However, how silicate weathering and riverine Li isotopes respond to an extreme hydrological event has rarely been investigated. Owing to homogeneous geochemical compositions, loess provides a unique setting to understand how riverine Li isotopes trace silicate weathering under an extreme hydrological event. Here, we collected and analyzed river water samples within the Beiluo River catchment that fully covered by loess in the dry and wet seasons, in order to capture the response of silicate weathering to a flood event that accounting 1/5 annual runoff in 9 days. The results showed that δ7Liriv values have distinct seasonality between the regular dry and wet seasons and the flood event. In the regular dry and wet seasons, δ7Liriv values were controlled by two processes: 1) mixing between groundwater and silicate weathering in the upper stream, and 2) Rayleigh fractionation processes caused by loess weathering in the middle-lower reaches. In contrast, mixing between extruded porewater and groundwater controlled the δ7Liriv values throughout the flood event. Our findings provides new clues into silicate weathering processes and the response of δ7Liriv to extreme hydrological events.

title: Stable Mg-Zn isotope compositions in Mangaia HIMU lavas as tracers for ancient recycled carbonate
description: Publication date: Available online 3 July 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Si-Yi Yang, Yongsheng He, Oliver Nebel, Jon D. Woodhead, Yang Wang (汪洋), Ying Han, Shan Ke
abstract: Intraplate lavas with heavy Zn isotopic compositions commonly exhibit light Mg isotope signatures, a pattern interpreted as evidence for recycling of Mg-rich carbonate. We report high-precision Mg and Zn isotopic data for lavas from Mangaia, an extreme HIMU OIB end-member thought to be derived from a CO2-rich parental melt. The Mangaia samples display whole-rock δ26Mg values ranging from −0.76‰ to −0.17‰, while δ66Zn varies narrowly between +0.19‰ and +0.39‰. After excluding samples affected by post-eruption alteration processes, we constrain the primary δ26Mg of the Mangaia lavas to −0.241 ± 0.018‰ (2SE, N = 15), indistinguishable from compositions of depleted upper mantle and mid-ocean ridge basalts (MORB). In contrast, the primary δ66Zn is +0.35 ± 0.01‰ (2SE, N = 15), significantly higher than MORB, indicating a unique Mg and Zn isotope composition for the Mangaia mantle source. The elevated δ66Zn can be explained by a contribution of subducted altered oceanic crust (AOC), but a major AOC component is ruled out by petrological evidence for a peridotite-dominated source beneath Mangaia. Binary mixing and melting models show that the HIMU peridotite source was metasomatized by ≤ 10% melt derived from AOC containing 5–10% magnesite. The light Mg isotope signature of magnesite is diluted during mixing with the slab-derived silicates and ambient peridotite, whereas its heavy Zn isotope composition is preserved due to the high Zn concentration in magnesite. The ‘decoupled’ Mg-Zn isotope systematics of Mangaia thus reflect an ancient, well-homogenized carbonate-recycling event. In contrast, the light δ26Mg and heavy δ66Zn observed in some other intraplate basalts are consistent with melts generated directly from carbonate-rich portions of young subducting slabs, prior to extensive dilution by peridotitic mantle. This distinction makes combined Mg-Zn isotope investigations of intraplate lavas a useful tool to distinguish between contrasting carbonate recycling regimes, such as low-flux versus high-flux carbonate-rich melt metasomatism in ancient, hot subduction zones versus young, cold ones.

title: Metal and phosphorus accumulation in cryogenic alkaline lakes: Implications for salts in icy planetesimals and phosphate on early Mars
description: Publication date: Available online 29 June 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Shuya Tan, Takuma Kitajima, Keisuke Fukushi, Baasansuren Gankhurel, Shuukhaaz Ganbat, So Fukaya, Davaadorj Davaasuren, Tuvshin Gerelmaa, Masahiro Yoda, Yasuhito Sekine, Yoshio Takahashi
abstract: The geochemical effects of freezing are becoming important in the investigation of closed aqueous environments, such as inland water on Earth and early Mars, and liquid water on planetesimals. Carbonate-bearing alkaline saline lakes in Mongolia are frozen in the cold season, with chemical species being partitioned among surface ice, lake water, and sediments. Freezing of the lakes leads to the accumulation of dissolved carbonate species, thereby decreasing the pH. The lakes are enriched not only in heavy metals, such as As, Mo, and U, but also in phosphorus. However, little is known about how metals and phosphorus are affected by chemical changes during freezing. Moreover, the mechanisms of major chemical changes are poorly understood and reproduced. Here we performed field surveys to investigate the behavior of these elements during lake freezing. Heavy metals and phosphorus accumulate in lake water during freezing, similar to major elements such as Cl−, with Mo and U concentrations reaching ∼1 mg/L. On the other hand, As and P accumulations are limited. Concentrations of heavy metals and phosphorus in ice increase with depth in the ice. We interpret the observed behavior using a geochemical model that accounts for their adsorption reactions coupled with water removal by freezing and carbonate precipitation. The model successfully reproduces the major chemical changes, including the decrease in pH, achieving quantitative accuracy by accounting for the combined effects of freezing and the revised solubility of carbonate minerals. The pH decrease promotes the adsorptions of As and P on sedimentary ferrihydrite particles, suppressing their accumulation in lake water. However, the decrease in pH is insufficient to promote adsorptions of Mo and U, resulting in their accumulations as major dissolved species. Adsorptions of heavy metals and phosphorus by iron oxides may be an important factor in their behaviors at low temperatures near the freezing point of water. Based on our model and observations, we discuss phosphate/carbonate precipitation in freezing porewater of icy planetesimals and phosphate availability in lake water on early Mars.

title: Constraining marine silicate alteration in volcanic material-rich continental margin sediments since the last Glacier Maximum evidenced by stable Si isotopes
description: Publication date: Available online 23 June 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Quanchao Cui, Min Luo, Wei-Li Hong, Tzu-Hao Huang, Weidong Sun, Xiaole Sun
abstract: Marine silicate alteration is tightly linked to carbon burial over geological time scales, especially in continental margins known as ‘hotspot’ due to active organic carbon-driven diagenetic processes. Volcanic materials are one of the most reactive silicate groups, which plays an important role in sedimentary Si processes in continental margins. Since the Last Glacial Maximum, continental margins have undergone strong sediment regime shift, including sediment source changes, due to sea level rise. However, how marine silicate alterations respond to such sediment regime shifts remain largely unexplored. This study uses a 155-meter-long sediment core (IODP Exp. 375 U1518) from the Hikurangi margin, eastern New Zealand, one of the most representative sites in the subduction zone that are enriched with volcanic materials and meanwhile suffers from drastic sea level rise over a hundred of meters in the past 20,000 years. A tailored Si isotope-based sequential chemical leaching protocol in combination with porewater chemistry and geochemical analysis enable us to interrogate the sediment core in great details and uncover sedimentary Si mass balance by constraining various Si endmembers and major Si geochemical processes. Our results show that the δ30Si values of Si endmembers can vary by 1‰ within 1.5–155.7 mbsf due to sediment source changes and early diagenetic modifications. This suggests that conventionally fixed δ30Si value of a single Si endmember through one sediment core may result in large uncertainty in constraining sedimentary Si processes. A potential organic-bounded Si phase with a δ30Si value of −0.19 ± 0.21‰ was also observed in this study. Simulations of a reactive-transport model further reveal enhanced clay mineral dissolution in the shallow Holocene sediments, leading to rapid porewater dissolved Si (DSi) increase and δ30SiDSi value decrease. Compared with the Pleistocene sediments, these changes directly elevate DSi diffusive flux by an order of magnitude with a lower δ30Si value toward seafloor. Meanwhile, slow incongruent volcanic material dissolution in the deep Pleistocene sediments drives the gentle increase of DSi concentrations and δ30SiDSi values, from 541 μmol/L and + 0.24 ± 0.16‰ at 37.10 mbsf to 686 μmol/L and +0.94 ± 0.23‰ at 155.70 mbsf, respectively. High vs. low silicate alteration rates between shallow and deep sediments generates a large DSi concentration gradient and downward diffusion. We propose that it is necessary to include Si phase-based isotope analysis for better constraining marine silicate alterations and its mass balance, particularly for those environments subjecting to sediment source changes. Our findings also highlight that simply attributing decrease of DSi concentration to authigenic clay precipitation (reverse weathering) may cause an overestimation of its role in regulating marine carbon cycle during glacial-interglacial transgressions.

title: Atomic mechanisms of diopside (CaMgSi 2 O 6 ) surface hydroxylation
description: Publication date: Available online 20 June 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Shang Ma, Simon A.T. Redfern
abstract: Understanding how silicate surfaces interact with water is essential for predicting weathering, reactivity, metamorphic reactions as well as interface design. The initial adsorption of water at very low surface coverage governs subsequent hydroxylation, dissolution, and element release. Here, we use density functional theory to compare low-index diopside (CaMgSi2O6) surfaces and their terminations, and then focus on the lowest energy and experimentally relevant (110) facet as a reference for hydration analysis. Upon cleavage and relaxation, the surface develops a pronounced surface–subsurface stratification, with Si and Mg exposed in the outer layer and Ca in the subsurface. Relaxation leads to a local increase in the coordination of undercoordinated Si through short-range interactions with subsurface oxygen atoms, resulting in the formation of protruding SiO4 motifs that act as reactive centres without inducing large-scale structural rearrangement. Early hydration is characterized by configurations in which water-derived hydroxyl and proton species are stabilized at the surface, rather than by intact molecular adsorption. The first water-derived hydroxylation event shows that the hydroxyl group preferentially binds to protruding Si-centred reactive motif, and that the released proton preferred localizes at the neighbouring Image 1001 bridging oxygen. This event restores near-bulk tetrahedral coordination at Si and passivates the protruding site. After this initial dissociation event, the local reactivity is altered: further hydroxylation becomes more favourable at an undercoordinated Mg site, whereas Image 1002 + Image 1003 and Mg-H2O configuration become closer in energy, indicating increased local proton flexibility. These results provide an atomistic picture of the early low-coverage hydration on diopside (110), which is interpreted as a site-resolved mechanistic description of incipient hydration, rather than a full equilibrium thermodynamic description of the aqueous interface.

title: Lithium and calcium isotopes in various shallow-water carbonates: Disentangling the effects of mineralogy, vital effects, and early diagenesis
description: Publication date: Available online 17 June 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Guang-Yi Wei, Simon V. Hohl, Jack G. Murphy, Ashley N. Martin, Yi-Sheng Yin, Zhuang Xiao, Xiaobin Cao, Hong-Fei Ling
abstract: The isotopic composition of metals in marine carbonates provides a powerful archive of past seawater chemistry, yet these primary signals can be modified by diagenetic alteration and vital effects associated with biomineralization in biogenic carbonates. This study investigates the behaviors of calcium (δ 44/40Ca) and lithium (δ7Li) isotopes across a diverse set of shallow-marine carbonate systems, including microbialites from Hamelin Pool in Shark Bay, Western Australia, and bulk carbonate sediments and biogenic corals from the Nansha Islands, South China Sea, to evaluate how depositional conditions, mineralogy, and early diagenesis govern their isotopic compositions. The microbialites exhibit low average values of δ 44/40Ca (–1.22 ± 0.23‰, 2σ, n = 8) and δ7Li (+21.1 ± 3.5‰, 2σ, n = 8), with their offsets from modern seawater values (δ 44/40CaSW = 0‰; δ7LiSW ≈ 31‰) primarily controlled by carbonate mineralogy. A positive correlation between δ 44/40Ca and δ7Li within different individual microbialites is also identified, which is not regulated by vital effects, salinity, or basin restriction, but likely reflects the modest diagenetic alteration of primary metastable aragonites. Compared with microbialites, bulk carbonate sediments show elevated average values of δ 44/40Ca (–1.09 ± 0.22‰, 2σ, n = 23) and δ7Li (+24.0 ± 1.3‰, 2σ, n = 30), indicating mixing of primary aragonite and high-Mg calcite in these sediments. In contrast, the shallow-water corals exhibit higher average δ 44/40Ca values (–1.02 ± 0.14‰, 2σ, n = 4) and lower δ7Li values (+18.0 ± 0.9‰, 2σ, n = 4), which we interpret as the influence of vital effects associated with isotopic fractionations during transmembrane transport of cations between seawater and the calcifying fluid for coral biomineralization. The agreement of δ 44/40Ca and δ7Li data from this study with published shallow-water carbonate records suggests that the isotopic compositions of primary carbonate sediments are predominantly controlled by carbonate mineralogy, while additional processes, particularly vital effects in biogenic carbonates and early diagenetic alteration in carbonate sediments, can further influence these isotopic signatures. This underscores the need to account for carbonate mineralogy, vital effects, and diagenetic alteration when reconstructing coeval seawater signals from ancient carbonates, which can be done using multi-proxy isotope datasets and a modeling framework. Further, when carbonate mineralogy and diagenesis are well constrained, microbialites may be used to reliably reconstruct δ 44/40Ca and δ7Li signatures of Precambrian seawater, as their isotopic signatures are largely insensitive to salinity, basin restriction, and vital effects.

title: Deep mantle reservoirs of recycled surface carbonates revealed by Mg-Sr-Nd-Pb isotopes in continental basalts
description: Publication date: Available online 11 June 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Yan-Qing Li, Chang-Qian Ma, Xiao-Ping Xia, Bin Liu, Ji-Ping Yu, Xiang-Yun Hu
abstract: Deep carbon recycling plays a pivotal role in redistributing carbon among the Earth’s internal reservoirs and modulating global climate over geological timescales. However, the depth at which subducted carbon is stored in the deep mantle, and the dynamics of its recycling remain poorly constrained. Subducted carbonates, typically characterized by lower δ26Mg values relative to the ambient mantle, make magnesium isotopes a powerful tracer for identifying recycled carbonates in mantle-derived rocks. In Eastern China, widespread Cenozoic basaltic volcanism is thought to be driven by hot and/or hydrous upwellings originating from the mantle transition zone (MTZ). Here, we present new Mg isotope data for Cenozoic basalts from Southeast China. Through a comprehensive comparison of Mg-Sr-Nd-Pb isotopic and elemental compositions of basalts from both Northeast and Southeast China, we identify distinct mechanisms of deep carbon recycling beneath the two regions. The low δ26Mg values observed in the Northeast China basalts are attributed to contributions from eclogites metamorphosed predominantly from ancient carbonated sediments stored within the MTZ. In contrast, the recycled carbon signatures in Southeast China basalts were derived mainly from eclogites metamorphosed from dehydrated oceanic crust, with only minor contributions from recycled sediments stored in the MTZ and possibly the deeper mantle. Considering the contrasting tectonic evolutions of Northeast and Southeast China since the Mesozoic, we propose a dynamic link between western Pacific Plate subduction and regionally distinct deep carbon cycling processes. Continuous subduction of the western Pacific Plate has formed a hydrous, carbonate-rich mantle domain beneath Northeast China, where fluid-induced partial melting acts as the key mechanism for carbon recycling. Conversely, dense, dehydrated carbonated eclogite fragments preserved in the deep mantle beneath Southeast China are difficult to ascend on their own, with local thermal upwellings providing the necessary dynamics for magma ascent. Our findings highlight that mantle hydration critically influences the efficiency of deep carbon recycling back to the surface through volcanism, with broader implications for the long-term stability of Earth’s carbon cycle

title: Iron isotope evidence for rapid marine euxinia driven by volcanic Fe-C-S cycles during the end-Permian mass extinction
description: Publication date: Available online 10 June 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Qi Ju, Yi-bo Lin, Hua Zhang, Thomas J. Algeo, Shu-zhong Shen, Feifei Zhang
abstract: The end-Permian mass extinction (EPME) is widely attributed to widespread marine anoxia, likely initiated by large-scale volcanic activity associated with the Siberian Traps Large Igneous Province (STLIP) and coeval eruptions in South China. However, the mechanisms connecting volcanic activity to marine redox dynamics remain debated. Iron, a limiting micronutrient for marine productivity, has an isotopic composition that is sensitive to marine redox conditions. Here, we present high-resolution iron isotope (δ56Fe) data from the Meishan GSSP section in China to reconstruct marine redox dynamics across the EPME. Our results capture a rapid ∼56-kyr transition from oxic to euxinic conditions, marked by a pronounced negative δ56Fe excursion of 0.61‰ and extreme iron enrichment. We indicate that enhanced volcanic and continental weathering increased terrigenous inputs of nutrients and reactive iron, stimulating primary productivity and initiating early-stage ocean anoxia. Under these conditions, reactive iron effectively preserved organic carbon through adsorption and co-precipitation, promoting temporary carbon burial. However, the expansion of the oxygen minimum zone facilitated widespread microbial sulfate reduction, producing hydrogen sulfide that sequestered reactive iron as pyrite. The progressive depletion of oceanic iron pool dismantled the Fe-OC preservation mechanism, triggering extensive organic carbon remineralization and further H2S release. Volcanically derived sulfate aerosols from South China likely enhanced this feedback by fueling additional sulfate reduction. These findings demonstrate that volcanic modulation of coupled iron‑carbon‑sulfur (Fe-C-S) cycles triggered rapid marine euxinia and the EPME. Taking the EPME as an example, our study also demonstrates the robustness of iron isotopes as a redox-sensitive geochemical proxy and highlights their utility in linking process-based insights from modern redox environments to the interpretation of complex redox dynamics preserved in deep-time geological records.

title: Sedimentary Hg isotope signatures overprinted by lateral transport and upwelling-driven Hg recycling in the Benguela upwelling system
description: Publication date: Available online 6 June 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Yaqiu Zhao, Michelle L. Abshire, Stephen J. Romaniello, Jiayu Wu, Ruoyu Sun, Yi Liu, Jiubin Chen, Wang Zheng
abstract: Mercury (Hg) stable isotopes are increasingly used to reconstruct volcanic activity and ocean redox conditions in geological deep time, but the primary sedimentary signals may be modified by water-column and early diagenetic processes, potentially complicating their paleoenvironmental implications. Here we investigate Hg concentrations and isotopic compositions in organic-rich sediments collected along a shelf-to-slope transect across the Namibian continental margin in the Benguela Upwelling System, which spans contrasting depositional settings and redox conditions associated with a persistent oxygen minimum zone. We found that while all sites share the same primary Hg source (atmospheric deposition), they differ markedly in Hg distribution and isotope signatures. The suboxic shelf break site (GC4) has the lowest Hg content, highest Hg/TOC, and lightest δ202Hg, whereas the oxic slope site (GC5) has higher Hg content, lower Hg/TOC, and substantially heavier δ202Hg (by 0.43‰) but similar Δ199Hg (∼0.15–0.16‰). These contrasts are consistent with lateral sediment transport and redeposition, during which oxidative loss of organic matter and Hg repartitioning preferentially retain lighter Hg isotopes at the remobilization site while exporting heavier Hg to the slope, producing substantial mass-dependent fractionation but little mass-independent fractionation. In contrast, the highly productive anoxic shelf site (25020) shows higher Δ199Hg and δ202Hg than the other sites, a pattern likely governed by upwelling-driven Hg recycling, whereby inorganic Hg(II) and methylmercury in anoxic bottom waters and sediments are returned to the surface ocean and photochemically reprocessed, resulting in positive shifts in both Δ199Hg and δ202Hg in the residual Hg pool. Our results demonstrate that sediment reworking and upwelling-driven Hg recycling may substantially alter the sedimentary Hg distribution and isotopic signatures. Thus, the application of Hg and its stable isotopes as paleoenvironmental tracers requires careful consideration of the impact of depositional environment and local redox conditions. More broadly, our findings also highlight the potential of Hg isotopes as a tracer of ancient upwelling systems and the associated ocean anoxia.

title: FTIR constraints on Martian mantle water from clinopyroxene in nakhlite and shergottite meteorites
description: Publication date: Available online 5 June 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Ioana-Bogdana Radu, Cécile Deligny, Henrik Skogby, Roland Stalder, Jeremy J. Bellucci, Martin J. Whitehouse
abstract: Water on Mars has traditionally been estimated from hydrogen contents in melt inclusions and apatite, yet these may not account for magma degassing or post-crystallization dehydration. Pyroxenes offer an alternative approach, as they incorporate trace amounts of water during crystallisation via charge-balancing structural defects, that are retained after dehydration enabling experimentally reversing water loss and constraining magmatic water contents. Here we report the first hydrothermal rehydration experiments on pyroxene from both nakhlites and shergottites. The treated nakhlite augites contain 140‒185 ppm H2O, consistent with previous values for Nakhla (130 ± 26 ppm) and within the range of terrestrial basaltic pyroxene. Using clinopyroxene-melt partition coefficients, this corresponds to 1.59 ± 0.03‒1.83 ± 0.10 wt% average H2O in the nakhlite magma, slightly higher than previous estimates (0.69‒1.42 wt% H2O). The complex hydrothermal history of nakhlites, including evidence for magmatic degassing and interaction with H2O-poor, Cl-rich fluids, suggests these estimates may represent minimum values of the nakhlite magmatic water content. Assuming a low degree of partial melting, the nakhlite mantle source is expected to contain 80‒91 ppm H2O, overlapping previous estimates (59‒184 ppm), and comparable to Earth’s MORB mantle (54‒330 ppm). This is consistent with a common magmatic source for all nakhlites, and broadly consistent with water estimates for the chassignite mantle source (39‒252 ppm), suggesting that any exogenous fluid assimilation had a negligible effect on the net water budget. In contrast, shergottite pigeonites show no detectable water by Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy, consistent with expected water contents of ∼ 2‒11 ppm H2O derived from published source compositions for depleted and enriched shergottites. Together, these results refine our understanding of martian magmatic water content, consistent with a common, more water-rich mantle source for nakhlites, distinct from the more heterogeneous and generally drier shergottite mantle reservoirs.

title: Assessing stable silicon isotopes as proxy for nutrient utilization and carbon cycling in low-productivity marine systems
description: Publication date: Available online 3 June 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Chaoyong Wang, Zhouling Zhang, Zhengjie Hou, Yifan Ma, Junhui Chen, Jin-Yu Terence Yang, Xin Liu, Chuanjun Du, Bangqin Huang, Martin Frank, Minhan Dai, Zhimian Cao
abstract: Silicon (Si) plays a central role in regulating marine primary productivity and mediating interactions between carbon (C) and nitrogen (N) cycling through its control on diatom growth. The stable Si isotopic composition (δ30Si) of biogenic silica (BSi) preserved in sediments has therefore been widely used to reconstruct past nutrient utilization and productivity. However, its applicability in low-productivity ocean regions, where diatoms contribute only modestly to total primary production, remains poorly constrained. Here, we present the first high-resolution, seasonally resolved datasets of coupled Si, C, and N isotope systems from the upper 200 m at two stations in the oligotrophic South China Sea (SCS) basin. Surface waters exhibit relatively heavy δ30Si signatures of dissolved silicic acid (DSi; δ30SiDSi; +2.6‰ to +3.2‰) and of BSi (δ30SiBSi; +1.9‰ to +2.1‰), reflecting near-complete DSi utilization by diatoms. Both Rayleigh-derived fractionation factors (30ℇDSi) based on δ30SiDSi data and apparent fractionation factors (Δ30Si, δ30SiBSi_obs. − δ30SiDSi_obs.) show a strong seasonal variability. 30ℇDSi in the euphotic zone ranging from −1.1‰ to −1.3‰ in summer and −0.6‰ to −0.8‰ in winter, and Δ30Si in the surface mixed layer ranging from −1.0‰ to −1.1‰ in summer and −0.5‰ to −0.8‰ in winter, with no clear spatial variability. Seasonal shifts in diatom productivity influence the distribution and export of biogenic particles. While the overall contribution to bulk primary production remains limited in the picophytoplankton-dominated SCS basin, diatoms can enhance BSi export and particulate organic carbon and nitrogen (POC and PON) production in winter. Coupled analyses of δ30SiBSi and C and N isotopic compositions of POC (δ13CPOC) and PON (δ15NPON) in the euphotic zone reveal a significant positive correlation between δ30SiBSi and δ13CPOC during the winter mixing period, indicating a strong linkage between the Si and C cycles under favorable environmental conditions. In contrast, no correlations are observed between δ30SiBSi and δ15NPON in either season, suggesting that Si and N cycles are largely decoupled due to complex N cycling processes. These findings indicate that δ30SiBSi holds potential as a proxy for tracing primary production in oligotrophic settings and highlight the value of integrating multiple isotope systems to disentangle cycling of different nutrients and improve palaeoceanographic reconstructions in low-productivity ocean regions.

title: Global control of riverine U isotopes by source and weathering processes
description: Publication date: Available online 1 June 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Quentin Charbonnier, Julien Bouchez, Jérôme Gaillardet, Robert G. Hilton, Edward T. Tipper, Derek Vance
abstract: The use of marine sedimentary uranium isotopes (δ238U) to investigate past variability in the redox state of the ocean–atmosphere system rests on a robust quantification of the riverine U isotope flux, the dominant U input to the ocean. However, there is no consensus on the relative importance of lithology versus fractionation during weathering in controlling the riverine U isotope flux to the ocean. Here we report the riverine dissolved and solid uranium isotope composition from fourteen of the world’s largest rivers, integrating lithologies and processes relevant at the global scale, which we compare with data from the literature. The riverine dissolved δ238U ranges from −0.47 to 0.08‰, while the solids range from −0.65 to −0.24‰. Collectively, our results indicate a dominant control by weathering processes on the global riverine U isotope flux, with the notable exception of the Mackenzie Basin. No relationship emerges between riverine dissolved U isotope and lithological tracers. Whilst river solid U isotope variability reflects different relative contributions from erosion of silicate versus organic-rich sedimentary rocks, most large rivers lie close to the silicate erosion end member, and mass balance calculations indicate that silicate rock weathering can explain the total riverine U isotope flux. In this view, elemental and isotope partitioning of U between the riverine dissolved and solid loads suggests a dominant control by weathering processes that fractionate U isotopes. This interpretation is supported by the relationship between the fraction of U remaining in solution following secondary mineral formation during weathering and riverine U isotope signatures. Finally, a complex pattern emerges between climate and U isotope fractionation and weathering intensity. However, based on data collected so far, the U isotope system appears analogous to lithium isotopes, whereby moderate weathering intensity leads to the largest shift in river dissolved load δ238U values under optimal conditions for U incorporation into secondary minerals.

title: Tin isotope fractionation during tropical basalt weathering: Ti mineral control and light Sn retention
description: Publication date: Available online 1 June 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Ting Gao, Zihan Xia, Chuanwei Zhu, Chengshuai Liu, Wenrui Song, Qi Liu
abstract: Continental chemical weathering plays a critical role in redistributing tin (Sn) partitioning among rocks, soils, and waters, yet Sn isotopic behavior during soil development remains poorly constrained. Here, we investigate Sn isotope fractionation within a ∼6 m-thick intensely weathered basalt profile from tropical Hainan Island, China, to assess its implications for Sn mobilization and the global Sn cycle. Integrated mineralogical, elemental, and Sn isotope data show that, although Sn concentrations increase residually with progressive weathering intensity, strongly negative mass transfer coefficients (τSn: average ∼ − 35.2%) indicate substantial Sn loss during chemical weathering. The δ 122/118Sn values of the weathering products range from 0.07‰ to 0.25‰ (average ∼0.17‰, n = 28), systematically lower than those of the parent rocks (0.26‰, n = 2), demonstrating the preferential release of heavy Sn into aqueous phases and the sequestration of light Sn in residual solids. An open-system Rayleigh fractionation model for δ 122/118Sn yields fractionation factors (α) of 1.00021 to 1.00307, corresponding to positive Sn isotopic offsets (Δ122/118Sn up to ∼3‰) between dissolved and solid phases. Mass-balance calculations further suggest that the dissolved phase exported from the profile is isotopically heavy, with δ 122/118Sndissolved varying from 0.40‰ to 3.18‰ (average ∼1.75‰, n = 21). Strong correlations between Sn isotope compositions and Ti contents indicate that the isomorphous substitution is the primary control on Sn isotope fractionation, overprinting initial kinetic dissolution effects. The δ 122/118Sn values become systematically lighter toward the surface, and their covariation with CIA and TiO2/Al2O3 ratios further indicates that Sn isotope fractionation increases with elevating weathering intensities. Overall, our results provide a process-based framework showing that continental weathering drives weathering products to be isotopically lighter than coexisting aqueous systems, thereby highlighting the potential of the Sn isotope system as a proxy for chemical weathering intensity and secondary mineral formation.

title: Synergistic interfacial and multi-omics regulation of La 3+ /Gd 3+ biomineralization by Micromonospora auratinigra
description: Publication date: Available online 14 February 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Lili Wang, Chenyu Yin, Xinyu Chen, Chengliang Cao, Xiuming Liu, Wenping He, Rongpeng Li, Jihong Jiang, Jinjuan Liu
abstract: Microorganisms play pivotal roles in the formation of weathering crust-type rare earth elements (REEs) deposits, yet the mechanisms underlying microbial-mediated REEs immobilization and secondary mineral formation remain insufficiently understood. This study systematically explores the synergistic biosorption and biomineralization mechanisms of La3+ and Gd3+ by the highly tolerant actinobacterium Micromonospora auratinigra. Under optimized conditions (biomass 1.5 g/L, pH 5, La/Gd ratio 2:1), the strain exhibited a preferential affinity for Gd3+ (135.9 mg/g) over La3+ (110.1 mg/g), with further enhanced uptake in mixed systems (143.1 mg/g). Kinetic and isotherm modeling indicated monolayer chemisorption behavior following pseudo-second-order kinetics and Langmuir adsorption patterns. Functional group masking experiments, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) analyses revealed that carboxyl, phosphate, and amino groups on the cell surface were key contributors to REEs binding, with carboxyl groups playing the dominant role. Electron microscopy confirmed the formation of LaPO4 and GdPO4 nanocrystals on the bacterial surface, while HRTEM and SAED analyses revealed the formation of distinct monazite-type mineral phases. Multi-omics analysis demonstrated that the biosorption and mineralization processes were regulated by peptidoglycan functional groups, heavy metal resistance genes, oxidative stress response systems, and phosphate metabolism pathways. Notably, upregulation of phosphate transport and regulatory genes (pstSCAB, phoR/phoU) promoted phosphate acquisition and REEs-phosphate precipitation, while downregulation of organic acid biosynthesis genes prevented mineral dissolution. This work elucidates the molecular and interfacial mechanisms by which M. auratinigra immobilizes REEs, offering new insights into microbial mediation of REEs geochemical cycling. These findings provide a theoretical basis for the development of environmentally friendly technologies for REEs recovery and sustainable resource utilization.

title: Impact-induced submicroscopic metallic iron particles identified in “dusty olivine” from brecciated lunar meteorite Bechar 012
description: Publication date: Available online 27 January 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Yutong Ma, Zhuang Guo, Aicheng Zhang, Jingjing Niu, Shan Qin
abstract: Nanophase iron particles are ubiquitous in lunar soils and are largely attributed to space weathering; however, no nanophase iron particles formed in lunar crystalline minerals via impact events have been reported. Their growth, migration, spatial distribution, and interactions with host minerals under impact remain poorly understood. Here, we report the discovery of impact-induced dusty olivine clasts (containing nanoscale to submicron iron metal particles) in the lunar breccia meteorite Bechar 012. These clasts encapsulate a comprehensive record of iron particle formation and distribution within their crystalline host. Their well-preserved state provides a clear snapshot of the microscopic mineral processes often obscured in more heavily processed soils or breccias, making Bechar 012 an ideal natural sample for study. Crystallographic orientation analysis suggests that these dusty olivine grains undergo plastic deformation, with iron metal particles concentrated within the deformed regions, indicating a correlation between deformation microstructures and iron metal particle formation. We propose a three-step model for the formation of dusty olivine and the iron metal particles therein: (1) impact-induced plastic deformation of olivine; (2) sub-solidus olivine decomposition (Fe2SiO4 = 2Fe + SiO + 3/2O2) within partially amorphous zones, leading to the nucleation of nanosized iron metal particles, with SiO and O2 diffusing away through disordered pathways (e.g., partially amorphous zones, dislocations and pores) in the deformed olivine; and (3) capture of particles by migrating dislocations, followed by aggregation and oriented attachment (OA)-driven growth along the olivine lattice at dislocations and subgrain boundaries, resulting in the formation of submicron-sized iron metal particles. These processes indicate an equilibrium shock pressure below 16 GPa, with temperatures between 1000 °C and 1650 °C. These results confirm the pivotal role of impact-induced olivine deformation in facilitating the formation, migration, and growth of iron metal particles and highlight the significance of OA in their coarsening. The discovery of impact-induced iron metal particles in the lunar meteorite indicates that these particles can be broadly formed within crystalline minerals, rather than being limited to the amorphous rims of lunar regolith minerals and glassy impactites, while also offering a potential explanation for the lunar magnetic anomalies.

title: Unraveling the structure–performance relationship of Co–Co/Co–N dual active sites in ZIF-8 derived nitrogen–doped carbon catalysts for efficient N 2 O decomposition
description: Publication date: 1 September 2026 Source: Journal of Hazardous Materials, Volume 515 Author(s): Ke Zheng, Ruirui Wang, Longqing Wang, Ruifang Wu, Xiangqian Lin, Xiaoting Du, Liangliang Zhang, Chengming Zhang, Yongzhao Wang
abstract: Catalytic decomposition is widely recognized as a promising approach for N2O abatement, yet the rational design of highly active catalysts still remains a huge challenge. In this study, a small Co nanocluster catalyst anchored on a nitrogen–doped carbon framework (Cox/NC) was constructed via a host–guest encapsulation strategy using ZIF-8 as precursor. The Co0.09/NC catalyst with Co/2-methylimidazole molar ratio of 0.09 exhibited the best catalytic activity, achieving a T90 of 294 °C and outperforming most reported catalysts. This outstanding catalytic performance was attributed to the synergistic interplay between Co–Co and Co–N coordination. Specifically, the highly dispersed small Co nanoclusters provided abundant Co2 + active sites for efficient N2O adsorption and activation, while the peripheral Co–N coordination optimized the d-band center of Co and enhanced electron back-donation.
